item.title: Policy and Public Affairs Manager
item.description: About Woman's Trust The charity was established in 1996 to meet the gap in specialist mental health services. Woman’s Trust is led by and for women and aims to ensure that women affected by domestic abuse can live a life free from further harm and abuse. Our approach is trauma-informed and person-centred, empowering survivors on their journey to recovery from the trauma. We are committed to a positive, inclusive and equitable environment for our staff, service users and volunteers. Alongside delivering our existing 1-1 counselling, self-development workshops and therapeutic support groups for women who have experienced domestic abuse, we are focused on developing our innovative mental health services for young women and girls, delivering new peer-led support groups and providing therapeutic groups to children and their mothers. We are also committed to developing further awareness-raising workshops and training for professionals, building on our research and policy to improve systems nationally. About the role The Policy and Public Affairs Manager will establish and lead Woman’s Trust’s policy and public affairs function. She will grow the organisation’s influence with UK and London government, Parliament, NHS systems, commissioners and sector partners so that the voices and experiences of women and children affected by domestic abuse shape policy, commissioning and practice. The postholder will develop and deliver an evidence-led influencing strategy; own a focused portfolio of policy priorities; build and manage senior stakeholder relationships; produce high-quality analysis, briefings and consultation responses; and provide timely political and public affairs advice to the CEO, Chair, trustees and senior colleagues. Working across services, data, communications and fundraising, she will ensure Woman’s Trust’s external positions are grounded in frontline expertise, robust evidence and appropriately supported survivor involvement. She will identify opportunities for the organisation to influence debate and policy at the intersection of domestic abuse, women’s mental health, health inequalities and public services. Hours : 35 hours per week. A four-day/0.8 FTE arrangement will be considered. In return, we can offer: 25 days' holiday + 3 days at Christmas + Public holidays (pro rata for part-time working) Hybrid & flexible working - office based with minimum of 50% of working hours in Woman’s Trust London office, we also support mutually agreed flexible working arrangements Cycle to work scheme Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Mandatory job-related training Individual staff professional development budget A caring, committed and highly collaborative environment Several social events/lunches per year Friendly, all women team To find out more and apply with your CV, please visit our website via the apply button. Please note, CVs and cover letters should be sent in Word format. Closing date: Monday, 7th September 2026. First stage interviews: Friday, 11th September 2026. Second stage interviews: Wednesday, 16th September 2026. Please note, this post is open to female applicants only – Equality Act 2010, Schedule 9, Part 1 applies.

item.title: Operations Manager
item.description: Tinnitus UK is looking for an experienced, ambitious and highly organised Operations Manager to join our senior team and play a key role in the leadership and future development of the charity. You will work closely with our CEO, Board of Trustees and colleagues across the organisation to help turn our ambitions into action and ensure Tinnitus UK has the strong foundations, systems and ways of working it needs to succeed and to best support people living with tinnitus, and those who support them. You will be an important link between the staff team and Board, bringing insight, challenge and practical solutions to organisational decision-making. You will lead and develop a small team, build strong relationships with external partners and suppliers, and take ownership of a broad portfolio spanning finance, governance, people, systems, risk, compliance and organisational improvement. We are looking for someone who enjoys making organisations work better: someone who can see the bigger picture while also making sure the detail is right. You will be comfortable moving between strategic conversations with the CEO and Trustees and the practical work required to make things happen. You do not need to be an expert in tinnitus. What matters is that you share our values, are motivated by our purpose and want to use your operational leadership to help Tinnitus UK achieve more for people affected by tinnitus. About the role As Operations Manager, you will provide leadership across Tinnitus UK’s internal operations, ensuring we have robust systems, financial oversight, governance, people processes and infrastructure in place to deliver our strategy. Working closely with the CEO, you will translate organisational priorities into effective plans and ways of working. You will help create clarity across the organisation, identify risks and opportunities, make sure decisions are followed through and drive continuous improvement. You will also play an important role in ensuring that Tinnitus UK is ready for the future: improving organisational resilience, strengthening our infrastructure and helping us develop the capacity to grow our reach and impact. About you We are looking for an experienced operations professional who enjoys making organisations work better and wants to take significant responsibility within a national charity. You will be proactive, solutions-focused and comfortable bringing structure to complexity. You can see the bigger picture while making sure the detail is right, manage competing priorities and take ownership of work through to delivery. You will be confident working with colleagues at all levels, from supporting and developing your team to discussing finance, governance and organisational priorities with the CEO and Trustees. You will build trusted relationships with external partners and suppliers and be comfortable offering constructive challenge when needed. You will bring experience across a number of areas including organisational operations, financial management, project and change management, governance and risk, people management, suppliers and contracts, and organisational systems or CRM platforms. Experience within the charity sector, membership organisations, digital transformation, events or professional education would be valuable, as would experience working closely with a CEO, senior leadership team or Board. Most importantly, you will be collaborative, pragmatic and dependable, with the confidence to take ownership, maintain high standards and help create an organisation in which people can do their best work. What we can offer This is an opportunity to take on a genuinely influential role within Tinnitus UK at an important point in our development. You will have the scope to shape how the charity operates, introduce improvements and work closely with our CEO and Board to strengthen the organisation for the future. The role offers considerable variety. One day you might be discussing organisational risk and financial performance with Trustees; the next you could be improving a system, negotiating with a supplier, supporting a member of your team or developing the operational plan for a major national event. You will join an organisation committed to improving the lives of people affected by tinnitus and a team that wants to continually improve the way we work and the impact we achieve. Tinnitus UK is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcomes applications from people with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. If you are an experienced operations professional looking for a senior role where you can influence, improve and help lead an organisation with a clear social purpose, we would love to hear from you. How to apply Please apply with your CV and a cover letter outlining how you meet the person specification, including the experience and skills you would bring to Tinnitus UK. The deadline for applications is 5pm on Monday 14 September 2026. Interviews will take place in person on Wednesday 23 September 2026 at our Sheffield office.

item.title: Volunteer Programme Manager
item.description: Volunteer Programme Manager Part-time, 3 days per week Up to £40,000 (pro rata £24,000) + excellent benefits Leatherhead, Surrey About the role: We are looking to appoint a Volunteer Programme Manager on a part-time basis to lead Rainbow Trust’s Volunteer Programme, playing a pivotal role in raising the profile of Rainbow Trust and acting as an ambassador for the organisation. Reporting to the Director of HR & Volunteering, the Volunteer Programme Manager will be responsible for developing and delivering Rainbow Trust’s volunteer strategy in line with wider organisational objectives, taking the lead on strategic volunteer projects and embedding volunteering across our services. Working closely with all our internal departments and external volunteer networks, and line managing the Volunteer Coordinator, the post holder will lead volunteer engagement activities, manage the volunteering budget and policy, and support volunteer recruitment, training, support, engagement and retention. What we’re looking for: A clear and creative communication style – you have strong interpersonal skills, develop effective working relationships with a wide range of people, and inspire motivated team working Poised, enthusiastic and outgoing – you have a collaborative approach to achieving goals through knowledge-sharing and effective delegation. You are excellent at building rapport and engaging the commitment of others. A multi-tasker with a sense of urgency for goal achievement – you delegate effectively with thorough follow-up and are quick to learn and adapt. An innovative, practical and creative problem-solver – you are a big picture thinker that responds quickly to varied activities and changing conditions Professional experience of working in a volunteer management capacity – with experience of developing policy and implementing strategic projects. What we offer: We’re proud to be a Two-Star Best Companies Top 50 mid-sized organisation and a Top 10 Charity, and we’re committed to being a great place to work. You will benefit from: 25 days of annual leave plus public holidays – rising to 26 days after 1 year, 27 days after 5 years and 30 days after 11 years, with an additional 5 days to use in your 10th or 20th year of service (pro rata for part time). A pension scheme where we contribute 5% of your salary and you contribute at least 3%. A life assurance scheme for all employees which provides a death in service benefit of three times’ basic pay. Flexible core working hours to balance home and working life. The option to buy/sell annual leave, as well as additional leave for your birthday, wedding/civil ceremony and an extra half day off for Christmas shopping. Time off in lieu. Employee Assistance Programme with access to remote GP, counselling, physiotherapy, resources to support your mental health and financial wellbeing, as well as a 24/7 helpline via Help@Hand. Family friendly policies, focused on employee wellbeing, and an active cross-organisational wellbeing group running a number of initiatives throughout the year. Access to the Blue Light Card Scheme, and other rewards and discounts. Bike to work, season ticket loan and payroll giving schemes. A recommend a friend recruitment bonus scheme. Robust training and development programmes to support your learning and growth If you’d like to find out more about these benefits and working with us, please visit our website. About us: Rainbow Trust Children’s Charity enables families who have a child with a life-threatening or terminal illness to make the most of time together, providing expert, practical and emotional support, where they need it for as long as it is needed. For families living with childhood illness, time is everything. Right now, there are too many families coping alone with no support, no time to think, no time to make memories and no time for each other. We believe that no family should go through this alone, so we are here to change that. Apply now: To apply please send your CV and a Covering letter highlighting why your application should be considered above others and clearly stating how you meet the essential criteria of the role, to us via the link. For a full job description and person specification visit our website Please disclose in your covering letter if you have used AI for any part of your job application. Interviews will take place at our Head Office in Leatherhead. We will only contact those applicants who have been successful. If you require any adjustments during the interview process, please let us know. An enhanced DBS disclosure will be required for this post. Rainbow Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all employees to share this commitment. Rainbow Trust is an equal opportunities employer, and we welcome applications from all backgrounds.

item.title: Fundraising Lead
item.description: Job overview The Fundraising Lead will act as a specialist professional, leading on the development and delivery of the Head to Toe's engagement and communications activity that supports the charity’s strategic objectives, reputation and profile. Working within Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust (CPFT), the role will provide expert advice and delivery across campaigns, partnerships and stakeholder engagement, ensuring the charity’s messaging is consistent, impactful and aligned with CPFT and Head to Toe branding and values. You will support the development and delivery of a varied and ambitious fundraising programme. This is a hands-on role, ideal for someone with experience in fundraising, charity events, or income generation who is looking to take the next step in their career. You will be responsible for delivering a programme of income generation and engagement events, helping to grow support and raise awareness of Head to Toe, and the support that we provide CPFT NHS services across the region. This includes building partnerships and creating meaningful opportunities for people and organisations to get involved. You will be involved in a wide range of activities – from writing funding bids and supporting major campaigns, to delivering events and building relationships with supporters, clinicians, and partners. No two days will be the same. Main duties of the job Fundraising, events & income generation Campaigns, projects and Trust fundraising Stakeholder engagement Additional Information This role does not involve delivering patient care, but you will have contact with patients and service users. You will be expected to communicate with empathy, professionalism, and respect always. Supporting Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust is a health and social care organisation dedicated to providing high quality care with compassion to improve the health and wellbeing of the people we care for, as well as supporting and empowering them to lead fulfilling lives. Our clinical teams deliver a wide range of NHS services across inpatient, primary care and community settings, including children’s, adult and older people’s mental health, forensic and specialist mental health, learning disabilities, primary care and liaison psychiatry, substance misuse, social care, and research and development. To achieve our goals, we recruit high calibre candidates who share our vision and values. As an equal opportunities’ employer, we welcome applications from all sections of the community, particularly under represented groups including people with long term conditions and members of our ethnic minority and LGBTQ+ communities.

item.title: Challenge Events Officer – Fixed Term (9 months)
item.description: About the Role As a Challenge Events Officer you will support the delivery and growth of MDUK's challenge events and community fundraising programme, helping to achieve fundraising targets through high-quality event management and exceptional supporter engagement. The role involves coordinating challenge events, driving participant recruitment and income generation, and delivering inspiring stewardship journeys that enhance the supporter experience, build long-term relationships, and encourage ongoing involvement with the charity. Main tasks and responsibilities : Support the planning and delivery of challenge events, including participant recruitment, event logistics coordination, and supporter stewardship to maximise fundraising income. Manage participant recruitment, volunteer coordination, event logistics, and supporter communications to ensure successful event delivery and achievement of income targets. Coordinate recruitment, onboarding, and stewardship activities to deliver an outstanding supporter experience and strong fundraising outcomes. Assess event applications, identify high-potential fundraisers, and provide tailored support to help participants achieve and exceed their fundraising goals. Assist with participant stewardship, supporter communications, and fundraising activities to support the successful delivery of large-scale challenge events. Work collaboratively to increase participation opportunities and improve accessibility across the challenge events portfolio. Contribute to the development and improvement of supporter journeys, increasing engagement, retention, and fundraising performance through effective stewardship and automation. Act as a first point of contact for fundraising enquiries, providing guidance, support, and signposting to relevant colleagues when required. Other responsibilities: Ensure all personal data is handled securely, ethically, and in line with the Data Protection Act. To represent the charity externally if required and to undertake other such tasks as required by the line manager. Working arrangements Fixed Term Contract - 9 months Full time: Monday to Friday, 35hours/week Hybrid working arrangement All necessary equipment provided About Us Muscular Dystrophy UK is a charity that connects a community of more than 110,000 people living with one of over 60 muscle wasting conditions, and all the people around them. So, everyone can get the healthcare, support and treatments needed to feel good, mentally and physically. This is an exciting time to join the charity. We recently launched our new 10 year strategy to transform the lives of people living with muscle wasting conditions. Our vision is clear, a world without limits for people with muscle wasting conditions, and we won’t stop until we achieve it. We believe that by creating opportunities for all, we strengthen our impact and better support the communities we are committed to serve. What we offer At Muscular Dystrophy UK, you'll have the opportunity to do meaningful work that makes a real difference to the lives of people living with muscle wasting conditions. We are committed to creating an inclusive, supportive workplace where colleagues can thrive and enjoy a healthy work-life balance. In return, we offer a competitive benefits package, including: 25 days' holiday (pro rata) - increasing by one day each year after five years' service, up to 30 days, plus bank holidays. Time off in lieu - reward colleagues who volunteer their time to support community Employer contribution of 5% with a minimum employee contribution of 3%. Life Assurance - up to 4x your annual salary Health and wellbeing HSF Health Plan, including cashback on healthcare costs for you and your family. Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) offering free, confidential advice and support. Health and wellbeing resources, including Healthy Living support. Access to osteopathic treatment through the UCO Clinic Community Partnership. Discounted gym memberships. Lifestyle benefits Employee discounts at a wide range of high street and online retailers. Interest-free season ticket loans. Cycle to Work scheme. Discounts on cinema tickets, live events and much more. How to Apply Please complete our application and include: Your CV and Cover Letter (PDF or Word format). Responses to the application questions Important information This role is open to candidates based in the UK who have the right to work in the UK. Applications that do not include all the requested information may not be considered. Next Steps Application deadline: Sunday 13 September 2026, 11:59pm Note: We reserve the right to close this vacancy early and bring forward interviews if we identify an exceptional candidate before the advertised closing date. Interviews: Week commencing 21 September 2026. Expected start date: October 2026. We actively encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, particularly those from underrepresented groups, including people from ethnic minority backgrounds, LGBTQ+ individuals, previous convictions and those with lived experience of the conditions we represent. We are committed to fair and inclusive recruitment, with disclosure only requested where relevant at the appropriate stage If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know. We will work with you to understand your needs and make the recruitment process as accessible as possible. Please download the job description to see full role responsibilities

item.title: Recovery Community & Therapeutic Service Manager
item.description: Spitalfields Crypt Trust (SCT) is an East London charity supporting people affected by homelessness and addiction to rebuild their lives. We are looking for an experienced and inspiring Recovery Community & Therapeutic Service Manager to lead the development, delivery and continuous improvement of our Recovery Community and Therapeutic Service. This is a part-time role working 28 hours per week and is fully onsite at our Shoreditch hub. There is some flexibility around how the hours are worked across the week, although ideally Friday will be included as a working day. This is a key leadership role bringing together therapeutic support, aftercare, peer-led activity, volunteering, training and community engagement to create an integrated recovery journey. You will ensure that people accessing SCT's services have opportunities to strengthen their recovery capital, build supportive networks and progress towards greater independence and wellbeing. Working closely with our Director of Services and colleagues across SCT, you will: Lead the ongoing development of SCT's Recovery Community and therapeutic offer. Oversee recovery-focused programmes, therapeutic interventions, aftercare and peer-led activities. Create meaningful opportunities for people with lived experience to shape services, volunteer, mentor and support others. Lead and develop staff, volunteers, peer mentors and facilitators, fostering a positive and inclusive culture. Build strong partnerships with commissioners, funders, treatment providers, housing and mental health services and other community organisations. Oversee service quality, budgets, monitoring and evaluation, ensuring services are safe, effective and demonstrate positive outcomes. Develop pathways into volunteering, employment, education and wider community engagement. About you We are looking for someone with significant experience of leading services within recovery, social care, community development, housing, health or a related field. You will have a strong understanding of addiction recovery and the challenges experienced by people affected by homelessness and multiple disadvantage. You will be a confident and collaborative leader with experience of managing people, developing programmes, building partnerships and delivering measurable outcomes. You'll also bring strong organisational and communication skills, sound judgement and a genuine commitment to person-centred, trauma-informed and recovery-focused practice. Above all, we're looking for someone who can inspire others, develop strong services and help create an environment in which people in recovery are active participants in their own community. Location: SCT's Shoreditch hub, London E1 Hours: 28 hours per week, onsite, ideally including Friday as a working day Please see the attached Job Description for full details of the role, responsibilities and criteria.

Interview dates: 8th (afternoon), 12th, 13th October 2026 What you will be doing: We are seeking a conscientious and organised individual to lead the management of reserves across Shropshire, ensuring they are in good ecological condition and developed as safe, inspiring places for public access, education, research and demonstration. You will also support the Head of Reserves in managing and developing the Reserves team, with a particular focus on trainees, placements and apprentices. You will oversee the safe and effective management of reserves through regular inspections, risk assessments and reactive works relating to trees, infrastructure and visitor safety. You will engage, support and enable branch groups (member groups) and volunteers working on allocated reserves, ensuring they follow Trust processes while building and maintaining positive relationships with neighbours, partners, members, volunteers and contractors. You will manage resources effectively, securing and overseeing funding and schemes and ensuring these are delivered, monitored and reported against. You will support and guide colleagues to make the best use of their time and resources, helping to ensure that reserves are well managed, well known, accessible and welcoming to the widest and most diverse possible audience. What we’re looking for: We are looking for someone with a genuine passion for wildlife and nature, combined with practical experience in habitat and estate management. You will have experience carrying out inspections, planning and directing work, as well as managing wildlife projects, including budget management. You will be a personable, well-organised individual who enjoys working with a wide range of people. You will have experience supporting and directing colleagues through mentoring or coaching, managing and motivating volunteer groups, and supervising contractors. You will also be confident working independently, using your initiative and managing your workload with minimal supervision. Good IT skills are essential, including experience using Microsoft Word, Outlook, Excel and ArcView GIS. You’ll also need to hold a full UK driving licence. The Trust is committed to building an equal, diverse and inclusive workforce we encourage applications from a diverse range of suitably qualified candidates. Please let us know if you require any adjustments to make our recruitment process more accessible. Why work for us - benefits we offer: 25 days holiday plus Bank Holidays and Service related holiday (pro-rated for part time staff) Salary sacrifice benefits Life assurance Generous pension - company contribution 7%, employee contribution 3% Enhanced Sick Pay Flexible working policy Employee Assistance Programme Staff discounts Employee away days Enhanced pay for maternity and adoption leave Coaching Support with training and development to assist career progression Inclusive & supportive work atmosphere About us: Shropshire Wildlife Trust (SWT) has a vision of a thriving natural world, where Shropshire's wildlife and natural habitats play a valued role in addressing the climate and ecological emergencies, and people are inspired and empowered to take action for nature. We combine projects across Shropshire (including Telford & Wrekin) with advocacy and campaigning to restore nature and to engage people. We manage over 40 nature reserves and have almost 50 staff, 300 volunteers, and over 9000 members. SWT is an autonomous charity, but we are increasingly working collectively, as part of The Wildlife Trusts (TWT), to ensure that our local actions have a national impact and help to address global issues.

item.title: Fundraising Manager
item.description: We are seeking a confident, experienced and motivated Fundraising Manager to join our team! Our Organisation SLRA is a frontline community organisation established in 1991 which supports refugees, asylum seekers and migrants in crisis in South London. We provide specialist legal advice and holistic casework to enable people to regularise their immigration status, access rights and entitlements and move on from destitution. Every year we provide support directly to over 1000 migrants in the London Boroughs of Lambeth, Merton, Croydon, Wandsworth, Southwark and beyond. Our support gives marginalised people access to justice and the opportunity to build a safe, stable and positive future. The Role This is a key role in ensuring that we continue to secure the resources we need to provide our vital services and activities for refugees, asylum seekers and other migrants in South London. As Fundraising Manager for SLRA, you will play a pivotal role in implementing our fundraising strategy, building relationships with donors and exceeding fundraising goals. We are predominantly funded by Trusts and Foundations and you will be responsible for maintaining and expanding this funder base, while helping to diversify our income streams in order to ensure that established services and activities are sustained. If you have substantial experience of building relationships and securing funds from Trusts and Foundations, and an understanding of the challenges and opportunities faced by small, local voluntary organisations we would love to hear from you! Closing date: Monday 21st September at 9am (please note that we will close the advert early if enough strong applications are received, so please apply promptly) First stage interviews online: Monday 28th and Tuesday 29th September Second stage in person: Friday 2nd October As an organisation working with migrants, we particularly welcome applications from people with lived experience of the impact of the UK immigration or asylum system. We guarantee an interview for all applicants with lived experience who meet the essential criteria for this post.

item.title: Community Connector
item.description: We’re looking for a compassionate and motivated Community Connector to join our GP Integrated Mental Health Service and Mental Health Integrated Community Service in Surrey Heath. This is an exciting opportunity to work at the heart of local communities, supporting people with their mental health and wellbeing by helping them access the right support at the right time. Working alongside GPs, mental health practitioners, partner agencies and community organisations, you will provide timely assessments, brief psychosocial interventions and practical support that helps people build on their strengths, overcome barriers and connect with services, activities and networks that promote independence and recovery. As part of Catalyst Support, you will be joining a Surrey charity committed to supporting wellness together through kindness, integrity and commitment. We are looking for someone who is confident working with people experiencing mental health challenges, able to build positive relationships with professionals and community partners, and passionate about making support more accessible, joined-up and person-centred. Location: Surrey Heath Salary: £30,280 Hours: 35 hours across Monday to Friday Contract type: Permanent Key responsibilities: To work jointly with the Mental Health Practitioner in conducting assessments, including risk assessment, and to work with patients to support them in identifying their socially determined needs and goals, provide self-management tools and facilitate the development of personal support plans To provide a range of motivational and structured psychosocial interventions To promote independence through an enabling asset-based approach that draws on individuals’ strengths, preferences and ‘natural’ support networks To establish effective working relationships with a range of agencies to facilitate a ‘joined up’ approach to support plans To liaise with, develop and maintain good relations with GPs, practice managers and other health practitioners across mental health and physical health pathways and wider support networks To provide continuity throughout recovery; engaging the patient with key services such as Safe Havens, accessing CMHRS, and providing support for those engaged with and leaving CMHRS, and linking into local wellbeing services and activities To co-ordinate and support patients to access a range of community services such as wellbeing services, housing providers, family and carer support services, debt and employer advisors where appropriate To assist with community resource mapping exercises and maintain a database of community resources; map where there are gaps in provision across the PCN and wider geography and work with other VCS organisations to develop resources where most needed To promote and support (where necessary) advised follow up actions from physical health checks for people with serious mental illness To support patients to engage with local peer support workers and volunteering services To support and supervise any peer support workers linked to PCN To work with the service to identify opportunities to expand provision particularly in local communities where there is a lack of service provision identified To broker and establish new partnerships between public and voluntary sector agencies to enhance service delivery and access to services To develop and sustain professional relationships with service users, partner agencies and appropriate external agencies To complete locally agreed quality outcome measures, with patients and to undertake regular reviews You may be required to cover duties not listed within this job description. About the organisation Through Community, Specialist and Outreach services, we support recovery, mental health, and wellbeing—together, every step of the way. About you Essential: A diploma or degree in an appropriate subject, e.g. counselling, psychology, social work, probation, mental health, or Health and Social Care Level 3; and/or a minimum of two years’ community experience in drug, alcohol or mental health work. Understanding and ability to work to confidentiality, consent, information sharing and safeguarding policies within an integrated service. Good communication and written skills, with a commitment to accurate and confidential record keeping. Ability to interact effectively with the client group, colleagues and other professionals while maintaining clear boundaries. Ability to break down stigma and barriers associated with working with the client group. Understanding of the issues and needs of the client group. Knowledge and understanding of community working and lone working, with the ability to maintain safety while working in the community. Ability to work to all policies, procedures and standards of the service and joint-working arrangements with key partners. Good understanding of personal limitations, with the ability to identify when to seek advice and support and deal with emotionally challenging issues objectively and professionally. Ability to manage challenging behaviour, anger and verbal aggression from patients. Proficient in Microsoft Word, Outlook and Excel. Ability to enter data onto a database as required by the service. Demonstrates Catalyst’s values of kindness, commitment and integrity. Ability to maintain equal opportunity standards at all times. Ability to be resilient when working with the client group, while demonstrating compassion and willingness to go the extra mile. Ability to maintain respect for the client group, peers and partners. Adaptable to change. Dynamic and self-motivated. Proactive, motivated and energetic. Ability to work calmly in a challenging environment. Capacity to innovate and work flexibly on own initiative as well as part of a team. Commitment to developing skills and knowledge through ongoing learning and development. Ability to work flexibly across operational hours. Ability to work to the policies, procedures and standards of the charity. Desirable If holding a professional qualification, maintain up-to-date professional registration, e.g. BACP, HCPC, BPS or recognised equivalent. Benefits 26 days annual leave plus bank holidays (increasing with service) Pension scheme and access to Simply Health (including optical, dental, counselling sessions) Birthday leave, employee discounts, and flexible working where possible Supportive probation, sick pay after probation, and wellbeing/EAP resources Safeguarding & Checks This role is subject to a basic DBS check. A past history of drug/alcohol issues or criminality will not necessarily exclude you from this role; we encourage applications from people with lived experience where appropriate. All applicants must have a valid right to work in the UK Catalyst Support is an equal opportunities employer. We celebrate difference and are committed to fairness, accessibility, and inclusion throughout recruitment and employment. We welcome requests for reasonable adjustments at any stage of the process. item.title: Individual Giving Manager
item.description: Shaftesbury is a national disability charity that supports more than 4,000 children, young people and adults with a disability every year to live a life that truly adds up for them. That is at the heart of everything they do. Their vision ‘all together better for disability’, is about working alongside the people they support so they can participate, contribute and be valued for who they are. Their work is spearheaded by 1,500+ dedicated staff and volunteers who deliver a wide range of disability care, special education and rehabilitation services across England, Wales and Northern Ireland, around the clock. To achieve their vision, they are looking for an Individual Giving Manager with a focus on acquisition to work alongside the Head of Individual Giving across regular gifts, appeals, lottery, raffle and other new products. The Individual Giving Manager drives the recruitment of new supporters and supports the stewardship of warm audience, generating sustainable income for Shaftesbury. The proportion of acquisition focus v retention focus is likely around 70/30. This role focuses on maximising long-term value through innovative and impactful multichannel campaigns including reactivating lapsed supporters, optimising supporter conversion and delivering engaging onboarding experiences. The Individual Giving Manager will work on growing regular giving, cash and gaming pipelines and manage exciting projects which could include digital, DRTV, face-to- face, telemarketing, direct mail and radio. The role will provide assistance to the Head of Individual Giving with all retention activity, including cash appeals and newsletters. Shaftesbury is happy to consider fundraiser or officer level candidates looking to step up into their first manager level role. At present this role doesn’t line manage, so management experience is not necessary. The successful candidate will be able to demonstrate project or product management skills, an enthusiasm for fundraising, familiarity with supporter journeys, creative thinking and will have experience within a UK based charity in either IG and legacies, community fundraising, corporate or philanthropy. This role is hybrid, with 4 days per month on average at either the Gateshead office or London office. The one role is being advertised twice to ensure candidates from both geographic locations see the role within their search remit and feel able to apply. Application notes Please download the Candidate Info Pack provided for further information about the role, timelines and next steps. To express interest, please contact THINK Recruitment using the information in the Candidate Pack to organise an informal screening call. Please note, we cannot progress candidates through to longlist without speaking with them, so please ensure you leave enough time to organise a screening call before the role closes. Following your call we will share the info needed to submit a full application. If you need assistance with downloading the pack, please send an email to THINK and our team will support you. Deadline for expressions of interest: Midnight Sunday 13th September Closing date for applications: Midnight Monday 14th September

The Organisation The Chartered College of Teaching is a charity and the professional body for teachers. We are working to empower a knowledgeable and respected teaching profession through membership and accreditation. We are dedicated to bridging the gap between practice and research and equipping teachers from the moment they enter the classroom with the knowledge and confidence to make the best decisions for their pupils. Our activities mainly focus on four key areas: membership teacher CPD and accreditation research, policy and events online and print resources Since opening membership in 2017, we have grown rapidly. In total our work reaches over 40,000 teachers and more than 3.6 million young people. We are a growing and multi-skilled team of 30 people, supported by a Board with a significant track record of experience in a range of fields. Our business plan focuses on growing membership and Chartered Status, strategic positioning of the College in the education sector, and providing meaningful professional learning opportunities for the teaching profession. The Opportunity Our organisation supports teachers to make a difference to the lives of millions of children worldwide. Our Research and Policy team, within which this role will be situated, works to connect research, policy and practice through internally and externally funded research projects, thought leadership work as well as online and face-to-face events. Over the duration of the contract, you will: lead the final phase of delivery of our Rethinking Curriculum project with a focus on delivering sustainable impact for the future; update the College’s existing curriculum Toolkits, so they align with ongoing updates of the National Curriculum; refine an online course on creative and critical thinking, transitioning from a cohort-based model to a self-paced model; oversee and chair an online events portfolio relating to the project; support the organisation and delivery of an in-person book launch and celebration event to mark the culmination of the project; contribute to the final report of the project; develop the existing Rethinking Curriculum Evaluation Framework to extend so could be suitable for secondary settings, particularly KS3 to support transition; develop a strategy for and launch a curriculum-focused special interest group (SIG) for members to support the legacy of the Rethinking Curriculum project; support the Fellow engagement strategy at the College by organising relevant, curriculum-related roundtables to support the legacy of the Rethinking Curriculum project; oversee project finances under the guidance of the Associate Director for Research and Policy; develop a suite of relevant resources to support schools in implementing changes following the consultation for the new National Curriculum; ensure funder requirements for the delivery and closure of the project are met; represent the Chartered College of Teaching at relevant events. This would be an ideal opportunity for somebody with a strong background in curriculum development. You will: have autonomy for the delivery of the final stages of our flagship Rethinking Curriculum project; work collaboratively with many of the team across the organisation, supporting recruitment and retention of our members; help to grow the professional membership organisation for the teaching profession and be part of the team driving the organisation forward at an exciting time for the future of the College About You Curriculum development is a key priority area for the government and therefore for school leaders and teachers in England. You do not need to have expertise in absolutely all areas, let us decide! We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment and encourage you to apply. We’re looking for someone who is motivated by our vision and is passionate about Curriculum Development. Systems you would be using include Asana, Google Suite and MyPD (an online learning platform). Essential skills and experience: Educated to at least degree standard with QTS, with experience teaching in schools in England; Experience designing, leading and/or evaluating curriculum-related teacher professional development at a whole-school, Trust and/or wider professional network level; Experience supporting and/or leading curriculum change and implementation within a school setting; A good understanding of the research landscape relating to curriculum development and implementation across phases; Experience developing teacher-facing resources and professional learning content relating to curriculum planning and development; Experience producing content (e.g., written reports and research summaries) for a range of audiences (e.g., teachers, school leaders and policymakers); Experience liaising with funders and managing a project, including a project budget; Experience organising and delivering professional events, including conferences, roundtables, workshops or other engagement activities. Desirable skills and experience Educated with a higher degree in education and/or Chartered Teacher Status; As well as technical requirements, we are looking for people who: Believe in the transformative power of education, see teachers as key drivers in achieving improved educational outcomes for all and are motivated to contribute to this change. Communicate clearly and effectively, understanding the importance of conveying complex ideas in an easy-to-understand way and respecting the work schedules and patterns of colleagues. Learning and feedback oriented and keen to develop their skillset. Are committed to equality and diversity, demonstrating these through their work and daily interactions with colleagues, members and other stakeholders. Why Us? As an organisation we care deeply about creating a working environment that supports our people to grow personally and professionally. These are reflected in our organisational values which outline the distinctive working culture we are looking to create. In particular, these values are reflected in our commitment to: Flexible working: responsive management, flexible hours, hybrid or fully remote working Professional development, including formal and informal training and support Transparency and ownership: we have an open culture that ensures all staff guide our strategic direction Mental health and wellbeing: access to health and wellbeing advice and health cash plan. Diversity and inclusion at the Chartered College As a growing organisation we are committed to: Becoming increasingly representative of the sector and geographies that we operate in Providing a positive experience of work as part of an inclusive culture led by our organisational values Maintaining an annual EDI action plan - led by the internal team. What to expect from the recruitment process All applications are anonymised until the point of interview Line Managers trained in recognising bias We implement a standardised interview template and competencies matrix for a fair and transparent process All interviews are conducted via Zoom and the use of camera is optional. If you require any adjustments in order to proceed with an application please contact us. For more information about joining the Chartered College, please watch this short video from Dame Alison Peacock (CEO). Your Personal Data As part of the recruitment process, the Chartered College of Teaching collects and processes personal data relating to job applicants. The organisation is committed to being transparent about how it collects and uses that data and to meeting its data protection obligations. Pre-employment checks All conditional offers of employment are subject to: Two satisfactory references Proof of qualifications Eligibility to work in the UK. We are an employer committed to the safeguarding of children and young people.

item.title: Support Time Recovery (STR) Worker
item.description: 6 x Vacancies Available We are looking for six client-focused Support Time Recovery Workers to join our new Wigan Crisis Space service, supporting local residents experiencing emotional distress and mental health challenges. Wigan Crisis Space is a new service providing a safe space for those in distress and struggling with unwanted thoughts and feelings. Looking to improve mental health and wellbeing, we connect individuals to a range of services to reduce low mood, anxiety and loneliness, develop new skills and ensure their voice is heard. Our STR Workers provide low-level calming interventions and one-to-one support to help people identify the causes of their emotional distress and put in place a support plan that includes signposting and referrals to other appropriate organisations and services. The ideal candidates will have an awareness of mental health conditions, experience of building strong relationships with people and excellent listening skills. The ability to develop trust with those accessing the service is key to supporting them to achieve their recovery goals and desired outcomes. Main Responsibilities • Develop trusting relationships and provide short-term one-to-one appointments that offer practical and emotional support. • Carry out initial ‘getting to know you’ conversations, working with individuals to plan their support and achieve the goals and outcomes that are important to them. • Develop and maintain knowledge of local services and organisations that can provide support to improve wellbeing. • Ensure regular and robust case recording and risk management in line with quality standards. • Complete referrals to ensure people accessing Wigan Crisis Space have the appropriate support networks around them. • Support and facilitate group activities that promote wellbeing and recovery as part of our prevention agenda. Benefits • 25 days annual leave (pro rata for part-time employees), increasing by one day each April up to a maximum of 30 days, plus bank holidays. • Up to 6% matched pension contributions. • Flexible working arrangements, with the right to request flexible working from day one. • Enhanced paid sick leave and family leave provisions. • Eye care vouchers and winter flu jab vouchers. • Cycle to Work scheme. • Ongoing training and professional development opportunities. Role Details • Salary: Starting at £25,221 FTE per annum, rising to £27,780 FTE per annum (£14,314.62 to £15,766.02 per annum for 21 hours per week). • Location: Wigan Crisis Space, Crompton Street, Wigan, WN1 1YP. Office-based and wheelchair accessible. • Hours: Part-time, 21 hours per week. The role includes evening and weekend working on a rota basis. Find Out More Interested in learning more about Wigan Crisis Space and what it's like to work within the service? We are holding an informal online drop-in session where you can meet the Service Manager and Operational Manager, learn more about the role and the service, and ask any questions you may have before applying. • Date: Tuesday 1 September 2026 • Time: 10:30am • Location: Online via Microsoft Teams • Joining details are available on the Family Action vacancy webpage. No booking is required. We would be delighted to meet anyone interested in joining the team and learning more about the service. About Family Action Wigan Crisis Space is delivered by Family Action, a national charity that works from the heart of local communities. For more than 150 years, we have supported people through change, challenge and crisis, providing practical, emotional and financial support to families, children, young people and adults across the UK. We are a forward-looking, ambitious and people-focused organisation, committed to continuous improvement, mutual respect and excellence in all we do. How to Apply • Click the Apply button below. You will be redirected to the Family Action vacancy webpage to complete your application. • Closing Date: Sunday 6 September 2026 at 11:59pm. Interview Dates In-person interviews are scheduled to take place on 16 and 17 September 2026. For Direct Queries If you would like to discuss any aspect of the role, the selection process or flexible working requests, please visit the Family Action vacancy webpage for the hiring manager's contact details. Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion We are committed to building a diverse workforce and welcome applications from all sections of the community. We particularly encourage applications from people from ethnically diverse communities, LGBTQIA+ candidates and disabled candidates. We are happy to consider reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process and in the workplace. Candidates with a disability are welcome to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and request priority consideration for interview, provided they meet the essential criteria for the role. To help remove financial barriers to working with us, we will reimburse reasonable travel costs for candidates invited to attend an interview in person.

item.title: Global Accounts Receivable Assistant
item.description: Compassion in World Farming International is a global movement transforming the future of food and farming. As Global Accounts Receivable Assistant, you’ll help ensure supporter income is recorded accurately and efficiently, supporting the financial data that enables our teams to keep driving change for animals, people and the planet. Global Accounts Receivable Assistant Role type: Permanent; Full-time or part-time hours considered, minimum 0.8 FTE Location: Godalming HQ, UK, hybrid working pattern, 2 days in the office per week Salary: £26,000 - £28,000 per annum (depending upon skills and experience) About the role As our Global Accounts Receivable Assistant , you’ll be part of our Finance team, helping to maintain timely and accurate recording of supporter income across our global entities. This is a key role supporting the financial processes that underpin our fundraising activity and wider mission to end factory farming. As our Global Accounts Receivable Assistant, you’ll be responsible for: Recording global donations accurately - Downloading and posting accounts receivable income received for all entity bank accounts, ensuring clear audit trails are maintained. Supporting accurate financial coding - Amending postings to reflect accurate campaign codes and responding to reconciliation queries around donation recording. Flagging issues and queries appropriately - Escalating refunds, disputes, discrepancies and inaccuracies to the right manager or senior colleague for review. Supporting improvements to procedures and systems - Helping to test system and procedural updates, query discrepancies in existing processes and provide constructive feedback where needed. Working collaboratively across teams - Building effective working relationships with colleagues across Finance, Marketing and Fundraising, and directing donation queries to the correct point of contact. About you To succeed as our Global Accounts Receivable Assistant , you’ll be organised, accurate and proactive, with a positive approach to routine administrative work and a genuine interest in supporting a purpose-led Finance function. Skills and experience you’ll need to bring: Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications, internet use and confidence using basic Excel formulas. Strong attention to detail, with the ability to set high standards for your own work and maintain accurate records. Sound judgement and the confidence to make timely decisions at the appropriate level, including knowing when to escalate to a manager or Financial Controller. Good time management skills, with the ability to plan and organise your workload and manage busy periods effectively. A collaborative and respectful approach, recognising the perspectives and values of others and communicating positively with colleagues across the organisation. A proactive mindset, with a willingness to learn, support agreed processes and contribute to continuous improvement. Previous experience working with CRM and ERP Systems such as Salesforce and Netsuite If you don’t meet every requirement but believe you could thrive in this role, we encourage you to apply. Why join us This is more than just a finance role. It’s a chance to use your accuracy, organisation and attention to detail to support a global movement working to end factory farming and create a more compassionate future. We offer a supportive, flexible workplace with a strong focus on wellbeing and development, including: 25 days annual leave + bank holidays Health Cash Back Plan and 24/7 GP access Employee Assistance Programme and MHFA support Premium Calm App subscription Electric car scheme available Defined contribution pension scheme Enhanced discretionary sick pay Hybrid working model (role and location dependent) Free onsite parking and office next to mainline station Cycle Benefit scheme and other savings options Ongoing learning and development opportunities How to apply and key dates If you’re ready to make a global impact, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your CV and a cover letter outlining how you meet the Person Specification. To support a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly ask that you do not include a photo in your CV. Please note that we may begin interviews on a rolling basis, so early applications are encouraged. Closing date: Thursday 17th September 2026 1st Stage (Teams) Interview: Anticipated planned dates Tuesday 22nd and Thursday 24th September 2026 2nd Stage (Face to Face at HQ) Interview, with task: Anticipated planned Tuesday 29th September 2026 “ Join us in building a more compassionate future for animals, people, and the planet.” As part of Stage 1 interviews, shortlisted candidates may receive pre‑shared, values‑based interview questions to support a positive candidate experience. If you require any adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know, we’re always happy to support candidates. About Compassion Compassion in World Farming International is a leading global organisation working to end factory farming. Founded in 1967 by British farmer Peter Roberts, we’ve spent over 50 years driving change, successfully campaigning to ban cruel practices such as barren battery cages, veal crates, and sow stalls across the UK and Europe. Our work combines advocacy, campaigning, and collaboration with policymakers and businesses to promote animal welfare and sustainable food systems. We envision a future where animals are treated with compassion, and farming supports both people and the planet. To learn more about our mission, culture, and opportunities, please explore our Candidate Pack, and Careers Page. To comply with legal requirements in the UK and internationally, all applicants must be able to demonstrate their right to work in the country where the role is based. Compassion in World Farming is absolutely committed to providing equal opportunities for everyone regardless of their background. We value diversity and live experience and acknowledge the underrepresentation of people from certain backgrounds, both within our organisation and across the sector. We welcome applications from underrepresented groups, whether these be of ethnicity, gender, identity, religion, physical ability, sexual orientation or other.

item.title: Youth Services Team Lead
item.description: We have an exciting opportunity to join our Youth Team. This role will suit someone with experience supporting and/or working with ADHD and/or autistic young people who is highly organised and shares our passion for making a difference. About the Role Support the operational management of the Youth Service , assisting the Youth Services Manager with the day-to-day leadership, coordination, and development of youth programmes across North West London. Line manage and support Youth Support Workers , providing supervision, guidance, and oversight to ensure high-quality service delivery and achievement of programme objectives. Deliver direct support to neurodivergent young people and families through one-to-one sessions, group activities, courses, and peer support programmes that improve understanding, wellbeing, and quality of life Undertake administrative, project management, and strategic planning activities , including scheduling appointments, creating content, facilitating groups, monitoring service delivery, and ensuring funder requirements are met. In this role, you will join the CAAS Youth Services Team as we work to educate, empower and improve quality of life for neurodivergent individuals, their families, and the communities they live in. We work in a variety of settings, so a flexible approach is essential. Some evening or weekend work may be required depending on scheduled sessions Who We Are Looking For: You’ll have experience or strong knowledge of working with ADHD and/or autistic young people You’ll have previous experience of managing people and projects Enjoy working with people, and feel confident running groups and courses You’ll be organised, a good communicator, and committed to neurodiversity affirming, person-centred support. About Us: T he Centre for ADHD and Autism Support (CAAS) is a registered charity (Charity Registration Number: 1193799) and we provide information, training, support groups and practical help to residents of North-West London. Our support services encompass education, benefits, parenting and care advice with signposting to other agencies if appropriate. Remuneration Package & Contract Details Annual FTE salary: Up to £37,250 FTE per annum (based on 35hrs a week) / Pro-rata £29,800 based on 28 hours a week Contract Type: Permanent Working Weeks Per Annum: 52 weeks Working Hours Per Week: 28 hours Working Days: Flexible hours - evening and weekend work may be required, and the hours may differ each week, depending on the activity that is being undertaken. Annual Leave Entitlement: 20 days annually, plus bank holidays, plus your birthday off each year If you’re looking for a supportive, inclusive workplace with an excellent reputation for family‑centred practice, we’d be delighted to receive your application, along with a short covering note. Safeguarding Statement: The Centre for ADHD and Autism Support is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff, workers and volunteers to share this commitment. The successful candidate will be required to provide two satisfactory references, undertake pre-employment checks and have a cleared Enhanced Disclosure & Barring check. Please note If you haven’t heard from us within two weeks of the closing date, please assume that you have not been shortlisted for interview. Due to the volume of applications we receive, we are unfortunately unable to respond to everyone individually. Thank you for considering a role with us – we genuinely value your interest and hope you will consider applying for future opportunities.

item.title: Head of Research and Evaluation
item.description: About the role As Head of Research and Evaluation, you will be responsible for the development and delivery of our research and evaluation strategies. This work will help us to understand and provide insight into the challenges and difficulties faced by families with disabled children, the quality of services we provide and the difference our support makes for the families we serve. You will ensure that the voice of families is at the centre of our research and evaluation approach to help shape existing and new programmes and services, and our policy and public affairs work. If you join us, you’ll be: Leading the continued development and implementation of Family Fund’s research and evaluation strategies. Developing and overseeing our evaluation and service quality frameworks, including our Theory of Change outcomes measurement framework. Championing the ‘voice of families’, embedding their lived experience at the heart of our research. Managing and delivering high-quality research and evaluation projects/initiatives. Producing accessible, engaging, and impactful research outputs for a variety of audiences. Promoting the use of innovative and participatory research methodologies. Presenting and disseminating research findings internally and externally, including at events, conferences, and through publications. Developing and maintaining strong relationships with stakeholders and representing Family Fund in strategic research partnerships, networks, and advisory forums. Commissioning external research and evaluation where appropriate, ensuring quality, value for money. Maintaining oversight of the team’s input to government/ funder reporting, ensuring timely and accurate submissions aligned to contractual and organisational requirements. Providing visible, hands-on leadership and line management to the Research and Evaluation Team. About you For this role you will need to have experience in developing and managing research and evaluation strategies, frameworks, activities and production of subsequent products. You will also need to have experience of working in partnership with other organisations, and of resource and budget management. To be successful in this role, you will need excellent analytical skills as well as sound knowledge of quantitative and qualitative methodology and best practice through the research cycle. You will need to have good writing skills and an ability to communicate effectively with different audiences. You will also need to have the ability to interpret and present research in an accessible and engaging way. You will be a self and team motivator with excellent communication skills, and the ability to develop and sustain positive relationships with a range of stakeholders. You will be pro-active and driven to succeed. About us Family Fund is a great place to work for great people. We provide a challenging and rewarding working environment where every staff member can make their mark. We are a values based organisation and we aim to show our values in all that we do. Read our staff stories here, and see how our staff display our values every day. We commit to inclusion, equity and diversity and we welcome applications from all parts of the community. Family Fund is a Disability Confident Leader. We will invite to interview all disabled applicants who meet the requirements for the role. If you have a disability, and are happy to let us know, please highlight this in your covering letter. We have also signed the Armed Forces Covenant and we welcome applications from the Armed Forces Community. How to apply Please read and download the job description. When you’re ready to apply, complete the online application and submit a CV and a covering letter. Your letter will need to explain what skills and qualities you would bring to the team. Please note that the successful candidate will be required to complete pre-employment checks that meet the Baseline Personnel Security Standard. This includes a right-to-work check, a basic check for unspent criminal convictions, and an employment history verification for the last three years.
item.dc:creator: Family Fund

item.title: Senior Philanthropy Manager
item.description: Senior Philanthropy Manager £53,947 - £63,350 per annum inclusive of London Weighting Allowance Waterloo campus About us Philanthropy & Alumni Engagement (P&A) raises philanthropic funds in support of King’s College London and engages with the university’s worldwide alumni community. We are proud to enable the work of colleagues across the university and its health partners, helping them serve society through world-leading education, research and healthcare.Our activity includes a partnership with the Maudsley Charity in support of children’s mental health and initiatives between the university’s Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neuroscience and the South London & Maudsley NHS Trust. We are entering an exciting period as a team. Our work is identified as a key enabler of the new King’s Strategy 2030, with associated ambitions that include preparing for our next major philanthropic and engagement campaign. This will accelerate and energise our work in support of the University’s mission to be ‘in service to society through academic excellence’ – be that through exceptional, impact-led research; ensuring our students are supported to thrive during their time at King’s and beyond; or by helping the university to invest over the long-term into its people, ideas and infrastructure. We plan to deepen and scale engagement with our global alumni community, donors and other supporters, mobilising them behind these shared priorities. We are strongly values-driven with a focus on sustaining a strong and supportive culture, which we see as key to creating a successful team that can realise these ambitions. More on King’s College London For almost 200 years, King’s has been a place where ideas turn into action. From revealing the structure of DNA to reimagining nursing, from advances in medicine, law and the study of war and peace to shaping culture and public debate, our work has always been guided by a belief that knowledge should serve society. Over our history, King’s has been home to 14 Nobel Prize winners, and to scholars whose ideas and leadership have shaped thinking, policy and practice around the world. King’s has always been a place where knowledge is put to work for the benefit of others. King’s College London is a world-renowned university that delivers exceptional education and world-leading research. We're committed to creating positive and sustainable change in our local and global communities through outstanding education, impactful research, and genuine service to society. King’s Strategy 2030 sets out how we take that purpose forward, with four key priorities including student success in and beyond university, investment in research and education excellence that responds to the changing world, fostering innovation and entrepreneurship, and delivering sustainable finances for a secure future. About the role We are looking for an exceptional individual fundraiser to join the Philanthropy team at King’s College London, leading on fundraising for the Faculty of Social Science and Public Policy. This role will be responsible for managing a portfolio of major gift prospects, securing and stewarding significant philanthropic gifts at the £50k to £5 million gift level, supporting senior stakeholders with their fundraising efforts, and championing the work and priorities of King’s and the Faculty. The team will play a crucial role in the delivery of the University’s ambition to significantly scale philanthropic income for faculties, as we prepare to launch our next major fundraising campaign in 2027 and mark the university’s bicentenary in 2029. We will build on our already successful fundraising to achieve ambitious new goals for philanthropy – creating strong partnerships across campus and with donors, to realise shared priorities and deliver strategic impact. The successful candidate will work collaboratively with academic and professional service colleagues across King’s to secure significant philanthropic income to support student outcomes and drive world-leading teaching and research. We are strongly values-driven with a focus on sustaining an excellent and supportive culture, which we see as key to creating a successful team that can support the university and its partners in making a real and positive difference to the world we live in. The Faculty of Social Science and Public Policy (SSPP) is home to one of the largest, most diverse and international communities for social research and education in Europe. In a world of global, social, technological and economic transformations, the Faculty seeks to understand and shape these changes through its education and research. It has world-leading expertise across social science disciplines, with recognised strengths in security studies, political economy, global health, social risk and resilience, education and social justice. Building on this world-leading expertise and deep relationships with government, business, civil society and international organisations, the Faculty informs policy with local, national and global impact. This is a full time (35 hours per week), and you will be offered an indefinite contract. P&A has a hybrid working approach, with a minimum of 40% of time in the office. Typically, this equates to two days per week, but we’re very happy for colleagues to be in more frequently if they so wish. About you To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience: Essential criteria 1. A proven track-record of cultivating, securing, and stewarding five- and ideally six-figure gifts 2. Experience of qualifying and cultivating new philanthropic relationships. 3. Ability to develop and maintain key relationships with senior internal stakeholders. 4. Proven interpersonal and communication skills (written and verbal). 5. Ability to plan strategically and implement those plans. 6. The ability to negotiate throughout a large, complex environment with multi-dimensional points of view. 7. Ability to manage multiple projects, identifying conflicting demands and establishing clear priorities in order to meet agreed objectives and income. 8. An understanding of the philanthropic landscape and what would motivate a prospect to give to King’s. Desirable criteria 1. Major gifts fundraising experience in areas relevant to the Faculty of Social Science & Public Policy Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document. Closing date: 13 September 2026

item.title: HR Change Roles
item.description: We have multiple roles at different levels for an upcoming project. We're partnering with a well-respected public sector organisation to appoint an experienced HR Change Consultant to support the delivery of a significant organisational change programme. This is an excellent opportunity for a change professional who is comfortable leading complex consultation processes, influencing senior stakeholders, and ensuring organisational change is delivered in a fair, compliant and people-focused way. Key Responsibilities Lead and support organisational change initiatives including restructures, service redesign and workforce transformation programmes. Manage collective and individual consultation processes from planning through to implementation. Provide expert advice on employment law, redundancy, redeployment and organisational change matters. Build strong relationships with senior leaders, managers and trade union representatives. Develop business cases, change documentation, consultation materials and communications. Support risk management, governance and decision-making throughout the change lifecycle. Ensure all activity is delivered in line with legislation, organisational policy and best practice. Essential Experience ✅ CIPD qualified ✅ Significant experience leading complex organisational change programmes ✅ Strong consultation management experience, including collective consultation ✅ Previous experience within the Public Sector (Local Government, NHS, Higher Education, Central Government or wider public bodies) ✅ Experience working in unionised environments and engaging with Trade Unions ✅ Sound knowledge of employment law, organisational change, redeployment and redundancies ✅ Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills. What's on Offer? Opportunity to work on a high-profile transformation programme. Influence strategic workforce and organisational design decisions. Collaborative and purpose-driven public sector environment. Hybrid working arrangement. 🔥 Ideal for experienced HR Change Managers, Senior HR Business Partners, Organisational Development Consultants, or Workforce Transformation specialists looking to make an immediate impact. Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and employment business for the supply of temporary workers.
