item.title: Fire Safety Advisor
item.description: Fire Safety Advisor B&D Reside | £55,000-£65,000 | Hybrid - Barking / Sites / Home | Contract with potential to become permanent Goodman Masson are delighted to be supporting B&D Reside with the appointment of a Fire Safety Advisor , a newly created position within their Asset Management team. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced fire safety professional to join an organisation with a strong commitment to resident safety and play a key role in strengthening fire safety compliance, assurance and risk management across its housing portfolio. Working closely with the Fire Safety Manager, you will provide specialist technical advice across B&D Reside, supporting the Responsible Person and wider teams to ensure statutory and regulatory obligations are met. The Opportunity As Fire Safety Advisor, you will play a key role in ensuring B&D Reside's fire safety programme is delivered effectively, on time and to the required standards. You will work across Compliance, Repairs, Building Safety, Estates, Health & Safety, Asset Management and Housing Management , providing technical expertise and helping to embed a positive, consistent fire safety culture across the organisation. The role will have a particular focus on complex and higher-risk residential buildings, fire risk management, technical assurance, regulatory compliance, data governance and continuous improvement. You will also have the opportunity to influence how B&D Reside manages and improves its fire safety information, systems and processes as the organisation continues to develop its approach to the Golden Thread and building safety information . Key Responsibilities Support the Fire Safety Manager in developing and delivering fire safety policies, strategies and annual action plans. Undertake fire safety inspections and risk reviews, developing appropriate action plans and remediation requirements. Manage and oversee fire risk assessment programmes, ensuring assessments are completed to a high standard and within required timescales. Provide expert technical advice on fire safety across B&D Reside's property portfolio. Support fire safety improvement projects across Asset Management, Compliance, Repairs and Building Safety. Quality assure fire risk assessments, surveys, remedial works and wider fire safety activity. Maintain and develop comprehensive fire safety risk registers, ensuring risks, mitigations and actions are properly tracked. Investigate fire-related incidents, dangerous occurrences and near misses, identifying lessons learned and improvement opportunities. Support the delivery of PCFRAs and PEEPs where required. Oversee key fire safety documentation including evacuation plans, fire statements and supporting evidence. Work with external consultants and stakeholders on Fire Action Plans and the rollout of the triple pathway evacuation system. Provide oversight of Fire Incident Reporting, Fire & Rescue Service compliance and Regulation 38 certification processes. Act as an operational interface with relevant regulatory bodies and Fire & Rescue Services. Support the management of fire safety requirements across Higher Risk Buildings where required. Ensure key building information, including Regulation 38 information, as-built documentation, floor plans, PEEPs, evacuation strategies and fire safety records, is accurate and up to date. Act as the data steward for fire safety information, ensuring robust governance, accuracy and data quality. Support digital improvement initiatives and the development of effective fire safety information management systems. Promote resident engagement and ensure fire safety information is communicated clearly and effectively. Develop strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including contractors, consultants, the Council and Fire & Rescue Services. Horizon scan for changes in legislation, regulation and best practice, ensuring B&D Reside responds proactively. Contribute to committees, senior management meetings and reporting requirements relating to fire safety. item.title: Registered Manager - Argyll and Bute, West of Scotland
item.description: Job title: Registered Manager (Internal job title: Operations Manager) Location: Argyll and Bute, West of Scotland Contract : Permanent Salary: £49,142.17 Hours: Full-time (37.5 hours per week) Transport requirements: Full UK driving licence and access to a car/vehicle. Qualifications: At least SCQF Level 9 health and social care and Level 10 leadership and management, or a Registered Managers Award - or working towards Be the Inspiration Behind Great Teams Lead. Influence. Transform. At Affinity Trust, we support people with learning disabilities, autism, mental health, physical disabilities, and other complex needs to live their lives as independently as possible. This is an exciting leadership opportunity to lead and develop a team of managers across a variety of locations. You will oversee supported living, and outreach locations, helping to ensure people receive high-quality, person-centred support that reflects their individual goals, strengths, and aspirations. The people we support are at the heart of everything we do, and this role offers a real opportunity to make a positive difference in their lives and communities. As the Registered Manager, you will be working closely with the Divisional Director, support teams, and local authorities, to shape and grow our locations across the west of Scotland. Join us and play a key role in supporting people to live their lives their way. What You'll Bring To succeed in this role, you'll be a passionate and values-driven leader who can: Deliver safe, high-quality, person-centred support across multiple services Lead with compassion and integrity, creating a culture where people feel valued, respected, and empowered Inspire and develop strong leadership teams, keeping the people we support at the centre of every decision Champion choice, independence, and positive outcomes Drive service quality, performance, and continuous improvement Manage budgets effectively and ensure financial sustainability Ensure compliance with all regulatory and quality standards Participate in the on-call rota as the Registered Manager across your services Build and maintain strong relationships with people we support, families, colleagues, commissioners, and professional partners Our Values We work together | We have courage | We give our best | People are at the heart of everything we do We're Looking for Someone Who Is: An inspiring leader who brings out the best in others Skilled at managing operations while staying true to their values Passionate about coaching, developing, and empowering teams A confident change leader who embraces opportunities to improve and innovate Calm, resilient, and solutions-focused when faced with challenges Hands-on, approachable, and visible in their leadership style Committed to delivering outstanding support and achieving positive outcomes We’re waiting to hear from you Ready to Make a Difference? This is more than a management role. It's an opportunity to shape services, develop future leaders, and make a genuine impact on the lives of the people we support every day. If you're ready to lead with purpose, inspire others, and help build great services, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today and be part of something meaningful. Benefits That Work for You Choose from a range of benefits designed to support your wellbeing, finances, and lifestyle: Wagestream: Access your pay as you earn it, plus coaching, vouchers, discounts, and cashback Blue Light Card: We’ll cover your membership for discounts at shops and restaurants Simplyhealth: Fully funded health plans with 24/7 GP access and cash back on prescriptions, dental, opticians, and more Buy & Sell Annual Leave: Flexible leave options twice a year. Pension & Life Assurance: Automatic enrolment in our Scottish Widows pension and Life Assurance schemes. We’re committed to being Disability Confident and we guarantee to interview all applicants with a disability who meet the minimum criteria for the vacancy. Please note that we are actively shortlisting candidates throughout the duration of the advert, interviews will be held as soon as possible and we will make an offer immediately if we find the right candidate. Apply without delay!

item.title: Team Leader
item.description: 2 x Vacancies Available We are looking for two passionate Team Leaders to join our new Wigan Crisis Space service and support local residents experiencing emotional distress and mental health challenges. Wigan Crisis Space is a new service providing a safe space for those in distress and struggling with unwanted thoughts and feelings. Looking to improve mental health and wellbeing, we connect individuals to a range of services to reduce low mood, anxiety and loneliness, develop new skills and ensure their voice is heard. As a Team Leader, you will combine strong leadership skills with a caring and supportive approach. You will have a good understanding of mental health and the impact it can have on people's lives, alongside the ability to lead and develop a team delivering high-quality support. You will have a proven track record of working effectively with individuals and their families, contributing to service development, and supporting colleagues to learn and grow. You will be a self-starter who is confident in helping to shape and develop a new provision within the local community. Main Responsibilities • Lead and line manage a small team of Support Time Recovery (STR) Workers to deliver a safe, effective and responsive service. • Support STR Workers with goal setting, safety planning and interventions, providing guidance and advice on safeguarding matters and working closely with the Service Manager on complex cases. • Develop and maintain knowledge of local services and organisations that can provide support to improve wellbeing. • Ensure regular and robust case recording and risk management in line with quality standards. Benefits • 25 days annual leave (pro rata for part-time employees), increasing by one day each April up to a maximum of 30 days, plus bank holidays. • Up to 6% matched pension contributions. • Flexible working arrangements, with the right to request flexible working from day one. • Enhanced paid sick leave and family leave provisions. • Eye care vouchers and winter flu jab vouchers. • Cycle to Work scheme. • Ongoing training and professional development opportunities. Role Details • Salary: Starting at £28,884 FTE per annum, rising to £31,698 FTE per annum (£23,419.45 to £25,701.08 per annum for 30 hours per week). • Location: Wigan Crisis Space, Crompton Street, Wigan, WN1 1YP. Office-based and wheelchair accessible. • Hours: Part-time, 30 hours per week. Working late afternoons and evenings, with weekend working on a rota basis. • Contract: Permanent. Find Out More Interested in learning more about Wigan Crisis Space and what it's like to work within the service? We are holding an informal online drop-in session where you can meet the Service Manager and Operational Manager, learn more about the role and the service, and ask any questions you may have before applying. • Date: Tuesday 1 September 2026 • Time: 3:00 pm • Location: Online via Microsoft Teams • Joining details are available on the Family Action vacancy webpage. No booking is required. We would be delighted to meet anyone interested in joining the team and learning more about the service. About Family Action Wigan Crisis Space is delivered by Family Action, a national charity that works from the heart of local communities. For more than 150 years, we have supported people through change, challenge and crisis, providing practical, emotional and financial support to families, children, young people and adults across the UK. We are a forward-looking, ambitious and people-focused organisation, committed to continuous improvement, mutual respect and excellence in all we do. How to Apply • Click the Apply button below. You will be redirected to the Family Action vacancy webpage to complete your application. • Closing Date: Sunday 6 September 2026 at 11:59pm. Interview Date In-person interviews are scheduled to take place on Monday 14 September 2026. For Direct Queries If you would like to discuss any aspect of the role, the selection process or flexible working requests, please visit the Family Action vacancy webpage for the hiring manager's contact details. Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion We are committed to building a diverse workforce and welcome applications from all sections of the community. We particularly encourage applications from people from ethnically diverse communities, LGBTQIA+ candidates and disabled candidates. We are happy to consider reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process and in the workplace. Candidates with a disability are welcome to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and request priority consideration for interview, provided they meet the essential criteria for the role. To help remove financial barriers to working with us, we will reimburse reasonable travel costs for candidates invited to attend an interview in person.

item.title: Education Worker
item.description: We’re an award-winning charity running local learning centres in the heart of the communities where the young people we support live. Our centres provide a high-impact education programme which includes practical learning support, pastoral care, and motivational and confidence-building activities for young people aged 7-18. Our aim is to enable students from the least advantaged neighbourhoods to realise their ambitions and achieve their wonderful potential. As the UK’s leading university access organisation, our staff team is helping over 60,000 young people each year at its 46 learning centres and extension projects across England and Scotland, and we plan to scale-up our provision to 50 centres over the coming years. We are looking for graduates who will enjoy working each day with young people and who will thrive in a frontline, community-based, fast-paced and rewarding role . You will be taking up a permanent role as an Education Worker on IntoUniversity’s Graduate Scheme, helping to change the lives of young people. We believe that our Graduate Scheme is one of the most exciting in the charity sector, an excellent career opportunity with exceptional training and hands-on experience, opportunities for promotion , and the chance to work with young people and colleagues who will challenge and inspire you. The role at a glance Contract: Full-time, permanent Start date: As soon as possible Application deadline : 9am Friday 11th September 2026 Interview day (online): Friday 18th September 2026 Please ensure you are available on these dates Working hours Mon and Thurs: 09:30-18:00 Tues, Weds, Fri: 09:00-17:30 (Some additional weekend & unsocial hours will be required) Education Workers are based at one of our Into University learning centres and work directly with young people, schools and families on a daily basis. It is therefore not a hybrid role and is based full-time in our centres Location Into University Craigmillar The role requires intermittent travel in your region (usually within the day). Periodic travel out of the area is also required e.g. to London, this may include occasional overnight stays. Salary £29,050 per annum. Annual leave 33 days (inc bank & public holidays) (pro rata for part-time staff) + 3 closure days (two in December and one in July) + additional length of service entitlement (one day per year of service, up to 5 days)

item.title: Housing First Worker
item.description: Join our Housing First team and make a lasting difference to people experiencing homelessness and multiple, complex needs. As a Housing First Worker, you will provide personalised, trauma-informed support to individuals in their own homes, helping them build independence and sustain long-term tenancies. You will develop person-centred support and safety plans, manage risk, work closely with partner agencies and build strong support networks around each resident. Using a compassionate, strengths-based approach, you will empower people to achieve their goals, connect with their communities and create lasting positive change. Main Purpose Of Job: The Housing First Worker is part of a small dynamic team delivering a personalised, trauma informed support service to people with complex needs facing multiple exclusions in line with Housing First principles to create long term sustainable tenancies by increasing independence and maximising connectivity with the local community. Please use the link below to learn more about the principles of Housing First: The Principles of Housing First | Homeless Link Main Areas Of Responsibility: Deliver wrap-around intensive, trauma informed support to people with multiple and complex issues within their own independent tenancies. Maintain accurate up to date records of progress against individual support plans, safety plans and outcome information. Liaise with other agencies to facilitate access to support. Regularly review the person-centred support plan to update, record and monitor progress of caseload. Build and maintain networks with staff from other stakeholders building support around eacjh of our housing first residents. Adhere to good practice safeguarding procedures with a positive risk-taking approach to ensure the wellbeing of vulnerable people. Perform robust assessments of referrals for the service to ensure the service is provided to those that meet the eligibility criteria. Promote, and encourage peer involvement within the service. Complete dynamic risk assessments and maintain own safety by following lone working procedures. Comply with Homeless Oxfordshire’s policies and procedures. Contribute to a positive working environment in which equality and diversity are valued and staff are enabled to do their best. Contribute to the work of the broader team. Safeguarding Statement: Homeless Oxfordshire is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all adults, children and young people who are at risk of harm and that come into contact with our services. We believe that all adults, children and young people have an equal right to protection from abuse, regardless of their age, race, religion, ability, gender, language, background or sexual identity and consider the wellbeing of the vulnerable adult, child or young person is paramount. As a result, we have a robust safeguarding policy to ensure everyone is treated fairly and a whistleblowing policy to enable people raise any concerns confidentially. We expect everyone (staff, trustees, associates, volunteers and anyone working on behalf of the Company) to share this commitment and read, understand and adhere to this policy and related procedures. Equal Opportunities: We employ people on the basis of their abilities. We strive to attract and develop talent that is representative of our residents and all sections of the society, and do not discriminate based on of age, faith, disability, race, gender, sexuality and socio-economic, regional or cultural background. If you are shortlisted and need us to make any adjustments to help you attend for interview, please let us know. About Us: We are an open door for people experiencing homelessness whose lives have been shaped by trauma and disadvantage; providing safety, stability and support when it is needed most. We deliver this support across Oxfordshire by providing a range of accommodation with access to high quality support, offering a safe and welcoming space for people to take control of their own lives. We are an accredited Oxford Living Wage employer, and benefits to the role include: annual leave starting at 26 days (excluding bank holidays), flexible working, enhanced benefits with qualifying service, retail discounts with our Homeless Oxfordshire Benefits Hub, and life assurance up to four times your salary and a £250 bonus if you successfully refer a someone as a new colleague through our Employee Referral Scheme as a thanks from us! What’s Next: Have a look at the job description to find out more about the role and apply on our website. Please be aware that this role is subject to an enhanced DBS disclosure check and will be undertaken for the successful candidate . We reserve the right to close this advert early if we identify a suitable candidate before the advertised closing date.

item.title: Academy Learning Designer
item.description: The Academy Learning Designer will support the development, delivery, and maintenance of Academy face-to-face and online content. As a member of the Academy team, you will work closely with the Academy Programme Lead to build and maintain a portfolio of content and resources that are accessible and appropriate for rehoming organisations/individuals located in the UK and around the world. With skills in best practice pedagogy, and experience applying that across blended learning programmes, the role holder will have excellent communication skills and the ability to coordinate and manage relationships with Subject Matter Experts within and outside of Battersea What we can offer you: In return for your commitment to our cause and to recognise the value of our employees, Battersea offers a range of benefits to support the wellbeing of our employees. These include: 28 days of annual leave (plus 8 days paid public holidays) per year. Discounted gym memberships and cycle to work schemes. Employee Assistance Programme and access to Wellbeing Resources. Generous pension contributions - up to 10% employer contribution. Free healthcare cash plan, where you can claim for a range of treatment including dental, optical, physiotherapy, chiropody and acupuncture every year. Annual interest-free season ticket loans. We are also committed to providing learning and development to our employees. During your time with us, we provide support for your professional and career development, including access to digital and in-person training programmes, leadership and management training, mentoring and much more. Diversity and inclusion: We are committed to providing a welcoming and inclusive experience for all staff, volunteers and trustees and those hoping to join us. We operate an anonymised shortlisting process and actively seek to ensure our process is fair and equitable for all. We understand the value of diverse voices, perspectives, and experiences to help us deliver even more for our dogs and cats, and we welcome applicants from all sections of the community. As a Disability Confident Committed Employer we will ask about any adjustments you may need at application and/or interview stage, and if you are offered a role with us, we’ll talk to you about any workplace adjustments you may need to help you perform at your best. If you would like to talk more about this, please contact us. Greyscale copies of the recruitment pack are also available on request. More about us: At Battersea, we aim to never turn away a dog or cat in need of help. We give each one lots of love, expert care and get to know their characters and quirks so we can find them a new home that’s just right for them. Join us and help us be here for every dog and cat, wherever they are, for as long as they need us. Acceptable use of AI: At Battersea, we value expertise. We recognise each candidate that applies to us will have a range of expertise they can offer us, so we want to hear about this in your own words. We understand the support that generative artificial intelligence (AI) software can offer but it can also lead to numerous applications presenting as generic and impersonal. This makes it difficult to gain understanding of your unique experience. To best showcase yourself, we encourage you to write your responses without the assistance of AI. If you require the use of AI software to aid in completing your application, we ask you use the generative responses as a prompt for writing your answers and avoid copying and pasting. You must also ensure the information presented in your application accurately reflects your experience. Closing date : 13th September 2026, 11.59pm All applications must be submitted before the closing date advertised. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a high volume of applications is received. Interview date(s) : First round (online via MS Teams) - Monday 21st or Tuesday 22nd September 2026 Second round (in person at Battersea London) - if necessary to be confirmed For more information about the role, please download our Recruitment pack. To apply for the role, please click on the "Apply" button.

item.title: Head of Finance
item.description: We are Age UK York, a local independent charity which exists to support the older people of York and those around them. For over 50 years our team of staff, volunteers and supporters have helped us to offer a wide range of services providing vital and trusted support so often when it is needed most. Our vital work is needed today as much as ever and we ever welcome people to join our team as together we realise our shared mission of making a positive difference to the lives of the older people of York. Job Summary: Would you like to make a life changing difference in support of local people and communities in need here in York? Can you bring financial management expertise to support a team effort and help shape the future of our long standing charity? Age UK York is offering an exciting senior leadership opportunity to join our fantastic team and support our vital work here in York. Could you be our Head of Finance and help lead our team, ensure our effective financial arrangements and the vital part it plays in realising our mission in the positive difference we can make in helping others., We are looking to find for our new Head of Finance who can bring their experience, expertise and passion to support our local York charity, our team and those we are here to help each and every day. You will manage our brilliant team with a focus on strong financial management. With both internal and external focus the role will lead on our financial management and helping our charity make every penny entrusted to us count, as we develop, manage and realise our financial goals and the difference the enable Age UK York to make in supporting older people and those around them across York. You will be part of our energised senior leadership and management teams helping to shape our charity and the continued positive difference we make whilst working closely across our teams in their role together with our Board of Trustees. The opportunity offers an excellent benefits package and support for your own personal development and aspirations. The opportunity would not only empower you to take forward the strong legacy from our current team though bring your own identity, ideas and strengths to the fore in our collective efforts to be there tomorrow and beyond. Key Responsibilities: We are looking for an experienced financial manager with a keen eye for detail and drive for high performance, continuous improvement and team work. With an ambition and drive to make a telling contribution and strengthen our charity and the difference we can together make in supporting older people and communities. We would love to hear from you if you have: · Experience and success in leading the financial management for an organisation. · Experience in providing leadership within an organisation; an eye for detail and a driver of standards in continuously learning and strengthening working practices and outcomes. · Managed a team providing support, motivation and nurturing talent and opportunity · The ability to readily transfer your existing experiences and skills to a new challenge; · Understanding of your strengths and areas for continuing development and proactively build your knowledge and skills We would love to hear from you. We’re looking for someone who: · Is successful in providing financial management for an organisation and effective in collaborating and supporting non-financial colleagues in our shared financial goals and successful practice. · Demonstrates wider leadership qualities including contributing to overarching organisational strategic priorities. · Skilled, including an excellent communicator, in building and maintaining successful relationships across internal teams and external partnerships. · Able, and experienced, in delivering in meeting outcomes and targets whilst supporting a performance and continuous improvement organisational approach. · Highly organised, adaptable, and comfortable working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment; · Strong attention to detail, analytical and critical thinking qualities, and able to apply and be energised to meet organisational challenges and opportunities in continually strengthening our organisation to help us realise our vision, mission and priorities. Qualifications, Skills and Experience: · Ability to prepare, manage, monitor and report on budgets. · Previous experience in one or more, management or financial accounting roles delivering day to day finance functions. · Experience of line management and support, motivation and development to colleagues and collective team. · Experience of supporting the development and delivery of high quality services through financial management and support to operational colleagues. · Effective understanding of financial statistics and accounting principles. · Strong interpersonal, communication and presentation skills. Including interpreting and communicating financial information to non-finance function colleagues and in support of decision making; a facilitative and accessible approach; ability to manage remote communications and diplomacy and conflict resolution skills. · Passion and commitment to work within a not-for-profit organisation and support a team approach in working to help others. · Decision making – ability to make decisions based on an analysis of data and insights, including financial, performance and needs based data. Salary and Benefits: £17.75 per hour, £32,391 (FTE) per year, pro rata Flexible working options within our 21 hour per week role A genuinely friendly and supportive environment Generous holidays – 26.5 days plus bank holidays (pro rata for part-time employees). Additional leave – an extra day of long service. Birthday day off Enhanced sick pay after 6 months of service Flexible work schedule Potential for funding towards professional qualifications Employee discounts including Blue Light Scheme eligibility BUPA Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) Free eye test Free flu jab Free DBS (Disclosure and Barring Service)

item.title: Video Production Executive
item.description: About The Role Every story matters here. Some are quiet, some joyful, some hard to tell. As a Video Production Executive at Alzheimer’s Society, you will help bring these stories to life with care, honesty and craft. You will join a creative team that believes in storytelling as a force for understanding, challenge and change. Working with the Video Production Manager, you will create and edit content across social media, interviews, campaign films and longer-form storytelling. This role has a strong focus on editing and post-production. We’re looking for someone who enjoys shaping stories in the edit: finding the right moments, building pace and structure, working with sound and graphics, and turning raw footage into engaging, polished content. People come to this role from many paths, whether film or media training, freelance work, community storytelling or self-taught practice. What matters most is strong editing ability, a good instinct for storytelling and a commitment to creating inclusive, respectful work. What you’ll do You will work across the production process, but a significant part of your role will be focused on editing and post-production, supporting everything from quick-turnaround social content to interviews, campaign films and longer, story-led pieces. Using Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or similar professional editing software, alongside tools such as After Effects where appropriate, you will edit raw footage into clear and engaging stories. You will make confident decisions around narrative, pacing, music, sound and visual treatment, as well as adapting content for different channels and formats. You will create cutdowns and different versions of content, add subtitles and graphics, and apply accessibility best practice so our work can reach as many people as possible. You will also have opportunities to support filming and production. This may include shooting interviews and documentary-style content, setting up lighting and sound, and helping to create a calm, respectful environment where people feel comfortable sharing their experiences. Alongside editing and filming, you will support production planning and logistics, including call sheets, scheduling and risk assessments, and contribute creative ideas about how our stories can be brought to life. Collaboration is central. You will work closely with the Video Production Manager and colleagues across our creative and wider teams, respond constructively to feedback and help ensure finished content is delivered accurately and consistently across platforms including social media, YouTube and internal channels. About you We welcome applicants from all backgrounds. You do not need to meet every requirement, and we encourage you to apply if you bring relevant skills and a willingness to learn. You may have: - Experience working across the full video production process, from pre-production through to filming and editing - Strong working knowledge of Adobe Premiere Pro (and ideally After Effects), with the ability to edit content to a high standard - Practical experience recording sound and working with lighting in documentary or factual filming environments - Experience working on story-led content, including supporting people to share personal or sensitive experiences in a respectful and ethical way - An understanding of motion graphics, or a willingness to learn and develop skills in this area - A collaborative and inclusive working style, with strong organisation skills and a commitment to accessible, high-quality storytelling Interviews are provisionally scheduled to take place on the 23rd September via MS Teams About Alzheimer's Society Dementia is the UK's biggest killer. One in three people born in the UK today will develop dementia in their lifetime. At Alzheimer's Society, we're the UK's leading dementia charity and the only one to tackle all aspects of dementia by giving help and hope to people living with dementia today and in the future. We give vital support to people facing the most frightening times of their lives, while also funding groundbreaking research and campaigning to make dementia the priority it should be. Together with our supporters, we're working towards a world where dementia no longer devastates lives. Our values make sure that our focus is clear for the challenges and opportunities ahead and remind us of what we all stand for. Our commitment to Equity, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging We need to ensure the voices around our table better reflect and understand the communities we exist to serve. We strongly encourage individuals to apply who have a disability, impairment or health condition or individuals who identify as Black, Asian or from another minority ethnic background, as these groups are currently under-represented at Alzheimer's Society. We want everyone we work with, as a colleague, volunteer, supporter, or someone we support, to feel included and that they belong at Alzheimer's Society. Our Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Strategy here along with our internal employee forum and Employee Lived Experience network groups help us promote inclusion and belonging, becoming an engaged and inclusive organisation for all our people. Our hiring process During your recruitment process we want to make sure that you bring your whole self and can be at your best. We are working hard to ensure our recruitment process is as inclusive as possible, so please do inform us of your experience and anything you think we could do better by completing our candidate survey when you apply. Please also contact Alzheimer's Society Talent Acquisition Team via [email protected] for application support or any adjustments you might need. To ensure fairness and consistency to select the best candidate for this role, all our applications are anonymised up until an interview has been confirmed. We recognise the benefits of AI, but if you're considering using it to submit your application, we encourage you to reflect on the value it truly adds. AI tools often lack the personal touch and authenticity that set candidates apart. We want to hear your unique perspective, experiences, and skills, so we encourage you to showcase them in your own voice. We try to avoid closing roles early where possible, however if we receive a high volume of applications, we may close earlier than the advertised closing date. Should this occur, we will aim to provide you with at least 48 hours' notice. We are committed to safer recruitment and ensuring the welfare of those we work with, due to the nature of some of our roles, we might need to carry out a Criminal Record Check at the relevant level. You can read more information via our Website. Giving back to you Our employees work hard every day to make a true difference in people's lives. We are proud to support them with a range of benefits, recognition and many options for working agilely, all contributing to a strong work life balance. We also have various learning programmes to support you in your development and help you grow to realise your potential and shape a career with Alzheimer's Society. You can also visit our Working for Us pages, which give you more information about what it's like to be an employee at the Society. INDAZ

item.title: Junior Designer
item.description: About The Role There’s a moment, just before something goes out into the world, when everything clicks into place. The message is clear, the design feels right, and you know it’s going to connect with someone who needs it. At Alzheimer’s Society, those moments matter. Every piece of creative work helps people affected by dementia feel seen, supported and understood. As a Junior Designer, you’ll play a part in making that happen. Working within our Creative team, you’ll help turn ideas into thoughtful, well-crafted design across digital and print. From campaign visuals to everyday assets, your work will help bring our brand to life in a way that is consistent, accessible and meaningful. You’ll collaborate with designers, content specialists and digital colleagues, learning as you go and building your skills in a supportive, fast-paced environment where your work has real impact. What you’ll do In this role, you’ll spend your time bringing ideas to life through thoughtful, well-crafted design. You’ll work across a mix of digital and print, creating and adapting assets that help communicate important messages and support impactful campaigns. You’ll take creative concepts and shape them into clear, engaging visuals that feel consistent, on brand and accessible to a wide range of audiences. Whether you’re refining layouts, resizing assets or preparing files for delivery, you’ll care about getting the details right. Working closely with colleagues across creative, content and digital teams, you’ll help make sure design supports the bigger picture. You’ll be part of conversations, contribute ideas and collaborate to deliver work that lands well and makes a difference. Alongside this, you’ll manage your own workload, keeping projects moving and maintaining quality even when things are busy. At a glance, you will: - Create and adapt design across digital and print, from social content to campaign materials - Prepare and deliver artwork that meets brand, accessibility and quality standards - Collaborate with colleagues to ensure creative supports wider campaigns and activity - Manage multiple projects and deadlines, staying organised and focused About you You’re someone who cares about the details, but also understands how they fit into the bigger picture. You’re motivated, organised and ready to grow, with a natural ability to keep things moving even when things get busy. You’ll likely bring: - A strong eye for detail and pride in producing accurate, high-quality work - Good project and time management skills, with the ability to prioritise and meet deadlines - Confidence managing more than one task at a time, and knowing how to refocus when priorities shift - A proactive, self-starting approach, taking ownership of your work while knowing when to ask for support - The ability to build positive working relationships with a range of people - Confidence explaining creative ideas in a clear and accessible way, especially to non-design colleagues You care about inclusive design and understand that how something looks is only part of the story. You think about how it’s experienced, making sure your work is clear, accessible and relevant to different audiences, including people affected by dementia. We know that great candidates don’t always meet every requirement. If this role interests you and you feel you could make a difference, we’d love to hear from you. Interviews are provisionally scheduled to take place on the 23rd September via MS Teams. About Alzheimer's Society Dementia is the UK's biggest killer. One in three people born in the UK today will develop dementia in their lifetime. At Alzheimer's Society, we're the UK's leading dementia charity and the only one to tackle all aspects of dementia by giving help and hope to people living with dementia today and in the future. We give vital support to people facing the most frightening times of their lives, while also funding groundbreaking research and campaigning to make dementia the priority it should be. Together with our supporters, we're working towards a world where dementia no longer devastates lives. Our values make sure that our focus is clear for the challenges and opportunities ahead and remind us of what we all stand for. Our commitment to Equity, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging We need to ensure the voices around our table better reflect and understand the communities we exist to serve. We strongly encourage individuals to apply who have a disability, impairment or health condition or individuals who identify as Black, Asian or from another minority ethnic background, as these groups are currently under-represented at Alzheimer's Society. We want everyone we work with, as a colleague, volunteer, supporter, or someone we support, to feel included and that they belong at Alzheimer's Society. Our Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Strategy here along with our internal employee forum and Employee Lived Experience network groups help us promote inclusion and belonging, becoming an engaged and inclusive organisation for all our people. Our hiring process During your recruitment process we want to make sure that you bring your whole self and can be at your best. We are working hard to ensure our recruitment process is as inclusive as possible, so please do inform us of your experience and anything you think we could do better by completing our candidate survey when you apply. We want to hear your unique perspective, experiences, and skills, so we encourage you to showcase them in your own voice. We try to avoid closing roles early where possible, however if we receive a high volume of applications, we may close earlier than the advertised closing date. Should this occur, we will aim to provide you with at least 48 hours' notice. We are committed to safer recruitment and ensuring the welfare of those we work with, due to the nature of some of our roles, we might need to carry out a Criminal Record Check at the relevant level. You can read more information via our Website. Giving back to you Our employees work hard every day to make a true difference in people's lives. We are proud to support them with a range of benefits, recognition and many options for working agilely, all contributing to a strong work life balance. We also have various learning programmes to support you in your development and help you grow to realise your potential and shape a career with Alzheimer's Society. You can also visit our Working for Us pages, which give you more information about what it's like to be an employee at the Society.

item.title: Venue and Commercial Manager
item.description: Lead our landmark Engine Shed venue and shape unforgettable experiences at the heart of student life. Bring creativity, commercial drive, and operational excellence to one of Northampton’s most iconic spaces. Northampton Students’ Union is searching for an exceptional Venue & Commercial Manager to take the reins of The Engine Shed—our beautifully restored Grade II listed railway building and the beating heart of Waterside Campus. This is a rare opportunity to lead a venue that blends historic character with modern capability, delivering vibrant student events, standout commercial functions, and unforgettable experiences for our community. By day, The Engine Shed is a welcoming social hub where students meet, collaborate, and create memories. By night—and throughout the year—it transforms into a distinctive destination for live events, corporate functions, weddings, conferences, and community celebrations. We’re looking for someone who can harness this potential, driving both operational excellence and commercial growth while championing inclusivity, sustainability, and outstanding service. As Venue & Commercial Manager, you will lead the operational, creative, and commercial development of the venue. You’ll oversee daily operations across the Bar & Café, conferencing, and events, ensuring every aspect of the venue is safe, compliant, welcoming, and running at peak performance. You’ll line‑manage a diverse team—including the Deputy Venue Manager, Caterer, casual staff, and security—creating a positive, collaborative culture where staff thrive and students feel supported. You’ll be the driving force behind our events programme, coordinating everything from student socials to corporate conferences and weddings. You’ll work closely with clients to understand their vision, delivering bespoke, high‑quality experiences that set The Engine Shed apart. You’ll also lead on developing new income streams, crafting business plans, and presenting performance reports to the Commercial Strategy Meeting. Commercial acumen is key. You’ll manage budgets, monitor financial performance, refine pricing strategies, and ensure strong cost control. You’ll also oversee stock management, purchasing, and cash handling, ensuring compliance with SU financial procedures. Your ability to interpret data—tracking conversion metrics from web clicks to confirmed bookings—will help maximise the venue’s commercial potential. Collaboration is central to this role. You’ll work with the Marketing & Communications team to deliver compelling campaigns, build relationships with local businesses and community partners, and champion The Engine Shed’s sustainability credentials. You’ll also work closely with University Estates, Campus Services, elected officers, and SU leadership to ensure the venue continues to evolve in line with student needs and organisational strategy. As the designated Premises Supervisor, you’ll ensure full compliance with the Licensing Act 2003, conduct regular risk assessments, and lead staff training on health and safety and emergency protocols. If you’re an experienced venue operator with creativity, commercial instinct, and a passion for delivering exceptional experiences, we’d love to hear from you. Join us and help shape the next chapter of The Engine Shed—where community, innovation, and unforgettable moments come together.
item.dc:creator: Northampton Students' Union

item.title: Inclusion and Diversity Manager
item.description: Inclusion and Diversity Manager House of Lords – Inclusion and Diversity Team, Human Resources BELONG HERE. TOGETHER, WE MAKE PARLIAMENT HAPPEN. As an Inclusion and Diversity Manager in the House of Lords, you’ll play an important role in supporting the UK’s parliamentary democracy. Your work will help Members and colleagues carry out their responsibilities effectively — contributing to something bigger than any one role. You’ll be part of a collaborative community, working alongside colleagues from a wide range of professions. Together, we make Parliament happen. You’ll be based on the Parliamentary Estate in Westminster — a unique working environment shaped by history and powered by the people who work here today. What you’ll be doing In this role, you’ll: Contribute to a dynamic, high-performing Inclusion and Diversity team that supports the Administration’s value of inclusivity and executes initiatives that deliver on organisational inclusion priorities. Support a range of internal networks and programmes to champion diverse voices in the House of Lords and contribute to a positive workplace culture. Advise and guide colleagues to access the support they need to thrive in the workplace. Work with other functions in HR to draft guidance and policies that support an inclusive working environment and encourages inclusive leadership. What we’re looking for We’re looking for someone who can bring their skills and experience to make a meaningful contribution here. You’ll have: An interest in the House of Lords – Demonstrable interest in and commitment to the role of the House of Lords in parliamentary democracy. Experience with inclusion and diversity – Specialist knowledge and experience working in an inclusion and diversity function, including experience delivering measurable improvements through inclusion and diversity initiatives. Proficiency in strategic working – Experience contributing to and executing initiatives related to strategic objectives. The ability to assess the effectiveness of initiatives and adapt them to meet strategic aims. Competency in project management – Demonstrable ability to independently manage projects and programmes, including their design, delivery, and review to quality, time and budget, alongside “business as usual” and reactive work. It would be even better if you have (or are willing to learn) the: Stakeholder management skills – Proven ability to build effective working relationships with a wider range of stakeholders, including team members, senior leaders, and colleagues from different backgrounds. Ability to problem solve – High level of initiative and adaptability, including the ability to pick up work on short notice, offering resolutions and advice on inclusion and diversity-related issues. Ability to act with professionalism, tact and discretion – Demonstrable competence in managing sensitive issues tactfully and in alignment with the House of Lords Impartiality Guidance, representing the team with professionalism. For full details, please see the job description. What you’ll get in return Working at the House of Lords means joining a community that values your wellbeing, growth and contribution. You’ll benefit from: 30 days annual leave (rising to 35 after one year) Generous Civil Service pension scheme A comprehensive Parliamentary health and wellbeing programme Access to a wide range of learning and development opportunities across diverse professions The chance to witness democracy in action and work in a place of historic national significance The work we do is vital to the House of Lords — the second chamber of the UK Parliament. It plays a critical role in making laws, scrutinising government, and providing independent expertise on national issues. Ready to apply? If you’re looking for an employer where you can belong, grow and thrive, we’d love to hear from you. Please complete your online application by 23:59 on 8 September 2026. We recommend that your application answers do not exceed 300 words.

item.title: COMMUNITY PROJECTS WORKER (OASIS NORTH BRISTOL)
item.description: COMMUNITY PROJECTS WORKER OASIS NORTH BRISTOL HOURS: 8 HOURS PER WEEK (0.2FTE) CONTRACT: 12 MONTH FIXED TERM CONTRACT (Extension dependent on funding) SALARY: £5,673.80 per annum (FTE £28,369 pa for 1FTE) Want to develop, coordinate and manage a food insecurity and community cohesion project offering a diverse range of activities and support for the local community? Want to enable families and local residents to thrive? Want to lead a dynamic, passionate and impactful team of volunteers? Oasis’ vision is for community, a place where everyone is included, making a contribution and reaching their God-given potential. We have an exciting opportunity for a Community Projects Worker to join Oasis North Bristol. Our Community Projects Worker will work with families and residents across the community to develop positive activities and services which promote a sense of belonging and help break the cycle of disadvantage. We’re looking for an individual who has a passion for supporting families and adults, and developing community led activities. The role will involve supporting families and adults in the community, but also families in our local Oasis academies, inspiring and enabling local people to be an active voice and developer in their local area. Key responsibilities include: · To work with the Youth & Community Lead and other team members/partners as required to create and implement a strategy and vision for our food insecurity work. · Ensuring effective financial management and income generation to sustain and expand services · Managing and growing a team of volunteers, ensuring alignment with Oasis’ ethos and values. · Building strong partnerships with local stakeholders to support the delivery of impactful community projects. · Work directly with families and the wider community in a non-judgemental way empowering them and their families to get the most out of the opportunities available. · Create opportunities for families and the community to get involved in shaping and delivering the work of the community projects. · Developing and maintaining monitoring and evaluation frameworks to demonstrate the impact of activities. · Ensure compliance with health and safety, safeguarding, and other statutory requirements. The successful post holder must have: · Excellent organisational and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build positive working relationships. · Good standard of basic education, including English and Maths Level 2 · Proven experience of community work as a volunteer or professionally · Experience of managing and working with volunteers · Ability to build long lasting, positive relationships with both young people and adults · A commitment to the Oasis ethos and values, including inclusion, equality, and perseverance. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of a growing national organisation, making a real difference to communities on a local level. As part of the package, Oasis offers: As part of the package, Oasis offers: · A pension scheme, offering 7% employer contribution. · A generous holiday allowance, starting at 25 days per year (plus 8 Bank Holidays). · Policies which promote well-being and are family friendly. To apply, please send your CV and a Supporting Statement (no more than two A4 pages). Please expand on your CV to tell us about relevant skills, experience and qualification you have, that relate to the job description and person specification. Completed applications should be returned by 9am Wednesday 23rd September 2026. Interviews will take place Thursday 1st October 2026 . W e actively encourage applications from people of all ethnic backgrounds and underrepresented groups. If you require any assistance to overcome potential barriers during the recruitment process, please let us know. We appreciate you may wish to use AI to support elements of your application but we strongly encourage all candidates to submit applications that genuinely reflect their own skills, achievements and lived experiences. It's what makes your application stand out! Oasis is committed to making a difference to the lives of the communities it works in, and as such you must show a willingness to demonstrate commitment to the values and behaviours which flow from the Oasis ethos. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. We expect all staff to share this commitment and to undergo appropriate checks, including enhanced DBS checks. The successful candidates must have the right to work in the UK. Oasis cannot assist with sponsorship or visas. Oasis supports Equal Opportunities. Registered Charity No. 1163889

item.title: Campaigner - Rapid Response (FTC)
item.description: Amnesty International UK (AIUK) has a simple aim: an end to human rights abuses. Independent, international and influential, we campaign for justice, fairness, freedom and truth wherever they are denied. If you want to use your skills, knowledge, and experience to help fight for human rights, you could be our new Campaigner - Rapid Response. About the role At AIUK, the Campaigns and Political Relations team helps us achieve our goal of bringing an end to human rights abuses by working alongside individuals and communities to build a sustained movement to defend and promote human rights both in the UK and globally. The Campaigner - Rapid Response is accountable for running and assisting on projects and campaigns within our Human Rights Crises programme, focusing on areas including armed conflict, protecting multilateral and international justice mechanisms and other foreign affairs issues. Working with the Campaign Manager they will oversee discreet projects and initiatives as well as playing a key supporting role in the development and delivery of this work, including engaging parliamentarians and organising in key local areas to support localised campaigns. Occasional travel to London will be required for in-person meetings. More details can be found by downloading the job description from our careers portal. The role may be for you if: You're organised and skilled in project management to deliver campaign activities, such as events, communications outputs or local organising and have knowledge of how to bring about change. You are a good communicator and can build effective relationships. You collaborate and positively contribute to an inclusive culture. You can write, edit and develop compelling materials. You also have a good knowledge of UK foreign affairs and political processes. Our Commitment to you Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Anti-Racism (IDEA) are at the core of our values. We want to be an organisation that tackles structural inequality and prejudice as well as be an actively anti-racist organisation. This means taking a meaningful and equitable approach to supporting and developing you and others during your time with us. New colleagues receive 27 days leave annually (29 after five years), as well as bank holidays (pro rated for part time) and 3 wellbeing days. 2-5% employee pension contributions are matched at 6-9% and we offer 6 months full pay for family leave. We offer flexible working such as compressed work patterns and job shares. Apply for this role This vacancy advert may be taken down from job boards earlier than the stated deadline if a high standard of applications is received (if you have started an application in our portal, you will still have opportunity to complete it by the original deadline). We welcome applications from everyone and particularly encourage applications from people from an ethnic minority background, and people with a disability to help us achieve a balanced representation in our workforce, especially at senior grades. To reduce bias in our shortlisting process, AIUK operates an anonymised application process. If for any reason you prefer to apply in a different format, or require adjustments in the process, please get in touch. To support all candidates to perform their best at interview, we send interview questions in advance. We are a disability confident organisation. Visit our jobs page for application guidance and information on benefits, recruitment inclusion and hybrid working.

item.title: Rehoming Centre Manager
item.description: Rehoming Centre Manager Beagle Welfare is looking for an experienced, compassionate and highly organised Rehoming Centre Manager to lead the daily operation of our Rehoming Centre, based in Burton-on-Trent. This is a rewarding opportunity to make a visible difference to the lives of beagles, adopters, volunteers and colleagues by creating a centre where excellent welfare, effective rehabilitation and successful rehoming are at the heart of everything we do. As the lead on site, you will manage and develop staff and volunteers, oversee safe and efficient centre operations, and help ensure every beagle in our care receives the right support to progress towards a happy, secure future. You will also represent Beagle Welfare externally and contribute to the continued development of our rehoming work across the UK. About the role You will be responsible for the leadership, performance and smooth running of the Rehoming Centre, including staff and volunteer management, health and safety, site maintenance and the implementation of operational procedures. With rehoming at the centre of your decision-making, you will use data, strong people leadership and sound operational judgement to help improve outcomes for beagles and the people who care for and adopt them. Key responsibilities · Lead, motivate and develop a committed team of staff and volunteers, creating a positive, inclusive and high-performing culture. · Oversee day-to-day centre operations, ensuring high standards of dog welfare, customer service, health and safety, security and compliance. · Drive rehoming activity by supporting case progression, promoting beagles effectively and helping minimise the time beagles spend in our care. · Manage resources, reporting and administrative processes accurately and responsibly. · Build productive relationships with adopters, visitors, animal welfare organisations, and community partners. · Use data, feedback and quality assurance processes to identify improvements and support consistent application of procedures. About you We are looking for a confident manager with experience leading diverse teams, delivering against targets and managing a varied operational workload. You will be comfortable working around dogs, including beagles with different welfare and behavioural needs, and able to balance compassion with practical decision-making. Strong communication, organisation, collaboration and stakeholder management skills are essential, as is experience in supporting continuous improvement. You will also need a UK manual driving licence and be comfortable driving our van. Experience in a kennel or animal welfare environment would be advantageous, but above all you will share Beagle Welfare’s commitment to improving the lives of beagles and supporting the people who care for them. Working pattern and location This role is based at the Rehoming Centre and offers employment that includes employer provided accommodation (3-bedroom cottage) as part of the compensation package. The centre operates between 08:30 and 17:00 every day of the year, so weekend and bank holiday working will be required on a rota basis. Why join Beagle Welfare? You will join an organisation driven by purpose, teamwork and a shared commitment to dog welfare. This is a hands-on leadership role where your decisions, energy and care will directly support better outcomes for beagles, adopters, volunteers and colleagues.

item.title: Senior Campaign Manager (Trusts and Foundations)
item.description: Prospectus is delighted to be supporting a London health charity in the search for a new Senior Campaign Manager (Trusts and Foundations) to join their dynamic fundraising department. This charity supports the 17,000 staff and 2 million patients of the Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust, across Barnet, Chase Farm, North Mid and Royal Free hospitals, plus over 30 NHS services. The Royal Free Charity is now preparing for an ambitious £50million fundraising campaign in support of a ground-breaking £100million cancer centre. As the Senior Campaign Manager, you will lead on developing and implementing a comprehensive Trusts & Foundations strategy to secure six- and seven-figure gifts in support of the Join the Future Capital Campaign for the new Cancer Centre. This role will identify, cultivate, and steward relationships with Trusts and Foundations to secure income in line with campaign targets. With the support of the wider philanthropy team, the Head of Philanthropy and Campaign, as well as support from a Prospect Research team, this role will be a pivotal role in the campaign's success. To be successful within this Senior Campaign Manager role, you will have proven experience of securing income from trusts and foundations. You will have examples of securing six- or seven-figure gifts, and ideally have capital campaign knowledge and experience. Collaborating with various stakeholders internally and externally, this person will also be a good communicator and able to build strong long-term relationships. At Prospectus, we invest in your journey as a candidate and are committed to supporting you with your application. We welcome all candidates to apply, regardless of age, sex/gender, disability, race, religion, sexual orientation, marital status or pregnancy/maternity. If you have any disability and require reasonable adjustment/s to any part of the process then please contact Rhiannon Mehta at Prospectus. In order to apply, please submit an up-to-date CV and cover letter (max 2 pages) in the first instance. Should your experience be suitable, we will arrange for a meeting to brief you on the role. You'll then have all the information you need to formally apply.

item.title: Community Fundraising Executive
item.description: Join a respected charity at a pivotal time and help grow vital community income across the North Midlands and Scotland. This is a hands-on role for a motivated fundraiser who enjoys building relationships, delivering events, and providing outstanding supporter care. Working on a hybrid basis with two days per week in Sheffield, you’ll play a key part in connecting local communities with a cause that makes a tangible difference. About the Role: You will lead and coordinate community fundraising activity across the North Midlands and Scotland, driving income through events, challenges and supporter-led initiatives. Working closely with local supporters, groups and partners, you will ensure every interaction is well-managed, recorded and maximised for long-term engagement. This temporary role will have a direct impact on the charity’s ability to fund services and reach more people in need. Key Responsibilities: * Plan, deliver and evaluate a calendar of community fundraising events and activities across the North Midlands and Scotland. * Support, steward and motivate individual fundraisers, community groups and corporate supporters to maximise their fundraising potential. * Manage and update the CRM and donor database to ensure accurate recording of supporter interactions, income and event activity. * Coordinate logistics for community events, including venues, materials, volunteer support and risk assessments. * Develop tailored fundraising materials and communications to engage and retain community supporters. * Provide timely, high-quality supporter care, responding to enquiries and ensuring a positive experience at every touchpoint. * Monitor income and activity performance, producing regular reports and insights to inform future planning. * Collaborate with internal teams to align community fundraising with wider campaigns and brand messaging. Key Requirements: * Proven experience in community fundraising or a closely related fundraising role. * Demonstrable track record in planning, managing and delivering fundraising events and activities. * Strong CRM and donor database management skills, with experience of maintaining accurate records and generating reports. * Excellent relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage and motivate a wide range of supporters. * Strong organisational and time-management abilities, capable of managing multiple projects across a wide geographic area. * High standard of written and verbal communication, with confident presentation skills. * Ability to work on a hybrid basis with two days per week in Sheffield and travel across the North Midlands and Scotland as required. * Comfortable working to income targets and deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Desirable Skills: * Experience working within a charity or non-profit fundraising team. * Familiarity with fundraising regulations and best practice in supporter care. * Experience of virtual or hybrid fundraising events and digital engagement. * Knowledge of the North Midlands and Scotland fundraising landscape and local networks. * Competence in using email marketing tools or basic design software to create supporter communications. Qualifications: * Educated to degree level or equivalent experience in fundraising, marketing, events or a related field. * Formal fundraising training or certification (e.g. Institute of Fundraising) preferred. * Evidence of ongoing professional development in fundraising, events or supporter engagement. If you are a proactive community fundraiser ready to make an immediate impact in a temporary role, we’d welcome your application. Join us and help strengthen community support across the North Midlands and Scotland. essential criteria on the person specification and clearly provide as much information as possible with examples to demonstrate how and where you meet the criteria.

item.title: Fundraising Manager
item.description: Reports to : Chief Executive Officer, working closely with the Programmes Lead and Finance & Governance Lead. Hours : We anticipate appointing this role as a 2 days per week (0.4 FTE) employee. However, we are also open to hearing from experienced freelance fundraising professionals who are interested in delivering an agreed programme of work on a consultancy basis, equivalent to approximately one day per week. Salary : Employee: £27,000–£31,000 FTE (£10,800–£12,400 pro rata for 2 days/16 hours per week), depending on experience. Consultancy: Day rate to be agreed, depending on experience and scope of work. Location : Remote, with approximately two consecutive days per month at our office in Liverpool and occasional travel for meetings or events. Contract: 24 month fixed term (with the intention to extend, subject to funding). Probation Period: 3 months Line Management: This role has no line management responsibility. About Worldwide Radiology Worldwide Radiology is a UK registered charity working to improve access to high-quality diagnostic imaging in low- and middle-income countries. Working alongside hospitals, universities and health partners around the world, we develop practical, sustainable solutions that strengthen radiology services and improve patient care. Much of our work is delivered through a global network of volunteers and long-term partnerships. We're at an exciting stage in our development. Over recent years our fundraising income has grown significantly, but we're now looking to broaden and strengthen our funding base so we can increase our impact. This new role offers the opportunity to become Worldwide Radiology's dedicated fundraising lead, helping shape the next stage of the organisation's growth. About the Role This is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious fundraiser ready to take the next step in their career and take ownership of fundraising within a growing charity. As Worldwide Radiology's dedicated fundraising professional, you will lead our day-to-day fundraising activity across community fundraising, individual giving and trusts and foundations. You'll be responsible for planning and delivering fundraising campaigns, stewarding donors and writing funding applications that help sustain and grow our work. You'll also support the CEO and Programmes Lead in developing larger strategic partnerships with major funders and corporate partners through research, proposal coordination and pipeline management. Unlike many early-career fundraising roles, this position offers genuine ownership from early on. You'll lead fundraising across your portfolio while working closely with colleagues who have experience securing grants and developing partnerships, giving you the support and mentoring to develop your skills and confidence. While we expect to appoint a Fundraising Manager on a part-time basis, we also recognise that an experienced fundraising consultant may bring a different but equally valuable skillset. We're therefore open to considering either model, provided the successful candidate can take ownership of our fundraising programme and help build the systems, relationships and pipeline needed to support Worldwide Radiology's long-term growth. What Success Looks Like During your first 12–18 months you will: Lead successful delivery of WWR's community fundraising programme, including the Big Give Christmas Challenge and other supporter campaigns. Develop and manage a healthy pipeline of trust and foundation applications. Build strong relationships with our existing donors and funders. Help diversify the organisation's income by developing new fundraising opportunities. Introduce systems and processes that strengthen fundraising as the organisation continues to grow. Key Responsibilities Fundraising (Lead) You will take ownership of WWR's fundraising activity across your portfolio, working closely with the CEO while leading delivery day-to-day. Responsibilities include: Leading delivery of fundraising across community fundraising, individual giving and smaller trusts and foundations. Researching, writing and submitting grant applications to trusts and foundations. Managing relationships with existing trust funders and individual donors, including stewardship and reporting. Planning and delivering community fundraising campaigns, supporter events and online fundraising activities, including the Big Give Christmas Challenge and JustGiving campaigns. Developing opportunities to grow our supporter base and increase donor retention. Maintaining accurate fundraising records, donor data and reporting. Monitoring fundraising activity and providing regular updates to the CEO. Supporting the development of fundraising plans and identifying new income opportunities. Partnerships (Support) Working alongside the CEO and Programmes Lead, you will: Research prospective major trusts, foundations and corporate partners. Prepare briefing papers and background research ahead of meetings. Coordinate development of larger funding proposals by gathering information, managing timelines and tracking actions. Maintain the strategic funding pipeline and prospect tracker. Support follow-up from meetings, conferences and partnership discussions. Help identify opportunities to strengthen relationships with healthcare organisations, companies and strategic partners. Person Specification We recognise that no candidate will meet every criterion. If you can demonstrate most of the following, we'd love to hear from you: Experience in a fundraising, development or partnerships role within the charity sector. Experience researching and writing, or supporting the development of, funding applications to trusts and foundations. Excellent written communication skills with the ability to write compelling funding applications and supporter communications. Excellent relationship-building skills, with experience working positively with supporters, volunteers, partners or external stakeholders. Strong organisational skills, with the ability to maintain accurate records and manage information across multiple projects and deadlines. Comfortable working in a digital, remote environment and confident learning new systems, including fundraising CRM platforms. Enthusiasm for Worldwide Radiology's mission and the role of global health partnerships. Desirable attributes: Experience delivering community fundraising campaigns or challenge events. Experience using fundraising CRMs or donor databases. Experience of the Big Give Christmas Challenge or similar match-funding campaigns. Experience supporting corporate partnerships or major donor fundraising. An interest in global health, healthcare or international development. Why Join Worldwide Radiology? This is a rare opportunity to take ownership of fundraising within a growing international charity at an early stage in your career. You'll have the chance to lead fundraising campaigns, develop relationships with donors and funders, and shape how fundraising grows over the coming years. At the same time, you'll benefit from the guidance and support of experienced colleagues, giving you the opportunity to develop your skills while making a tangible contribution to improving access to diagnostic imaging around the world. We're committed to supporting your professional development through mentoring, networking opportunities and relevant fundraising training, helping you build the skills and experience to progress your fundraising career. We offer: Flexible remote working. A collaborative, supportive team with minimal hierarchy. Opportunities for professional development and responsibility. Up to 4% matched pension contribution. 25 days Annual leave plus 8 public holidays (pro rata).
