item.title: Quality Assurance Manager - Maternity Cover
item.description: REPORTING TO: Director of Front-line Services PURPOSE OF POSITION The Quality Assurance Manager is a blended leadership role combining strategic quality assurance, performance oversight, service management and practice development. The role is split broadly between focused on quality assurance, data-led improvement and performance oversight, and two days focused on service management, practice leadership and frontline improvement activity. The postholder will lead the development and delivery of a strong quality assurance framework across support services, ensuring that practice, performance and service delivery are safe, effective, person-centred and aligned with contractual, regulatory and organisational standards. Alongside this, the postholder will remain closely connected to frontline delivery through service management responsibilities and practice development leadership, particularly within Housing First and complex-needs services. This makes the role ideal for someone who enjoys combining strategic oversight, data insight, operational leadership and the development of high-quality, trauma-informed support practice. What makes this role different A distinctive role for someone who wants strategic influence while staying close to frontline practice. You will help shape quality, use evidence, support staff, strengthen resident outcomes and join an organisation committed to compassion, collaboration, inclusion, growth, learning and resident voice. Enjoy variety and influence work across performance oversight, service management and practice development, with scope to shape systems, standards and ways of working. RESPONSIBILITIES & ACCOUNTABILITIES Key Responsibilities Quality assurance and improvement: Lead the quality assurance function across support services, coordinating audits, quality checks, case file reviews, service reviews and improvement plans. Turn findings into practical actions that strengthen safety, consistency, resident experience, safeguarding, support planning and trauma-informed practice. Work with managers to embed learning, monitor progress and evidence improvement against internal and external standards. Performance oversight and reporting: Monitor performance against contractual, regulatory and organisational standards, including service outcomes, compliance requirements, safeguarding expectations and commissioner reporting. Identify risks, gaps, trends and good practice, escalating concerns and supporting corrective action where needed. Produce clear, evidence-based reports and briefings for senior leaders, governance meetings, commissioners and external stakeholders. Data, insight and systems: Use performance, safeguarding, complaints, incidents, resident feedback, outcomes and quality data to identify service strengths, pressures and improvement priorities. Maintain and improve reporting systems, including InForm, so information is accurate, consistent and useful. Analyse patterns, support decision-making and make practical recommendations that improve quality, accountability and resident outcomes. Information retrieval and STAIRs requests: Act as QA Manager lead for information retrieval relating to STAIRs requests, including triaging scope, gathering internal and contractor records, coordinating redaction and drafting responses within regulatory timeframes. Service and support management: Provide hands-on support management across frontline services, including Housing First improvement activity, Hope Street and St Mungo’s contracts, team rota management and the Support Manager on-call rota. Support managers and teams to manage risk, strengthen case accountability and recording, and deliver consistent, high-quality support to residents with complex needs. Practice development: Embed person-centred, trauma-informed and psychologically informed practice across support services. Develop practical tools, guidance, quality forums, workshops and reflective learning that help staff apply policy, improve support planning, strengthen safeguarding and promote consistent resident-centred practice. Resident voice and accountability: Strengthen resident engagement, feedback and involvement so resident experience informs service design, quality assurance, learning and improvement. People management and collaboration: Line manage agreed roles, including the Impact Specialist and Resident Engagement Specialist, supporting clear objectives, accountability, development and collaborative working across services. General duties: Attend key directorate, management, planning, quality and performance meetings; work flexibly across organisational priorities; and undertake other reasonable duties within the scope of the role. PERSON SPECIFICATION Assessment will be through application, interview and, where relevant, a practical assessment Quality assurance: Experience delivering quality frameworks, audits, case file reviews, standards and improvement plans that strengthen safe, consistent, person-centred and trauma-informed practice. Able to lead improvement activity, influence managers and turn findings into sustained service change. Performance and reporting: Able to monitor contractual, regulatory and organisational standards; identify risks, gaps, trends and good practice; and produce clear reports for leaders, governance forums and commissioners. Data, insight and systems: Strong analytical skills and confidence using performance, safeguarding, complaints, incidents, outcomes and resident feedback data to identify patterns, support decisions and improve services. Experience using resident feedback, consultation or involvement activity to inform quality assurance, service design and improvement, including through InForm or similar systems. Information governance: Understands confidentiality, record handling and information governance. Able to triage STAIRs requests, gather internal/contractor records, support redaction and draft timely responses. Support management and practice: Experience supporting people experiencing homelessness or rough sleeping with complex needs. Able to support managers, manage risk, strengthen recording and embed person-centred, trauma-informed, psychologically informed and anti-discriminatory practice. Safeguarding and risk: Sound knowledge of adult safeguarding, risk assessment, MARAC processes and safe information sharing with vulnerable adults. Communication and values: Strong written, verbal and facilitation skills; collaborative, organised, accurate and resilient, with commitment to compassion, collaboration, inclusion and growth. Appointment is subject to DBS check and right to work in the UK

item.title: Brand and Content Producer
item.description: Grade: 4 Salary: £37,321 per annum Hours: Full-time 37.5 hours per week (flexible working considered) Position type: Permanent Responsible to: Senior Brand Manager Direct reports: None Location: ShelterBox HQ, Truro, Cornwall or Remote (UK only) Travel: Ability to work away from home required. This may be UK (we expect up to 6 visits to Truro HQ per year) or an in-country deployment in a content gathering or representing ShelterBox role. ROLE PURPOSE: As part of in an in-house brand and creative team this role will help plan, shoot, create and oversee the production of quality audience-led graphic design and multi-media content under the ShelterBox brand. Working with the Senior Brand Manager and wider Brand and Content team, the successful candidate will deliver end-to-end projects to bring the brand alive and support our fundraising, communications and international teams to drive income, awareness and support successful user journeys. The role will advise all ShelterBox teams to work within brand guidelines and enable teams to access and use assets and templates by maintaining accurate systems. They will also support wider development of a purpose-led brand, using insight and by building strong relationships with audience and channel owners. WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? Are you looking to join an in-house Brand and Content team? This role would suit someone who's keen to work across all areas of the organisation, championing brand guidelines and managing and delivering a wide range of creative projects under the ShelterBox brand. You must be able to edit video and have a good knowledge graphic design and brand. It is a requirement of this role to have a working knowledge of Premier Pro, After Effects, Indesign and Illustrator, with experience across Adobe Creative Suite. You'll also be able to demonstrate great copywriting skills and have excellent attention to detail. The successful candidate will have experience in practical photography and film. You will need to be able to plan and lead a shoot and confidently pick up a camera and capture ShelterBox footage and interviews in the UK and in the countries where we work. This role will, at times, be required to deploy in both major disasters and pro-active content trips - gathering content themselves and supporting external freelancers. MAIN ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Within this role you will be a great relationship builder working across a wide range of ShelterBox teams, external agencies, partners and freelancers. A strategic thinker - able to work on multiple long and short project deadlines and prioritise to objectives. Driven by audience needs - whether that's optimising creative in response to Digital Marketing data and insight or getting under the skin of key strategic funders to make the right content at the right time to drive objectives. Experienced in working across fundraising and communications channels for both warm and cold audiences to drive income and awareness. We arelooking for a creative talent who can get to the core of ShelterBox's mission whilst remaining up to date with the detail, picking up new ideas and concepts easily. You'll understand the power of story in fundraising and communications, be self-motivated, with a can-do approach and be flexible in supporting the wider team. DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: Brand: Support and train the wider organisation to effectively create content within ShelterBox brand guidelines Support the continued development of an online brand hub Support the development of a purpose led brand. Help to develop and implement a brand strategy. Help drive brand and values led storytelling across the organisation driven priority audiences Position ethical storytelling as a central thread of the ShelterBox brand Creative and content development: Manage creative projects for key ShelterBox teams working across multi-media disciplines including video, scriptwriting and graphic design. Lead projects from creative brief stage through to asset delivery including all production. Responsible for core projects split across the team including warm and cold supporter journeys, evergreen and explainer content for digital optimisation, celebrity videos, philanthropy and partnerships, Rotary. Support the digital marketing strategy. Responsible for creating asset sets for Always On and time-framed campaigns. Work to tight deadlines and respond to agency and internal feedback to continually optimise creative. Support ShelterBox to develop our in-house creative approach. Facilitate workshops and creative exercises to ensure we create objective and audience led products. Support a review of design across the organisation and enable teams to design via templates. Support the development and re-fresh of templates for both design and video. Work with external agencies, freelancers and partners. Use audience insights to inform all plans and work with the insight team and others to measure success. Ensure all projects follow sign-off processes Content gathering: Plan and lead shoots in the UK and in countries where ShelterBox works. Film a wide range of ShelterBox spokespeople including CEO, board members, programme staff, partners and high-level celebrity supporters both at an in-house studio or on location. Photograph and film events in the UK and overseas. Shoot and manage a bank of studio photography of ShelterBox aid items - responding to audience insight and channel requirements. Develop and deliver quality content training for ShelterBox staff Help to manage ShelterBox photography, sound and video equipment and studio Work closely with the ShelterBox operations team and partners to ensure we are gathering high-quality content across all our live deployments. Process and edit raw content from deployments - case studies, photos, video. Deploy to gather content or train partners - dependent on funding and strategic need. At times this may involve taking freelancers on agreed trips. Note: Deploying in major disasters or to partner organisations may involve operating within ERA areas so role will need to be HEAT trained. Interview and film communities affected by disaster Gather content to ShelterBox ethical guidelines. Planning and team working Be an integral part of team planning Offer knowledge of best practice and innovations from other organisations and sectors. Support a measurement-based approach by contributing to monthly reporting as well as spotting trends and opportunities. Any other specific projects given by the Senior Brand manager. Please note: We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. We therefore encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. Please ensure your application is completed in full and you read the applicant guidance on our website before applying.

item.title: Senior Manager of Employee Engagement (Corporate Volunteering)
item.description: Contract Type: Fixed Term until 31st March 2030 Location: Any UK Trust office - 40-60% of the week spent in the office and an expectation to travel when required Interviews: 24/09 and 25/09 over MS Teams We are looking for an ambitious and commercially minded Senior Manager to lead the launch and delivery of a flagship corporate volunteering and fundraising campaign for The King’s Trust. This fully funded role runs until March 2030 and offers the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to a major employability programme supporting young people across the UK. This high-profile role sits at the heart of our corporate partnerships’ strategy, driving both employee engagement and income growth across a portfolio of valued partners. The income generated through this campaign will help fund a bold new initiative at The King’s Trust; one that will inspire businesses, communities, and volunteers to come together and support young people to thrive. You will work closely with corporate stakeholders to build strong relationships, unlock opportunities, and create compelling campaigns that inspire employees to take action and maximise impact. Working alongside the Head of Corporate Volunteering, you will lead planning and execution, bringing together internal teams, corporate partners, and external stakeholders to deliver seamless, engaging experiences. From developing innovative engagement strategies and managing communications, to overseeing events, budgets, and performance reporting, you will ensure every aspect of the campaign delivers against commercial objectives, generates income, and supports organisational goals. A key part of the role will be identifying and pitching new ideas, initiatives and engagement opportunities to corporate partners, helping them deepen their involvement and achieve their own social impact ambitions. You'll work closely with the Corporate Partnerships team, providing creative solutions, campaign expertise and strategic support to help unlock new fundraising, volunteering and partnership growth opportunities across their portfolios. This is a fast-paced, highly collaborative role for someone who combines strong commercial acumen with exceptional relationship-building skills. You'll be comfortable influencing senior stakeholders, spotting opportunities for growth, developing compelling propositions, and bringing diverse teams together to deliver ambitious targets. If you're energised by creating meaningful partnerships, driving measurable results, and delivering campaigns that make a lasting difference, we'd love to hear from you. What happens next? Please submit a CV, and Cover Letter that includes your experience, transferrable skills and motivation to work for The King's Trust! The Team will be in touch about the next steps shortly after the closing date. Why do we need Senior Managers of Employee Engagement? Last year, we helped more than 40,000 Young People, with three in four young people on our programmes moving into a positive outcome in work, education or training.The young people we help face a range of challenges, such as unemployment, mental health issues or some who have been in trouble with the law. We believe all young people should have the chance to succeed, and that young people are the key to a positive and prosperous future for all of us. We want to continue having a positive impact on young people’s lives, and we couldn’t do this without the important work of the Senior Managers! Perks for working at The Trust! Great holiday package! 30 days annual leave entitlement, plus bank holidays. Office closure on the days between Christmas and New Year Flexible working! Where operationally possible, our roles require a combination of office days and working from home (please speak to the hiring manager about this particular role) You can volunteer for and/or attend events – The King's Trust Awards, Pride, active events, etc. In-house learning platform! Develop your skills for your career and your role Benefits platform! Everything from health and financial well-being support to discounts on your favourite restaurants, shops and cinemas. Personal development opportunities through our Networks – KT CAN (Cultural Awareness Network), KT GEN (Gender Equality Network), KT DAWN (Disability & Wellbeing Network), and PULSE (LGBTQIA+ Network). Fantastic Family leave! Receive 13 weeks of full pay and 13 weeks of half pay for maternity and adoption leave. Receive 8 weeks of full pay for paternity leave. Interest-free season ticket loans The Trust will contribute 5% of your salary to the Trust Pension Scheme Generous life assurance cover (4 x annual salary)

item.title: Head of Fundraising
item.description: Job description The Wave Project is the UK’s leading Surf Therapy charity, a pioneer in using surfing as a form of therapy. As a multi award winning charity we pride ourselves on delivering a big impact with a small, committed team of 35 staff and 1,400 wonderful volunteers. In 2025, we supported over 2,600 children and young people to improve their confidence, self-esteem, resilience and social skills. The Head of Fundraising is a key member of the charity’s Senior Leadership Team and provides strategic leadership and operational oversight across all fundraising activities, ensuring sustainable income growth and enhancing The Wave Project’s visibility and impact. The role is critical to fostering a strong supporter base, developing innovative campaigns, and cultivating partnerships that align with the charity’s mission of transforming young lives through Surf Therapy. They will lead a small, talented team and will also work closely with our delivery team across the country, who are an essential part of our fundraising efforts. Please read the full job description and apply via our website. item.title: South West Regional Manager
item.description: Job description We're looking for a Regional Manager to provide tactical and operational leadership across a portfolio of The Wave Project delivery locations in the South West, ensuring children and young people receive safe, high-quality and consistent Surf Therapy services. Rather than delivering programmes directly, the Regional Manager enables high-performance through effective management, coaching and development of Project Coordinators, with accountability for safeguarding, quality assurance, finance, partnerships and local/regional fundraising. The role plays a key part in increasing organisational capacity by providing visible and effective regional leadership and improvements, enabling senior Operational leadership to focus on strategic priorities across the charity. Work closely with the Head of Operations and colleagues across Fundraising, Finance, Marketing and Research & Impact to support organisational sustainability and strategic ambitions. item.title: Interim Director of Fundraising
item.description: Harris Hill is seeking an interim Director of Fundraising for around 10 weeks, working 3 days per week, with one in the office, based in London. The role can either be paid via the agency on a day rate of £257.69 (£67k), on contract via the charity, or potential consultancy day rate where you charge the client direct. About the Role: As Interim Director of Fundraising, you will provide strategic direction and hands-on leadership across all fundraising activities, ensuring income targets are met and future growth is supported. You will oversee major gifts, corporate partnerships, grants, and individual giving, using data-driven insight to optimise performance. Operating on a hybrid basis, you will maintain continuity, enhance donor relationships, and prepare the function for a smooth handover to the incoming permanent Director. Key Responsibilities: * Lead the development and implementation of a short-term strategic fundraising plan to maintain and grow income during the interim period. * Oversee major gifts and philanthropy programmes, including managing key donor relationships and supporting high-value cultivation and stewardship. * Direct corporate fundraising activity, including pipeline management, proposal development, and relationship building with corporate partners. * Provide line management and leadership to the fundraising team, setting clear priorities, offering guidance, and ensuring accountability for targets. * Review and optimise fundraising data, reporting, and performance dashboards to inform decision-making and improve campaign effectiveness. * Oversee grant fundraising and management, including identifying opportunities, approving high-quality applications, and ensuring compliance with funder requirements. * Strengthen donor relationship management processes and systems to enhance retention, upgrade opportunities, and supporter engagement. * Prepare and deliver clear, timely income and activity reports to senior leadership, highlighting risks, opportunities, and recommended actions. Key Requirements: * Proven track record in senior fundraising leadership, ideally at Head of Fundraising or Director level, within the charity or non-profit sector. * Demonstrable experience in strategic fundraising planning and delivering against ambitious income targets across multiple income streams. * Strong expertise in major gifts and philanthropy, including managing high-value donor relationships and securing significant gifts. * Experience in corporate fundraising, including developing and managing partnerships and sponsorships. * Solid background in grant fundraising and management, including oversight of applications, reporting, and compliance. * Confident user of fundraising data and CRM systems, with the ability to interpret data and produce clear, actionable reports. * Proven team leadership and line management experience, including performance management and staff development. * Ability to operate effectively in a hybrid working environment, with at least one day per week in the London office and two days remote. Desirable Skills: * Experience of leading fundraising functions through periods of transition or organisational change. * Familiarity with UK charity fundraising regulations and best practice frameworks. * Experience in developing or refining donor journeys and supporter engagement strategies. * Background in integrating data insights into campaign planning and segmentation. * Previous experience working with boards or fundraising committees. If you are an experienced fundraising leader available to start quickly and ready to provide strategic stability and impact through to the end of November, we encourage you to apply.

item.title: Fundraising and Supporter Care Coordinator
item.description: Could you be the person who helps make brilliant fundraising happen behind the scenes? Natasha’s Foundation, the food allergy charity, is looking for an experienced, highly organised and personable Fundraising & Supporter Care Coordinator to join our small and ambitious fundraising team. We’re a passionate, energetic and friendly team, united by a determination to make a real difference. We work hard, move quickly and have big ambitions for a small charity – but we also really value the way we work together. Everyone brings something different, ideas are welcomed, people support one another and there’s a genuine sense of excitement about what we can achieve. This is a varied role for someone who loves working with people, takes real pride in getting the detail right and is equally comfortable supporting a donor, working with data or helping a busy fundraising team stay one step ahead. You’ll be at the heart of our fundraising operation: providing warm and thoughtful supporter care, supporting individual giving, helping us make the best use of our Beacon CRM, producing accurate fundraising and income information, and supporting proposals, reports, communications and fundraising resources. We’re looking for someone who is warm, organised, numerate and confident with data, with excellent attention to detail and practical experience of using Beacon CRM. Just as importantly, we’re looking for someone who will enjoy being part of our team – someone positive, proactive and willing to get stuck in. You’ll be joining Natasha’s Foundation at an exciting point in our journey. We are working to improve the lives of people with food allergy through education, campaigning and pioneering medical research, with one hugely ambitious goal: a future without food allergy. If you enjoy making things work brilliantly, care about giving supporters a great experience and want to bring your skills and energy to a charity where your contribution will genuinely be noticed and valued, we’d love to hear from you. 20 hours per week | Home-based | £32,000–£34,000 FTE

item.title: Counselling Outreach Worker
item.description: The Counselling Outreach Worker is key to SEL Mind's exciting new counselling service for Black residents of Southwark, delivered as part of the wider Southwark Wellbeing Hub. This part-time role will shape the Wellbeing Hub's provision to Black communities, expanding equitable access to culturally-appropriate support. As Outreach Worker, you will work closely in partnership with community organisations to ensure relevant, de-colonial approaches, including maintaining a delivery partnership with Black Psychotherapy. The main working site is a community centre in SE5, and the community outreach work involves regular travel across the borough. You will play a vital role in building community trust, ensuring that we are creating routes into the service and continually seeking and implementing feedback. We are seeking a community-based worker who is passionate about improving Black people's access to early mental health support. Relationships and partnership working is vital, so you should be able to work independently but collaboratively, to be proactive and show initiative. The role will involve: Maintaining a live engagement strategy and actively reaching out with physical presence to grassroots organisations, faith groups, community centres, cultural associations, and spaces for people experiencing difficult situations including e.g. food banks and advice/advocacy organisations Contributing to the development and continuous improvement of the service, bringing recommendations to support the SWH's inclusivity and best practice This role involves providing culturally specific support to Black clients. Applicants must be able to demonstrate lived experience of, and deep cultural understanding within, Black communities, and the ability to build trust with Black service users. Successful applicants will be expected to undergo an Enhanced Level Disclosure and Barring Service check. Closing date: Sunday 13th September (11:59pm) Likely interview date: Week beginning 28th September We encourage early applications as we reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high number of applications. About Us SEL Mind supports people with mental health problems and dementia in the boroughs of Bromley, Greenwich, Lambeth, Lewisham and Southwark. We are proud of our diverse workforce and know that our organisation is made stronger by the variety of backgrounds, experience, and ideas within it. We promote a culture of inclusion and representation, and are working hard to build a workforce that even better reflects the communities we support. SEL Mind is somewhere that you can be your authentic self without fear of discrimination on the grounds of ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, neurodivergence, gender, age, lived experience of mental health problems or anything else that’s part of who you are. Read more about staff benefits and why staff love working here on our website.

item.title: Parkinson's Local Adviser (Reading, Wokingham & West Berkshire)
item.description: Job description Locations: Reading, Wokingham & West Berkshire About the role Working as part of a regional team, you’ll champion Parkinson’s UK in your local community by building and sustaining relationships with a diverse network of health and social care professionals, clinics, and community groups. You’ll provide a personalised service that empowers people affected by Parkinson's, their families, and carers, to live fulfilling lives and become their own advocates in health and life wherever possible. You’ll manage a complex caseload of multiple clients simultaneously, expertly balancing needs-led support with immediate priorities like crisis intervention and end-to-end safeguarding in partnership with local services. What you'll do Provide in-depth, person-centred information, guidance, and emotional and advocacy support to empower clients with health, social care, and welfare issues Assist clients to identify needs against benefit criteria, navigate complex processes, and provide practical support via a range of channels, including home visits and community settings Respond to enquiries through a range of channels and areas based on service need, managing an active client caseload while keeping accurate, up-to-date online client records in line with practice guidelines Recognise and respond to potential safeguarding situations using established procedures Answer client enquiries professionally using a jargon-free approach and within established timescales What you'll bring Background and/or experience of providing health and social care information through a range of channels Well-developed communication skills including active listening and questioning Experience of supporting and empowering people with problem solving, navigating the health and social care system and participating in their own care Demonstrable digital competence, with experience of effective use of a range of tools including online case management systems or similar Live in the area specified by the role with the ability to travel and work flexibly without reliance on public transport Please apply by sending us your CV and a detailed cover letter explaining how you meet the criteria in the "What you'll bring" section of the job description on our website. Interviews for this role will be held online on 24 September 2026. Successful candidates will be invited to attend an in-person interview on 29 September 2026 in our London office. item.title: Freelance Trainers
item.description: Are you an experienced training facilitator? Can you support and deliver sessions to a wide range of professionals on how to best work alongside young women and girls affected by criminal exploitation and violence? Do you want to work for a values-led charity that centres young women’s voices? Abianda is a London-based charity that works with young women and girls affected by criminal exploitation and violence, and the professionals who support them. We exist to ensure young women are no longer hidden in our communities and can live free from harm and abuse. We aim to bring about a culture shift in how services are delivered to young women and girls, so that they can access support that works for them when they need it. We are seeking experienced, reflective and values-driven freelance trainers to support the delivery of high-quality training for professionals working with young women and girls affected by criminal exploitation and violence. This role is ideal for someone who is confident in participatory facilitation, committed to trauma-informed and intersectional practice, and able to work collaboratively. The role will involve facilitating sessions in person and online and may require overnight travel and stays. If you have experience delivering training and want to use your facilitation skills to improve professionals' understanding of young women and girls, we'd love to hear from you! “The trainers know how to hold a room well. Excellent knowledge and experience and interaction. Every session has been informative and enjoyable - the time passes so quickly!” - Abianda Training Participant, 2026 Role details: Freelance, sessional contract Day rate between £220 and £300, depending on support or lead delivery and experience Reporting to Abianda’s Training and Development Lead Please read the full job description attached. To apply , please send your CV and supporting statement (no longer than two A4 pages), detailing why you want to work with Abianda and how you meet the person specification via CharityJob. If you would prefer, you can submit your application via video or voice recording (no longer than 3 minutes) or a PowerPoint presentation (no longer than 5 slides). Please also download and our equal opportunities form (this is optional). The deadline for applications is 9am Thursday 10 September . First stage online interviews will be held the week commencing 21 September. Second stage in-person interviews will be held the week commencing 28 September. If you are invited to join the team, you must be available on 13 and 15 October for onboarding sessions. You must also be available for two out of the four following training delivery dates: 3, 11, 17 and 24 November. All applicants are requested to complete a criminal record self-disclosure form at interview stage. We value the lived experience of our applicants and all disclosures will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. Applicants must share a basic DBS certificate before starting work with Abianda. Please note Due to the work we do, Abianda's roles are subject to an Occupational Requirement on the grounds of the protected characteristic of sex. We are a women’s-only employer, and as such, this position is exempt under Schedule 9 of the Equality Act 2010. We particularly welcome applications from Black and Brown people, people of the global majority, disabled people, the LGBTQ+ community and people from different socio-economic and educational backgrounds. We encourage applications from people from all walks of life, including those who may have had exposure to similar experiences that young women across London are facing.

item.title: Independent Mental Health Advocate (IMHA) – West Sussex
item.description: Mind in Brighton and Hove empowers and supports people who have experience of mental health issues in Brighton and Hove and West Sussex. Our Advocacy Services take action to help people say what they want, secure their rights, represent their interests, and obtain services they need. We are seeking to appoint an Independent Mental Health Advocate (IMHA) in West Sussex. The role will be based at Langley Green Hospital in Crawley, with regular travel to other acute and forensic wards in West Sussex, such as Meadowfield, Priory and St Magnus. Occasional visits to Brighton head office for meetings and training. This role involves providing Independent Mental Health Advocacy, working within the framework of the Mental Health Act 1983 to support people to understand their rights under the Act and participate in decisions about their care and treatment across the area of West Sussex. The post requires an understanding of advocacy, experience of managing a client case load, excellent communication skills and the ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with a range of professionals, whilst retaining independence. Hours: Part-time, 28 hours per week. In return, we offer a range of benefits including full induction, nationally accredited advocacy qualification and 29 days’ leave (pro rata) per year excluding bank holidays, 3% pension contribution and access to a 24-hour Employee Assistance Programme. Closing date: 9am on Monday 14th September 2026. Interviews will take place on Tuesday 22nd September 2026 in central Brighton. Alternative interview dates can be arranged if required. We are committed to equal opportunities, and we value diversity in our workforce and aim to recruit a workforce that reflects the communities we serve. We encourage applications from everyone irrespective of age, disability (including experience of living with mental health issues), gender reassignment, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, marriage and civil partnership and pregnancy and maternity.

item.title: Energy Adviser
item.description: Energy Adviser Location : Doncaster (Office based) Salary : £27,000 per annum Hours : 37 hours per week worked over 4 days (08:00-18:00) Contract : Fixed Term until 31 October 2028 (2 years) Closing Date : 18/09/26 Help people tackle fuel poverty and improve financial resilience This role will deliver specialist energy advice and casework to residents experiencing fuel poverty, energy debt and complex energy-related problems. Working as part of a dedicated team, you will support some of Doncaster's most vulnerable households and help them achieve sustainable outcomes. About the role You'll provide in-depth energy advice and casework to clients whose circumstances require investigation, advocacy, negotiation and ongoing support. You will work directly with energy suppliers, represent clients where appropriate and help resolve complex issues including billing disputes, affordability concerns and energy debt. The role will include telephone appointments, video appointments, face-to-face appointments and occasional outreach/home visit activity. Key responsibilities Deliver specialist energy advice and in-depth casework. Conduct full assessments of client circumstances and energy needs. Investigate complex billing issues and supplier disputes. Support clients experiencing energy debt or self-disconnection risks. Negotiate with suppliers and other agencies on behalf of clients. Develop practical solutions to improve affordability and energy resilience. Maintain accurate client records and outcome reporting. Work collaboratively with colleagues and partner organisations. Contribute to achieving project targets and outcomes. About you We are looking for someone who: Has experience delivering advice, casework or advocacy services. Can manage complex cases and competing priorities. Has excellent communication and negotiation skills. Is able to work independently and take ownership of client outcomes. Has strong organisational and record-keeping skills. Is committed to empowering people and tackling inequality. Shares the values and principles of Citizens Advice. Desirable Experience of energy advice, debt advice, welfare benefits or housing advice. Understanding of fuel poverty and vulnerability within energy markets. Experience negotiating with utility providers or creditors. City & Guilds Level 3 Energy Awareness qualification, or willingness to achieve this during induction. What we offer Comprehensive training and supervision. Opportunity to develop specialist energy advice skills. Access to nationally recognised qualifications. Supportive team environment. The opportunity to make a lasting difference to vulnerable households across Doncaster. About Citizens Advice Doncaster Borough Citizens Advice Doncaster Borough provides free, confidential, impartial and independent advice to help people overcome the problems they face. Through the Energy Advice Anytime project, we are expanding access to energy advice through innovative and flexible delivery models to reach more residents, reduce fuel poverty and improve financial resilience across our communities. Citizens Advice Doncaster Borough values diversity, promotes equality and challenges discrimination. We welcome applications from all sections of the community.

item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: Chief Executive Officer London/Hybrid | 4 days a week (28 hours per week) £80,000 FTE Two-Year Fixed-Term Contract Our client is a respected UK-wide professional membership body representing more than 3,000 practitioners. Through advocacy, professional development, research and member support, the organisation champions professional standards and works to increase access to high-quality services across its sector. The organisation is seeking an exceptional leader to serve as its next Chief Executive on a two-year fixed-term contract , leading the organisation through a significant period of transformation, stabilisation and renewal. Working closely with the Board, staff, members and key stakeholders, the successful candidate will provide the strategic and operational leadership required to strengthen organisational effectiveness, enhance financial sustainability, build an engaged and high-performing culture, and position the organisation for long-term success. This is a unique opportunity to make a lasting impact on a well-established membership body, ensuring it emerges stronger, more resilient and better equipped to deliver for its members and wider stakeholders. As the organisation's senior executive and principal ambassador, you will lead the development and implementation of a clear transformation roadmap, strengthen organisational capability and governance, and build confidence across the membership and stakeholder community while championing the value and impact of the profession. To be successful, you will bring: Significant senior leadership experience as a Chief Executive, Executive Director or equivalent. A proven track record of leading organisational transformation, change, stabilisation or turnaround programmes. Experience developing and implementing strategy, translating vision into sustainable organisational improvement and measurable outcomes. Strong financial, operational and governance leadership skills, with experience improving organisational resilience and sustainability. item.title: Welfare Officer - RAF Leeming
item.description: About the role Our Welfare Officers provide direct and impactful welfare support to RAF personnel and their immediate family. As a trusted and confidential source of support, you will assist our service users with challenges they are facing, from mental ill-health, difficult relationships, domestic abuse, financial and cost-of-living concerns, resettlement, housing, childcare, equality issues, bereavement, military discharge or deployment and many more - no day will be the same, as such this is a great opportunity to develop your knowledge and skills within the Welfare sector. Our intervention is provided with consent on a non-statutory basis, and you will work with and engage our service users to develop appropriate interventions for individual outcomes. Our service is transitioning to become more accessible and inclusive, digital technology plays a key role in this, as such you will use digital technologies to complement and enhance processes and service user experience and as part of your role will be expected to provide virtual support to other teams and the Digital Welfare Hub. You will play an active role within the RAF community, promoting the service through the delivery of presentations and representing the service at public engagement events. You will also work closely with RAF welfare teams, local authorities, health, education, civilian agencies, charities and other military organisations to ensure the best outcome for the service user. About the Team 2025 marked 35 years since SSAFA began delivering an independent non-statutory, and confidential service, for the Royal Air Force community across the UK, and this is an exciting time to be joining as we were successful in our bid to continue delivering this service. We are continuously transforming our ways of working to be innovative, to ensure our service is even more inclusive and accessible to meet the needs of a modern RAF. We are a hard-working team from diverse professional backgrounds. Although we all have our own area of responsibility, we support each other in delivering the best possible service to our military community. Find out more about the Personal Support & Social Work Service on our website. About you To thrive in this role you will have relevant experience of supporting adults, families and children/young people. You will be able to take a flexible and creative approach to problem solving. You will have excellent communication skills and be able to deliver presentations with confidence. You will have used Microsoft Office 365 to a high standard. It is important that you have experience of planning and managing your own workload, with minimal supervision. It would be advantageous if you have experience of carrying out assessments, preparing plans, monitoring and reviewing outcomes. At RAF Leeming you will be part of a 2-person team which is part of a wider team across the region. But there will be times when you will be working alone. There will be some travel required and therefore you will need to be able to drive and have access to your own car. About SSAFA SSAFA, the Armed Forces charity is a trusted source of support for the Armed Forces community in their time of need. In 2025 our trained teams of volunteers and employees helped more than 53,000 people, including veterans, serving personnel (regulars and reserves) and their families. SSAFA understands that behind every uniform is a person. And we are here for that person and their family, any time they need us and in any way they need us. Diversity and Inclusion at SSAFA SSAFA exists to support a diverse range of beneficiaries within the armed forces community, and we believe diversity within our teams is key to ensuring we can deliver our services effectively. We thrive on differences and believe it is critical to our success as a worldwide charity. SSAFA is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace that seeks to recruit, develop and retain the most talented people from a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We therefore encourage applications from all genders, races, religions, ages and sexual orientations, as well as parents, veterans, people living with disabilities, and any other groups that could bring diverse perspectives to our business. SSAFA is committed to using the Disclosure & Barring Service to ensure we, as an employer, safeguard those we serve. Closing date: Midnight on Thursday 13 September 2026. SSAFA reserves the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications. Interviews: 24 and 25 September 2026

item.title: Social Prescribing Link Worker
item.description: Citizens Advice Milton Keynes is a local charity that helps people to resolve their legal, money and personal problems. We have been providing free, confidential, and impartial advice since 1972 and helped over 8000 local people last year. We are looking for an enthusiastic, reliable and confident person to join us in delivering a new project based in local GP Surgeries. The ideal candidate will provide a Social Prescribing Link Worker service, to patients of Ascent Primary Care Network (Ascent PCN) in Milton Keynes, working to support patients and staff at each of their 3 medical centres across the area. The Link Worker will take referrals from the PCN’s practices, and from a wide range of external agencies, and through self-referrals. They’ll work with people to identify issues that affect their health and wellbeing and co-produce a simple personalised care and support plan that connects them to non-medical community-based activities, groups and services that meet practical, social, and emotional needs. This is a challenging role, managing a demanding caseload, working to strict quality standards and playing a full part in multi-disciplinary team of health and social care professionals. Successful candidates will be able to ensure that all work is compliant with our contract funder – Ascent PCN, and Citizens Advice standards. Applicants need to be: Computer-literate, although training on our case recording systems will be given. Able to travel between each of the 3 surgeries in Milton Keynes. Confident in working to performance targets. Able to show good communications skills, both written and verbal. These are essential in the role, as are excellent customer service skills with a non-judgemental approach. Prepared to work independently and from a variety of community-based locations. A minimum of 12 months’ experience in a social prescribing role or an agency providing advice, support and signposting (or similar setting) is desirable. The successful Applicant/s will be asked to undergo an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. Closing date: Sunday 20th September 2026

item.title: Macmillan Project Caseworker
item.description: Citizens Advice Milton Keynes is a local charity that helps people to resolve their legal, money and personal problems. We have been providing free, confidential, and impartial advice since 1972 and helped over 8000 local people last year. As a Specialist Adviser within the Macmillan Money & More SWS Service, you will provide high-quality, confidential information, advice and support to people affected by cancer and their families across a region spanning from Milton Keynes to Cornwall. Working as part of a coordinated team of advisers across multiple Citizens Advice locations, you will take a person-centred approach to understand each client’s individual circumstances and provide tailored guidance on welfare benefits, financial support, debt, energy costs, employment issues and other practical challenges arising from a cancer diagnosis. You will help clients navigate complex systems, access available support, and improve their financial wellbeing during a difficult and often overwhelming time. Through compassionate and holistic advice, you will empower people affected by cancer to make informed decisions, build confidence, and feel supported throughout their cancer journey. The ideal candidate will provide advice and support in person, via telephone, email and video call to patients undergoing treatment for cancer. Macmillan Project Caseworkers will assist clients with complex welfare benefits and housing enquiries. This requires a good foundation knowledge of each advice area, so competence in these subjects is desirable, but full and ongoing training will be provided to support successful candidates in their professional development. This is a challenging role, managing a demanding caseload and working with people at every stage of their cancer journey. All our advice work is carried out to the strictest quality standards, and we are committed to ensuring that all our advice work complements the wider services provided by both Citizens Advice and Macmillan Cancer Care. Applicants need to be: Computer-literate, although training on our case recording systems will be given. Confident in working to performance targets. Able to show good communications skills, both written and verbal. These are essential in the role, as are excellent customer service skills with a non-judgemental approach. Prepared to work independently, sometimes remotely and also from a variety of community-based locations. A minimum of 12 months’ experience in an advice agency or similar setting is desirable. The successful Applicant/s will be asked to undergo an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. Closing date: Sunday 20th September 2026

item.title: Brand & Content Manager
item.description: This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who can combine strategic thinking with hands-on creativity to help shape how Phoenix Futures communicates with the people we support, our colleagues, partners and wider audiences. We’re looking for someone with significant experience in brand management, content and communications who can bring ideas to life across digital, print and internal channels. You’ll be passionate about creating engaging, accessible and impactful content, while ensuring our brand is consistently represented across everything we do. The Role As Brand and Content Manager , you will lead the development and delivery of Phoenix Futures’ brand, content and communications channels. Working closely with colleagues across the organisation, you’ll lead the creation of high-quality digital, print and creative communications, while managing and developing key platforms including SharePoint, our websites, social media channels and Phoenix News. You’ll be the organisation’s brand guardian and a key source of advice and expertise on brand, content, visual communications and creative best practice. You’ll help ensure that our communications are engaging, accessible, user-focused and aligned with our organisational priorities. You’ll also lead on content planning and editorial management, internal communications, creative storytelling and digital experience development. Using analytics, audience insight and feedback, you’ll identify opportunities to improve how we communicate and ensure our content reaches and engages the people who need it. The role will involve working with senior stakeholders, external suppliers, agencies and creative partners, managing projects, budgets and deadlines to deliver high-quality campaigns and communications. This is a 37.5 hour per week role, based on a hybrid London and home-working arrangement . About You To join us as our Brand and Content Manager , you will need: Significant experience in brand management and leading strategic content and communications across digital, print and internal communication channels Strong graphic design and content production skills, with experience using Adobe Creative Suite (InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop) or equivalent Experience developing and improving websites, SharePoint environments and digital communication platforms A strong understanding of user experience, accessibility, SEO, content optimisation and digital analytics Experience of content planning, editorial management and delivering communications across multiple channels Experience creating and managing internal communications and employee engagement content Experience managing external suppliers, agencies and creative partners to deliver high-quality communications and design projects Strong analytical skills, with the ability to use performance data and audience insight to evaluate content and drive continuous improvement Excellent project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders and deadlines Excellent written communication, editing and proofreading skills, with a high level of literacy and attention to detail Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills, including the confidence to work with senior leaders The ability to work independently, use sound judgement and take ownership of brand and communications activity A commitment to the values, mission and recovery-focused approach of Phoenix Futures Experience of photography, video production, animation or multimedia storytelling would also be desirable, as would a professional qualification in Graphic Design. If you’re a creative, strategic and organised communications professional looking for a role where your work can make a genuine difference, we’d love to hear from you. Your Rewards Starting salary of £35,500 + London weighting contribution of £500, with the opportunity to access potential yearly salary increments subject to appraisal, meaning potential salary increase up to £41,000 Committed to providing a Real Living Wage for you, through accreditation with the Living Wage Foundation 25 days’ annual leave plus Bank Holidays, increasing each year to a maximum of 30 days Benefits including season ticket loan, pension scheme and life assurance Support through occupational sick pay, eye-care vouchers and regular wellbeing talks and activities Continuous training and career development via PXL, our dedicated learning management system Access to a 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme, including telephone and online access A rewarding role where you can use your creativity, expertise and ideas to help us communicate our work and challenge stigma around drug and alcohol use We’ll ensure you get the support you need to thrive and succeed in your role and find your place amongst our incredible and collaborative team The Role The Marketing team plays a key role in helping Phoenix Futures communicate its work, raise awareness, challenge stigma and connect people with our services and support. As Brand and Content Manager, you’ll work across the organisation, collaborating with colleagues at all levels to develop engaging and effective communications. You’ll work particularly closely with senior stakeholders and teams across Phoenix to understand their communication needs and turn ideas and objectives into clear, compelling content. You’ll be part of a passionate and collaborative Marketing team, with the opportunity to influence how Phoenix Futures’ brand and communications develop across the organisation. The role is based on a hybrid London and home-working arrangement, with opportunities to work collaboratively with colleagues across Phoenix Futures. About Phoenix Futures Phoenix Futures Group is a charity with over 50 years’ experience and a leading provider of drug and alcohol treatment. We use our expertise to support people in their personal recovery and to improve their lives. We are dedicated to advocating for people who are often overlooked and stigmatised, to ensure they have a fair chance to lead healthy and fulfilling lives. Our aim is for everyone to be able to achieve their potential for themselves, their families and communities. We encourage and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and believe it is important to include people with lived experience to ensure the needs of the people we support are represented. We are committed to creating an inclusive working environment where everyone is free to be themselves and we ensure equity of opportunity. Our managers and leaders are guided by a shared set of qualities that shape how we work with colleagues, partners and the people we support. These are: BRAVE, HONEST, VISIBLE, VISIONARY, NURTURING and COLLABORATIVE . These qualities underpin our approach to inclusive leadership, accountability and compassionate practice across Phoenix Futures and support the development of a value-aligned culture. Interview Process We want you to feel comfortable to be your best during the interview process, so that you can get to know Phoenix and we can get to know you. If shortlisted, you will be contacted for a short digital interview via Microsoft Teams, approximately week commencing 14th September , and will be provided with full details about the assessment process. As part of the selection process, candidates will be asked to present their portfolio of work demonstrating their relevant skills, experience and impact. All details will be provided in advance so that you can feel adequately prepared and we can support you with reasonable adjustments as required. Please note, we will be assessing applications as they are submitted and may close this role should we find sufficient applicants with which to make our shortlist. As such, we would advise applying as soon as possible to avoid disappointment.
item.dc:creator: Phoenix Futures, SE1

item.title: Services Manager (Maternity cover)
item.description: Job title: Services Manager (Maternity Cover) Salary: £44,558 – £45,895 Hours: Full-time 37.5 hours per week (part time or flexible working options considered) Location: Home-based ideally Wales or Midlands area, but any location will be considered, with travel around England and Wales Contract: Fixed term – 9 months from December 2026 Are you an experienced employability service manager who would be able to confidently step into a 9-month maternity cover position and oversee a team of up to eight passionate and person-centred Employment Consultants, helping them deliver personalised, high-quality support to veterans and their families? You will also have the opportunity to contribute to our services development and continual improvement programme. At The Poppy Factory, we believe that everyone who has served our country deserves the opportunity to build a fulfilling life beyond the armed forces. For over a century, we have stood alongside veterans and their families, evolving our services to support veterans and adult family members to overcome barriers to employment and transform their lives. What we're looking for A collaborative mindset: You will thrive working as part of a team with colleagues based across the UK who support each other in what can sometimes be a challenging role. You enjoy building strong partnerships, and work effectively with colleagues and external organisations to enhance the services we offer. Motivation and commitment: You understand that supporting people facing complex challenges can be demanding, and you're ready to bring the energy, empathy and resilience needed to support your team to succeed. Adaptability: You will often need to balance competing priorities or quickly shift focus depending on the needs of the team you will be supporting and the clients they are working with. An empowering approach: You believe in people and their potential. Whether supervising your team or developing services, your goal is to support others to grow, achieve and thrive. Why should you apply? A chance to make a lasting impact: Your work will help veterans and their families move forward in life with confidence and dignity. Competitive salary and benefits including generous holiday and pension contributions. A welcoming and empowering culture , with regular opportunities for team connecting and shared learning throughout the year. Flexibility and variety: a mix of travelling in your area, home working and to the Poppy Factory in Richmond, London Autonomy and influence: The opportunity to shape your region, build meaningful partnerships, and develop services that meet real needs. Be part of an iconic charity with over a century of history supporting the Armed Forces community. For further information, including the full job description for the role, please refer to the candidate pack. Due to the travel requirements of the role and the region covered, it is essential that the post holder is able to meet these requirements through their own transport arrangements. How to apply To apply for this position please click "Apply for this job" to submit your CV and a covering letter outlining how you meet the essential criteria in the person specification. Please address your covering letter to Debbie Boughtflower, Director of Operations. Top tip: we don't recommend using AI to generate your covering letter (we've seen a lot of covering letters and we promise, we can tell!) - we want to know what makes YOU a good fit for the role, and AI covering letters can't capture your personality, values and qualities, or what makes your specific combination of skills and experience an ideal candidate. The closing date for applications will be 23 September 2026. Please note, we cannot accept late or incomplete applications. Only applications submitted through the online process will be considered. Online interviews will be held on 1 or 2 October 2026, with potential second interviews on 12 October 2026 in person @ The Poppy Factory in Richmond, London. To arrange an informal conversation about the role, please contact Kirsty Gronow No agencies please. The successful candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check.
item.dc:creator: The Poppy Factory, Newport

item.title: Head of Communications: Maternity Cover
item.description: Job Title: Head of Communications: Maternity Cover Location: London/Hybrid 2 days a week in office Salary: £70,700.00 per annum Weekly Hours: 35 Reference: YMC1231934 About Us Founded in 1844, YMCA is a global movement and the world's largest youth-focused charity. In England and Wales, YMCAs are based in over 700 communities across168 local authorities supporting young people and communities to reach their potential. The turnover of YMCA in 2025-26 was £386m. YMCA England & Wales is a £23 million organisation of more than 400 colleagues, supporting a Federation of 80 local YMCAs to deliver vital services which positively impact young lives across the country. As we enter 2027, a year of significant impact in our mission, we seek a Head of Communications for maternity cover. The opportunity As Head of Communications, you'll lead YMCA England & Wales' communications and reputation strategy, growing our influence, visibility and impact across England and Wales. You'll be responsible for leading the delivery of an integrated communications strategy that strengthens our reputation, supports organisational priorities, amplifies the voices and experiences of young people, and positions YMCA as a leading voice on the issues that matter most to young people and communities. Working closely with the Senior Leadership Team, local YMCAs and external stakeholders, you'll oversee YMCA England & Wales’ media relations, collaborative public affairs and campaign communications, digital communications, content development, brand amplification, event delivery, internal communications, and crisis communications. As part of the Leadership Team, you'll work collaboratively across departments to help deliver our strategic goals. Day to day, you'll provide expert communications counsel to senior leaders and trustees, protect and grow our brand and reputation, lead integrated campaigns that support our influencing objectives, and turn research and insight into compelling public narratives. You'll also lead our approach to crisis communications and issues management. You'll manage a high-performing communications team, alongside the budget for that team, and help strengthen communications capability across the wider YMCA Federation. About You You're an experienced, strategic communications leader who can operate confidently at senior and board level, translating organisational priorities into clear, compelling communications plans. You'll have a strong track record in brand awareness building, reputation management and media relations, and an instinct for storytelling that builds engagement and trust. You're calm and decisive under pressure, with proven experience leading crisis and issues communications. You know how to lead, motivate and develop a team, manage budgets effectively, and build strong relationships across a complex, federated organisation. Above all, you're passionate about YMCA's mission and committed to championing equality, diversity, inclusion and safeguarding in everything you do. Our recruitment process is anonymised and candidates' names are hidden. We welcome and encourage job applications from people of all backgrounds. Safer recruitment is important to us and the successful applicant will be asked to provide two references. They will also be required to complete a safeguarding self-declaration, safeguarding training and undertake a DBS check.
item.dc:creator: YMCA England and Wales

item.title: Local Campaigns Officer - London
item.description: Job description About the role You’ll lead and coordinate our local campaigning work across London. Your work will help the charity improve the lives of people in local communities affected by Parkinson’s. You'll listen to the needs of our local communities and work with colleagues in our wider directorate to do focussed political campaigning work and advocacy. Your work will help raise awareness and increase knowledge about Parkinson’s. Through your campaigns you’ll ensure that the voices of people with Parkinson’s, their families and carers are heard. What you'll do Be a first point of contact for supporters and campaigners in the local area,who want to improve services in their local area. Provide expert advice and support to colleagues and campaigners on how best to challenge and influence decision makers. Build close working relationships with our field staff and our local networks. Recruit and manage a sustainable network of local campaign volunteers. Lead campaigns to ensure everyone with Parkinson’s has access to the multidisciplinary team so they can live well with Parkinson’s. What you'll bring Experience of campaigning and an understanding of the basic tools and techniques used in campaigning. Experience of working with volunteers and services users including how best to support them to achieve their campaigning goals. Experience in organising events. Experience of delivering training to volunteers and staff. Ability to network and build supportive relationships with volunteers, MPs and health bodies. Please apply by sending us your CV, together with a detailed cover letter which will fully demonstrate how you meet all the criteria of the role, as stated in the "What you'll bring" section of the job description on our website. Interviews for this role will be held on Friday 25 September, online. Successful candidates will be invited to a second stage interview, held in person at our London Office. Refreshed on: 27 August 2026 Closing date: 13 September 2026 at 23:30 Tags: Advice / Information, Campaigns, Communications, Policy, Training / Learning, Advocacy, Volunteering Management, Customer support, Partnerships, Politics, Events / Activities

item.title: Head of Operations
item.description: Help build the operational backbone of a multi-award winning charity that's ready to grow further, with a clear path to becoming our COO. For seven years, one exceptional leader has held impact, organisational development and much of YUAF's operations, building the processes, funder relationships and team support that became part of the spine of how we grew. As they move on, we're not just replacing them. We're rethinking and widening the role. This post exists to hold the organisation steady and take operational responsibility off the Chief Executive's plate, freeing her to focus on strategy, key donors and the funding pipeline. What you'll hold You'll report to the Chief Executive and sit on the Senior Management Team, owning income generation, impact and evidence, business planning, governance, performance management and the systems underneath them all. You'll line-manage four people: the Pathways Lead, Marketing Lead, Project Manager and Futures Lead. Where the role is going From month seven, this role is intended to move to full time with deeper ownership of income and strategy. As YUAF grows, and subject to income generation, we want this post to develop into our Chief Operating Officer role. We'd rather appoint someone who outgrows this description than someone who fits it exactly. How you'll start The first six months are a settling period at 30 hours per week. You'll learn how the organisation actually works, get embedded in the culture, and understand the programmes by spending real time with young people and the people who deliver them. You'll build relationships across the team, with funders and with partners, and by month three, we want people to naturally come to you as a trusted point of contact. We also want you to look at YUAF with fresh eyes. Where are the gaps? What's held together by one person's memory alone? Where does delivery quality drop, and why? What would make life easier for the staff doing the hardest work? Bring us both the diagnosis and the solutions. The timing is on your side: November to February is our quietest season, when the Studio Bus is largely off the road. Delivery picks up again in March 2027, so the role builds in stages rather than coming to you all at once. How to apply In addition to providing your CV and cover letter, it is a requirement of the application process that you complete our Head of Operations Questionnaire. A link for this can be found on the attached job description. Note We recognise that AI is a useful tool, however, we will be assessing applications, cover letters and running through AI to ensure that it was written by yourself as part of our shortlisting process. So please take the time to write your own application, this is a serious role that requires critical and independent thinking.
item.dc:creator: Young Urban Arts Foundation
