item.title: Advisor (trainee)
item.description: Want to work in a fast-paced environment with opportunities to learn advice skills? Are you a proactive person interested in making a real difference to Disabled people? About the role RAID has 4 main advice areas: Information Navigation, Benefits Advice, Energy Advice and Money Advice. The Cost of Living Crisis has disproportionally impacted Disabled people, who are more likely to face higher living costs, barriers to employment and reduced financial resilience, making it harder to cope with rising household expenses. Many of the people we see are in challenging situations; struggling with debt, experiencing food and fuel poverty, facing homeless and dealing with loneliness and isolation. The work can be emotionally challenging. As well as our advice work we administer a number of grants on behalf of local grant giving charities and the local authority and you will play a key role in helping us to process grants in a timely and efficient way as well as supporting with advice enquiries. Our teams are busier than ever and this role will play a vital part in supporting the team with administration tasks including; processing grants and gathering client evidence, taking client enquiries from the phone, website and email and uploading them to our database, scanning and photocopying. You will spend your time working directly with clients with a range of physical, sensory and mental health impairments to help them to fill in grant allocation forms and other forms and helping people to know their rights. You will also support our advice teams administratively; arranging appointments, sending emails and letters and uploading information to our database You will receive training in a range of advice areas (housing, health and social care, benefits, transport and travel) as well as other relevant topics such as various mental health conditions, managing challenging behaviour, professional boundaries, and case management. You will be supported by a friendly team of experienced advisers who will have the opportunity to shadow and you will also have access to a range of external training and development opportunities. You will need to have clear written and oral communication skills as you will need to make phone calls and write emails and letters to clients as well as providing progress updates to the team. You will work closely with our experienced advice team and we can offer opportunities for training and development in a range of areas including social care, housing and benefits to support you on your journey to becoming and advisor. About you To be successful in this role you will have solid administration and organisational skills, a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail, and a level of emotional resilience that enables you to support people in challenging circumstances, while protecting your own wellbeing. You will have strong communication skills across all levels and will be a real team player with a genuine interest in supporting Disabled people. An interest in developing advice skills in essential and experience or a background in advice and information will be an advantage. You will have excellent communication and IT skills, administrative skills and be fully competent on Microsoft applications. You will have the ability to work independently as well as part of a team. The ideal candidate will be passionate about social justice and the empowerment of Disabled people and excited to learn valuable skills on the job. Disabled Candidates We are an equal opportunities employer and particularly welcome applications from Disabled candidates. We have been awarded the Disability Confident Employer quality mark, meaning any Disabled candidates that meet the minimum criteria will be invited for interview. Please advise if have a disability or long-term health condition that you would like considering when you apply.
item.dc:creator: Richmond Advice and Information on Disability (RAID), TW11

item.title: Young Carers Participation and Co-design Coordinator
item.description: About The Job Contract: Fixed-term, until 31st December 2026. Hours: 17.5 Hours per week (0.5 FTE). Salary: £12,901 - £16,126 (pro rata from £25,802-£32,252) Location: Remote working. Flexibility to work from other Carers Trust’s offices around the UK when needed. The Young Carers Participation and Co-design Coordinator will work collaboratively with young carers, schools, local carer organisations and Network Partners to coordinate and facilitate meaningful young carer participation across the programme. This includes coordinating a national Young Carers Ambassador Group, embedding co-design approaches throughout programme activity, and ensuring young carers’ voices and experiences inform the development of resources, programme delivery and future priorities. This role is central to advancing our mission by amplifying the voices of young carers and ensuring their lived experiences shape the support available to them. By strengthening participation opportunities, fostering collaboration between schools and local carer organisations, and embedding co-design at every stage of the programme, the postholder will help improve understanding of young carers’ needs and experiences. The work will contribute directly to improving educational outcomes and support for young carers, while also generating shared learning and evidence to inform future policy and practice, ensuring young carers’ voices are reflected in services, decisions and opportunities at both local and national levels. As the postholder you will: Facilitate workshops, discussions and feedback sessions with young carers. Regularly review participation activity to impropve quality, accessibility and impact. Support the coordination and tracking of young carer involvement in influencing activity, including ensuring that contributions are captured and fed into reporting. Please download the attached recruitment pack to find out more.
item.dc:creator: Carers Trust

item.title: Finance and Funds Business Partner
item.description: The Finance and Funds Business Partner role is a fantastic opportunity for an individual looking to work for a fast moving, growing organisation. Everything we do is geared to supporting the renowned Christie NHS Foundation Trust to ensure cancer patients receive the highest level of treatment and care and have access to world leading research and technology, ensuring they have the best possible experience. We are looking for a dynamic and enthusiastic self-starter to support the Charity Financial Controller with: - The financial management of the Charity’s funds and individually funded projects; and - The financial control and governance of The Christie Charity group, particularly its two wholly owned subsidiaries (The Christie Trading Company Limited and Northern Pathology Developments Limited). You will be joining The Christie Charity at an exciting time as we seek to diversify the Charity’s income streams through use of innovative social investments and strategic commercial ventures. This position provides an excellent opportunity to develop a deep understanding of charity and commercial finance within a dynamic and purpose-driven organisation. Financial management In relation to the financial management of the Charity’s funds, you will ensure that Individual Named Funds, containing designated funds, are utilised in accordance with their Terms of Reference. In relation to the financial management of individually funded projects, you will monitor spend against budgets through accountability mechanisms agreed with The Christie NHS Foundation Trust finance team. The postholder will be an integral part of the Charity finance team and partake in the annual budget setting process to the extent budgets relate to the Charity’s Individual Named Funds or individually funded projects. As part of your role in the financial management of individually funded projects, you will act a finance business partner to the broader Charity. You will be integral in liaising with the Charity’s newly appointed Grants Manager to ensure they are aware of new projects. Financial control and governance You will play a key role in ensuring robust financial control across the Charity group, with the opportunity to take ownership of its two wholly owned subsidiaries: The Christie Trading Company Limited and Northern Pathology Developments Limited. This is a hands-on role where you will be responsible for overseeing the accuracy and integrity of financial controls and reporting, supporting the Charity’s aim of maintaining strong governance across both charitable and commercial operations. Your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, budget preparation and monitoring, completing month-end close, submitting quarterly tax returns, and preparing the statutory accounts for both subsidiaries, as well as supporting the Charity Financial Controller in maintaining effective financial control and oversight of the Charity's operations as required. Additional information The Finance and Funds Business Partner is a well-established role in the Charity. The successful applicant will be provided on the job training to fulfil this role by the previous postholder who now holds the role of Charity Financial Controller in the organisation. In the immediate term, day-to-day financial transaction processing will continue to be delivered by The Christie NHS Foundation Trust, therefore, the postholder will be expected to work closely and collaboratively with their finance team to ensure seamless operations and continuity across the Charity group. These responsibilities are expected to transition in full to The Christie Charity by 31 December 2026. This post would suit an individual who enjoys working in a dynamic, evolving environment, where responsibilities may shift in response to organisational priorities. The postholder must be comfortable navigating ambiguity, demonstrating flexibility, initiative, and a proactive approach to problem-solving.
item.dc:creator: The Christie Charity

item.title: Finance Officer
item.description: Job description In your role as finance officer, you will work with the Head of Finance to provide finance support and advice to colleagues across the hospice, ensuring we make the most of every penny we raise. Your attention to detail and technical expertise is essential to maintain high standards of financial integrity at the hospice. This is an exciting time to be joining the team as we focus on developing our financial systems and processes, making the most of the technology on offer. As finance officer you will have a key role to play in making these changes. You’ll also be joining a vibrant, committed and driven team who get to see, first-hand, the impact the hospice has on people living in Wigan and Leigh and how we make a difference. Role requierments Support the production of accurate and timely financial information to support effective decision-making across the Hospice Maintain the integrity of financial records through regular review, reconciliationand analysis of financial data Support the production of monthly management accounts, ensuring informationiscomplete, accurate and supported by appropriate documentation. Investigate and resolve financial discrepancies, variances and anomalies, identifying root causes and escalating to the Head of Finance Maintain robust financial controls and ensure compliance with Hospice policies, procedures and regulatory requirements Build effective working relationships with managers and colleagues across the organisation, providing routine finance support and responding to finance-relatedenquiries Contribute to departmental budget monitoring by providing accurate financial information and supporting analysis for the Head of Finance Support the ongoing development of finance systems, digital processes and automation, ensuring financial information remains accurate, reliable and fit for purpose Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, strengthen controls and enhance the effectiveness of the Finance function through continuous improvement initiatives Work collaboratively with Finance colleagues to promote knowledge sharing, resilience and business continuity, supporting a flexible and customer-focusedFinance service Posted on: 28 August 2026 Closing date: 14 September 2026 at 09:00 Tags: Finance, Accounting, Accounts Payable, Data Entry, Health / Medical The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.

item.title: Head of Finance and Risk
item.description: UKCISA is looking for its Head of Finance and Risk as we continue on our exciting journey to long term financial sustainability. As a member of our Senior Leadership Team you will work with a financially astute CEO who together with our team and Trustees is leading the development of our next strategy. That strategy will position us to succeed as a trading entity, earning our revenue from the 400 member organisations from Higher and Further Education, schools and student unions. These organisations value our advocacy to government and our specialist advice, training, conferences and celebrations of international students and their role in supporting them. As the UK’s national advisory body for international students and the professionals who work with them, our purpose is clear: to ensure that every international student has the best possible experience while studying in the UK. This mission is more important than ever. International students currently studying across the UK make an invaluable contribution to our campuses, communities, and society. At the same time, the environment in which they live, and study has become increasingly complex, shaped by shifting government policy, economic pressures, and evolving student expectations. As our Head of Finance and Risk key areas of responsibility are: Playing a leadership and business partner role with colleagues and Trustees Working closely with the CEO to deliver on our financial strategy Delivering the operational financial activities for UKCISA and leading a small finance team to achieve successful audit outcomes Leading on areas of governance including finance, risk, audit, acting as the secretariat for the Finance, Audit and Risk Committee Managing the organisation’s risk management processes and register To be successful in this role you need: A recognised accounting qualification (min Level 4 Diploma in Professional Accounting AAT or equivalent) or chartered accountant status 3- 5 years finance experience in the charity sector producing year end/statutory accounts in accordance with the Charities SORP Experience in reporting to and advising Boards and/or committees Experience in developing finance strategies to drive financial sustainability To be interested in and developing a commitment to UKCISA’s vision and mission To be able to demonstrate excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work as a business partner and advisor with team members and trustees To be able to demonstrate excellent leadership skills to achieve strategic and operational goals To be able to demonstrate excellent analytical and audit skills to lead on risk and business continuity planning To be able to demonstrate high levels of personal and professional integrity If you don’t have all the experience we are seeking but believe you can still excel in the job, do please consider applying once you have read the full information pack. What’s in it for you: Working for a passionate team who have an exceptional reputation for advocacy, advice and guidance to the international student sector Having access to benefits such as professional development funds and leave, an EAP program, USS pension and hybrid flexible working with only a requirement to attend monthly in person all day staff meetings in central London An opportunity to use your finance and risk expertise to support UKCISA’s vision that every international student who comes to the UK has a positive experience and is able to tell friends and families that the UK is a welcoming place to study, and live. To apply for this role download our full information pack on our website, including job description and essential criteria Join our team at UKCISA Please note: CVs alone will not be accepted. You must respond to our three questions in order to be considered. Applications will close on Monday 14 September 9 am In-person interviews will take place at our office in central London on 24 September 2026
item.dc:creator: UKCISA

item.title: Head of Services (Female Applicants Only)
item.description: About the role This is an exciting opportunity to join Women and Girls Network's Senior Leadership Team and lead two of our most impactful service areas: the Intersectional and Anti-Oppressive (IOS) Team and the Criminal Justice and Violence Against Women & Girls (CJS, VAWG) Team. As Head of Services, you will play a vital role in shaping and driving services that support women and girls affected by gender-based violence, ensuring they receive empowering, trauma-informed and culturally responsive support. You will lead with a strong commitment to feminist, anti-racist and anti-oppressive values, ensuring that the voices and experiences of survivors remain at the heart of everything we do. Working closely with the Director of Services and senior colleagues, you will provide strategic leadership across a diverse portfolio of services, strengthening partnerships, influencing systems and championing innovative approaches that remove barriers and improve outcomes for women facing multiple disadvantages. This is a unique opportunity for an experienced leader to make a lasting impact, both within our organisation and across the wider VAWG sector. Job description As the Head of Services, you will: Lead and inspire the IOS and CJS, VAWG teams, providing strategic direction and oversight to ensure services are accessible, high-quality, survivor-centred and aligned with WGN's feminist values and vision. Champion intersectional and anti-oppressive practice, ensuring services are responsive to the diverse experiences of women and girls, particularly those from Black and Global Majority communities and others facing systemic barriers. Drive excellence in service delivery, safeguarding and quality assurance, ensuring robust risk management and compliance while creating environments where survivors can heal, recover and thrive. Lead, support and develop Service Managers, fostering a culture of collaboration, wellbeing, accountability and continuous learning that enables staff to deliver their best work. Build influential partnerships across statutory, voluntary and community sectors, strengthening pathways for survivors and ensuring WGN's expertise informs local, regional and national responses to violence against women and girls. Use insight, evidence and survivor feedback to evaluate impact, drive innovation and shape the future development of services, ensuring they continue to meet emerging need and deliver meaningful change. Represent WGN as a sector leader, advocating for systemic change and helping to create a society where all women and girls can live free from violence, inequality and discrimination. Supporting Statement Guidance Your supporting statement should clearly demonstrate how your experience, knowledge, skills, and qualifications meet the requirements of the role. Please address the key criteria outlined in the Job Description and Person Specification, providing specific examples of achievements and responsibilities that evidence your suitability for the position. Focus on relevant professional experience, transferable skills, and the impact of your work. Where possible, use concise examples to illustrate how you have successfully applied these skills in practice. The supporting statement should be no more than 500 words and should complement, rather than repeat, the information contained in your CV or application form. Closing date and interviews This vacancy will close at 9am on Monday 28 September 2026 . Interviews will take place shortly thereafter, and shortlisted candidates will be notified of the arrangements. We encourage early applications, as we reserve the right to close the vacancy before the advertised closing date should we receive a high volume of applications or identify a suitable candidate. The selection process will consist of two interview stages and a role-related assessment task. Interviews may be conducted either in person or remotely, depending on panel availability and logistical requirements, and may involve a combination of both formats throughout the process. Candidates invited to participate will receive full details of each stage, including the assessment task and interview arrangements, in advance. About us Women and Girls Network (WGN) is a pan-London organisation that supports women and girls affected by all forms of gendered-based violence. Our overall aim is to promote, preserve and restore the mental health and well-being of women and girls who have experienced, or are at risk of, gendered-based violence, whilst working towards a society free of gendered-based violence. We do this by: Providing women-only holistic and seamless therapeutic services, which meet women and girls’ needs and contribute to total and sustainable recovery from the experiences of violence. Evidencing the impact of gendered-based violence and presenting this information in appropriate forums to affect social change in attitudes towards, and responses to, gendered-based violence. Developing good practice in the sector by providing training and guidance on specialist service provision and the development of culturally appropriate service delivery. WGN is proud to be an accredited Living Wage Employer and a member of The London VAWG Consortium, Halo Code, and Helplines Partnership. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion We are deeply committed to building a workforce that reflects the diversity, resilience and strength of the women and girls we serve. We strongly encourage applications from Black and Global Majority women and applicants with Lived Experience, including those who may not meet every criterion. WGN is an equal opportunities employer. Exemption This post is exempt under the Equality Act 2010, Schedule 9, Part 1 , and is open to female applicants only , due to the nature of the role.

item.title: Appeal and Operations Executive
item.description: £29,500 - £34,750 per year Permanent, full-time (37.5 hours per week) Hybrid working with regular travel to our London Bridge Office What the job involves This is an exciting and pivotal moment for high-value fundraising at Prostate Cancer UK. Our groundbreaking TRANSFORM screening trial has already captured national attention, making real progress towards earlier diagnosis of prostate cancer. Now, through our £100 million Raise the Game appeal, we are accelerating that momentum to transform how prostate cancer is diagnosed, treated and experienced by men and their families over the next five years. We're looking for an Appeal and High-Value Operations Executive to join our High Value Fundraising team. In this newly created role, you'll help coordinate the operational delivery of the Raise the Game appeal, ensuring the infrastructure, governance and processes are in place to support sustainable growth in philanthropic and corporate income. You'll contribute to appeal planning and implementation, helping to deliver key workstreams and keeping activity well organised, aligned and effectively tracked. Working closely with the Appeal and High-Value Operations Manager, you'll help strengthen processes and ways of working, while producing high-quality materials, reports and updates for senior stakeholders, including the Appeal Development Board. Through this work, you'll play an important role in keeping stakeholders informed, engaged and well placed to support the success of the appeal. What we want from you You'll have an understanding of high-value fundraising and be excited by the opportunity to support a major fundraising appeal. You'll have experience supporting or contributing to complex projects or programmes, ideally within a fundraising, charity or not-for-profit environment, and be confident helping to implement and improve processes that support effective ways of working. You'll be a strong communicator who can take complex or technical information and present it clearly for different audiences, including senior stakeholders. You'll also be highly organised, with excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining high standards in a busy environment. If you're looking for an opportunity to develop your skills while contributing to an ambitious appeal with the potential to make a lasting difference for men and their families affected by prostate cancer, we'd love to hear from you. Why work with us? Every man needs to know about the most common cancer in men – prostate cancer. It’s a real and present danger that takes over 12,000 of our dads, grandads, brothers and friends each year. Prostate Cancer UK is the largest men’s health charity in the UK. We have a simple ambition – to stop prostate cancer damaging lives. We invest millions in research to revolutionise testing, treatment and care. We’re blazing a trail to a screening programme that could save thousands of lives with regular, accurate tests for all men at risk. And we work tirelessly to spread the word about risk and offer specialist support to people living with the disease. Work with us and you’ll see your efforts pay off as we give men and their families the power to navigate prostate cancer. Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion At Prostate Cancer UK we’re committed to righting health inequalities across the UK, starting with those faced by Black men. This includes ground-breaking research into Black men's risk and working with communities directly to overcome barriers to the diagnosis and treatment of prostate cancer. To make this happen, we're dedicated to being an inclusive, proactive organisation, as we strive to be Allies to Black communities. We’ll achieve this by advocating and working alongside those communities to promote change. We're also working to be Allies to each other, not only protected groups. In 2024, we launched our New Allyship Training Programme. All colleagues at Prostate Cancer UK will be trained to act and identify as an Ally. We've also signed Business in the Communities Race at Work Charter, as a dedication to our Black health equity work and wider EDI priorities. As a signatory, we're responsible and accountable for driving positive change. How and where we work Colleagues attend the office at least four days per month (pro rata for part-time colleagues) to collaborate, build relationships, and support projects and decision-making. You can choose where to work the rest of the time. Travel to the office is a commute, so we pay our own travel costs. Additional in-person attendance will be required during your first few months for induction and training, to support you to learn the role and get to know colleagues. We trust colleagues to work flexibly while balancing personal commitments with the needs of the charity, and we are committed to making reasonable adjustments for colleagues with a disability, neurodiversity, or a long-term physical or mental health condition. How to Apply Visit our Prostate Cancer UK Careers page to learn more about this role and the benefits we offer. On the vacancy advert, you’ll find everything you need to know about the role, how to apply, and what to include in your application. You can also download a copy of the job description and access the link to our careers portal to submit your application by visiting the website via the apply button. The closing date is Sunday 6th September 2026. Applications must be submitted by 23:45 UK time. Interviews: By arrangement. Currently scheduled for the week of Monday 21st September 2026. We’re expecting the interviews for this role to be held online with a potential second stage meeting. Prostate Cancer UK is a registered charity in England and Wales (1005541) and in Scotland (SC039332). Registered company number 02653887.

For more information about our benefits please visit our website. Office locations: London or Bristol Please note, the successful candidate will be expected to carry out two days in-person working per week on average which will include attendance at your office location. Flexible working arrangements can be discussed and agreed with the line manager subject to role and business needs. An exciting opportunity has arisen at the National Housing Federation (NHF) for a Marketing Assistant. The NHF is the voice of housing associations in England. We are the trade body to almost 600 housing associations, who have grown from philanthropic roots to provide 2.6 million homes to around six million people. You can find further information about the NHF here: https://www.housing.org.uk/about-us/ Interested in starting or developing your career in marketing? Please scroll down to the bottom of the page to download the full job profile and person specification for this role. Key elements of the role: - Support the planning and delivery of integrated marketing campaigns for conferences, events and partnerships activity. - Create and schedule email marketing campaigns, update webpages and produce engaging marketing content across multiple channels. - Monitor campaign performance, analyse marketing activity and produce reports to help drive bookings and engagement. - Coordinate marketing projects, stakeholder approvals, speaker promotion and event communications across teams. The successful candidate: The successful candidate will be able to demonstrate: - Excellent written communication and copywriting skills. - Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. - Confidence working collaboratively as part of a team and building positive working relationships. - A willingness to learn new skills and a commitment to professional development. - Good knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Excel and Word. - The ability to adapt and improve work in response to feedback. Equality, diversity and inclusion The NHF has published its equality, diversity and inclusion strategy, which was co-created with staff – https://www.housing.org.uk/about-us/transparency/who-we-are/. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and we value the contribution each individual makes to our work. We are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and are working to increase the diversity profile of our workforce. We are currently under-represented by ethnic minorities, people with a disability or disabilities and LGBTQ+, and would particularly welcome applications from people in these groups. Disability confident employer We are a disability confident employer and if you are a disabled person who meets the skills and experience we consider essential for the role, we will offer you an interview. Please note: there may be occasions where it is not practicable or appropriate to interview all disabled people who meet the minimum criteria for the job. In certain recruitment situations such as high-volume of applications, we may be required to limit the overall numbers of interviews offered to both disabled people and non-disabled people. In these circumstances the NHF will select the disabled candidates who best meet the minimum criteria for the job rather than all of those that meet the minimum criteria, as we would do for non-disabled applicants. This is in line with the Disability Confident guidelines. We are happy to consider reasonable adjustments to our recruitment process if you have a disability or have a condition that you feel may affect your performance during the recruitment process. Please e-mail the People team at [email protected] with your request or to arrange a time to discuss in more detail. Our role profile and job advert can also be requested in large print or in accessible format via this email address. Completing our Application Form To apply for this role, please complete our online application form. The application form includes your employment and education history plus you will be asked to answer questions in relation to your knowledge, skills and experience, why you are applying for the role and questions in relation to our values. The application form is anonymous and will not require you to upload a CV or cover letter. This will help us to shortlist candidates for interview based solely on their knowledge, skills and experience. Right to work in the UK/UK VISA sponsorship You must have the right to work in the UK and it is important to note that the NHF does not sponsor individuals to work in the UK. item.title: Senior Individual Giving & Campaigns Manager (Mat cover)
item.description: Senior Individual Giving & Campaigns Manager (Maternity Cover) YoungMinds Hybrid, London Bridge (1-2 days per week) £50,898 - £56,554 per annum Fixed-term, full-time contract: October 2026 to October 2027 (35 hours pw) Every day, thousands of young people across the UK struggle with their mental health. Too many are left waiting for support until they reach crisis point. At YoungMinds, we're leading the movement to change that. We amplify young people's voices, provide practical support and campaign for a future where no young person feels alone with their mental health. This work is only possible because of the incredible community of supporters who stand alongside us. We're now looking for an experienced and ambitious fundraising leader to join us as Senior Individual Giving & Campaigns Manager on a maternity cover contract and help drive the next stage of growth in our flagship mass market and individual giving activity. The opportunity This is an exciting leadership role at the heart of our Public Fundraising team. You'll lead and inspire a talented team responsible for growing income through mass market fundraising, individual giving and high-profile campaigns, including our flagship campaign, #HelloYellow which engages thousands of individuals, schools, communities and organisations across the UK to raise funds and wear yellow in solidarity for young people's mental health. You'll develop and deliver strategies that attract new supporters, deepen engagement, increase donor loyalty and grow sustainable income. Combining creativity with a data-led approach, you'll identify new opportunities, test innovative fundraising products, and ensure every supporter enjoys an exceptional experience as part of the YoungMinds movement. This is a role for someone who thrives on growth, innovation and impact. What you'll be doing Leading the Individual Giving & Campaigns team to deliver ambitious fundraising and income targets. Developing and delivering a strategy to drive the growth of regular giving and individual giving programmes. Managing major campaigns, including #HelloYellow to ensure that we maximise the opportunity to generate income Identifying and testing new fundraising products and audience engagement opportunities. Using insight, data and supporter feedback to improve performance, ROI and supporter retention. About you You'll bring significant experience of leading successful individual giving, direct marketing or public fundraising programmes and a track record of delivering growth. We're particularly interested in hearing from candidates who can demonstrate: Experience leading large-scale fundraising and supporter acquisition campaigns. Strong strategic thinking combined with excellent delivery skills. Success in developing and testing new fundraising products or initiatives. Experience managing budgets, setting KPIs and driving fundraising performance. The ability to analyse supporter data and translate insight into action. A collaborative leadership style that motivates, develops and empowers teams. Working effectively and collaboratively as part of cross-functional project teams Why join YoungMinds? This is a chance to join one of the UK's most influential charities and play a key role in helping young people get the mental health support they need. With 1-5 young people experiencing a probably mental health condition in the UK today, there has never been a more important time to lend your experience and skills to a cause that matters to so many. You'll be part of an experienced, multi disciplined, fundraising team that is friendly, supportive and collaborative, with a strong commitment to working together to achieve impact. We work hard but like to have fun while we do it. You'll also be joining a values-led organisation that puts young people's voices at the centre of everything it does, encourages innovation, supports flexible working and is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. And at YoungMinds, we believe every young person deserves mental health support when they need it - no matter what. But not all young people have equal access to help. That's why (AJEDI) Anti-Racism, Justice, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion is central to everything we do. It guides how we operate, support our people, and serve young people. We are committed to anti discriminatory policies and practices. We are also committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. Apply now If you're an experienced individual giving expert with the vision, creativity and ambition to grow income and supporter engagement at scale, we'd love to hear from you. To apply, please send your CV and cover letter to Philippa at Charity People. You will also be asked to complete an anti-racism, justice, equity, diversity and inclusion task as part of your application. Key Dates Closing date: 9am Monday 21 September Interviews: in person Tues 29 September Charity People is a forward-thinking, inclusive organisation that actively and deliberately promotes equity, diversity and inclusion. We know organisations thrive when inclusion is at the forefront. We evidence our commitment by matching charity needs with the skills and experience of candidates irrespective of background including age, disability (including hidden disabilities), gender, gender identity or gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. We do this because we believe that greater diversity leads to greater results for the charities we work with.

item.title: Director of Finance
item.description: Noah's Ark Children's Hospice is partnering with Robertson Bell on a retained basis to recruit a Director of Finance on a permanent basis. This is an exciting opportunity to join a highly regarded children's hospice at a pivotal stage of its development, taking a leading role in strengthening financial performance, improving organisational effectiveness and helping shape the charity's next phase of growth. This is more than a traditional Finance Director role. Noah's Ark has undergone significant transformation in recent years, moving from a predominantly community-based service to operating a 24/7 hospice facility at The Ark. The successful candidate will join at a critical point in this journey, with the opportunity to strengthen the finance function whilst working closely with the wider Senior Leadership Team to ensure the charity is making the best possible use of its resources and delivering maximum value for children and families. For an ambitious, commercially minded finance leader, this is an opportunity to combine strong financial leadership with genuine organisational impact, helping to shape a more effective operating model and contributing directly to the future direction of the charity. The role Partner with the CEO, Senior Leadership Team and Board of Trustees to shape the charity's financial and strategic direction during a period of organisational change. Stabilise and strengthen the finance function, ensuring high-quality financial management, robust controls and accurate, insightful reporting. Lead the budgeting, forecasting and financial planning process, including modelling different care delivery approaches, investment decisions and longer-term strategic scenarios. Support the charity to improve its financial position, identifying opportunities to increase efficiency and ensure resources are being deployed to maximum effect. Oversee statutory accounts, external reporting, audit and regulatory requirements, ensuring the charity maintains strong financial governance and compliance. Ensure effective management of reserves, investments, cash flow, liquidity, insurance and restricted funds. Contribute to the development of the charity's next multi-year strategic plan, bringing commercial discipline, financial insight and a practical focus on delivery. Identify opportunities for cost efficiency and productivity improvements across the organisation, working collaboratively with colleagues to turn insight into action. Support the design and implementation of new IT and financial systems, ensuring they provide the information and controls required to support an effective organisation. Lead and develop a small finance team, setting clear expectations, building capability and creating a culture of accountability and high performance. Play an active role in wider organisational leadership, bringing constructive challenge and financial insight to decisions beyond the traditional finance remit. The organisation Noah's Ark Children's Hospice provides specialist care and support to babies, children and young people with life-limiting or life-threatening conditions, alongside their families. Its purpose-built hospice, The Ark, opened in 2019 and provides a unique environment where children can receive specialist care, therapy, bereavement support and family services in a safe and welcoming setting. Rated 'Outstanding' by the Care Quality Commission, Noah's Ark supports families across North and Central London and Hertsmere, delivering care wherever it is needed - in the family home, within the community or at The Ark. This is an organisation with a warm, supportive culture and a strong commitment to its values of Kindness, Excellence and Courage. It is now looking for a finance leader who can combine that collaborative approach with the confidence to challenge constructively, make difficult decisions and drive meaningful improvement. Essential criteria Fully qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent). Strong experience leading a finance function. Strong understanding of financial controls, governance, audit and statutory reporting. Demonstrable experience producing and interpreting high-quality financial information that supports effective decision-making. Experience leading and developing teams, with the confidence to set expectations, address underperformance and hold colleagues accountable. Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage and influence senior stakeholders and non-finance colleagues. A proactive, hands-on and self-starting appr

item.title: Quantitative Research Fellow
item.description: Passionate about data? Help unlock insights into young people's wellbeing. Anna Freud is seeking a Quantitative Research Fellow to join our world-leading mental health charity for children, young people and their families. Our mission is to close the gap in wellbeing and mental health by advancing, translating, delivering, and sharing the best science and practice with everyone who impacts the lives of children, young people and their families. More information about Anna Freud is available on our website. Our EDI commitment We are dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace and being an equal opportunities employer, whereby equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are core to our recruitment practices. All candidates who meet the job criteria will be considered for employment, regardless of ethnic origin, religion or belief, gender, sexual orientation, disability, age, socioeconomic background, caring responsibilities and care experience. We ask candidates to share their diversity dimensions with us to help us identify, tackle and prevent bias across the employee lifecycle. We believe a diverse workforce enhances our ability to support mental health and wellbeing, allowing us to better meet the needs of the children, young people and families we serve . As a Disability Confident employer, disabled candidates meeting our criteria are guaranteed an interview. Applications are submitted anonymously and assessed using a fair evaluation process based on the criteria set out in our job profiles. What we offer We offer a range of staff benefits, including free counselling through our Employee Assistance Programme. We are proud to have staff-led Diversity Networks offering unique opportunities for learning, connection and impact. This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced researcher to contribute to impactful projects while developing their expertise in a collaborative, inclusive and values-driven environment. What you’ll do You will lead and support research projects exploring the factors that influence children and young people's mental health and wellbeing, using large-scale datasets, statistical analysis and evidence-based research methods. You'll work closely with researchers, schools and other partners to generate insights, evaluate outcomes and share findings that help improve practice, services and policy. What you’ll bring We are seeking a dedicated researcher with a PhD or relevant postgraduate qualification alongside experience of independently leading research projects. Essential skills and experience: Advanced statistical analysis using R, STATA, or similar software. Experience managing and analysing large-scale longitudinal datasets. Experience producing research reports, publications and evidence summaries. Confidence in project management, research design and data collection. Advanced IT and data management skills, including Microsoft Office suite. Key details Hours: full-time (35 hours per week): usual working hours are Monday to Friday, 09:00-17:00. Flexible working is possible. Salary: £40,662 FTE per annum, plus 6% contributory pension scheme. Location: hybrid working (a mixture of onsite and home/remote working). Staff are working onsite for at least 20% of their working hours at our London office (4-8 Rodney Street, London N1 9JH) / our Northern Hub (Colony, 3.07 Jactin House, 24 Hood Street, Ancoats Urban Village, Manchester M4 6WX). Contract type: fixed-term (maternity cover November 2026 to November 2027). Next steps Closing date for applications: midday (12pm), Monday 7 September 2026. Please note that due to high interest in our research vacancies, this advert will close early once 70 applications are received. We encourage you to apply promptly and to keep an eye on our future vacancies for more opportunities. Notification of interview: shortlisted applicants will be notified no later than Friday 11 September 2026.During shortlisting, applicants are anonymously assessed using the criteria visible in the Job Profile. Please note: due to the high volume of applications received, we will not be able to provide feedback to unsuccessful applicants. Interviews: will be held remotely on 17-18 September 2026. How to apply: click on the 'apply now’ button to apply online. We are unable to accept CVs and kindly request no contact from agencies. Questions? Please email Recruitment with any job enquiries, or if you require assistance or experience difficulties when applying. item.title: Governance & EDI Officer (12-month Fixed Term Contract)
item.description: Job description The Biochemical Society promotes the future of molecular biosciences, facilitating the sharing of expertise, supporting the advancement of biochemistry and molecular biology, and raising the awareness of their importance in addressing societal grand challenges. We are seeking a Governance and EDI Officer, on an 12-month Fixed Term Contract, to support the Governance and EDI team. The Governance and EDI Officer will work closely with Trustees, the Senior Leadership Team, and other key stakeholders (both internal and external) to help deliver the calendar of governance committee, board and panel meetings ensuring adherence to pre-defined service standards and ensuring that all discussions, decisions and follow-on actions are recorded, communicated and actioned as appropriate, alongside supporting team members with EDI initiatives, including the Society’s EDI Community, the 2026 online EDI Symposium, Society involvement in the 2027 Minoritised Life Scientists Future Forum and organisational mentoring schemes. The post-holder will support with administration and management for various Committees by compiling and preparing agendas and associated papers before each meeting, preparing Chair Notes and producing accurate minutes of meeting within the agreed timelines. You will also act as a liaison between the Society/PPL and Committee members on practical and logistical matters, such as supporting with expenses, as required. The role will provide administrative support for the Nominations process and success planning, including Committee Chair, Trustee and Director inductions, along with drafting and reviewing policy documents and terms of reference. In addition, providing support on EDI initiatives with the wider team on the EDI Toolkit management. Suitable candidates will have experience in Committee work, with excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to build and maintain positive relationships with a variety of stakeholders. The successful candidate will also be able to present information in a concise report format, with strong attention to detail, while being able to work flexibly to manage competing demands as required. For more information about the organisation, please visit our website. Here is some information on our Benefits package. Closing date: 11th September 2026 Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Please note that this role is home-based and as such interviews will be virtual. “We are interested in every candidate who is eligible to work in the United Kingdom. However, we are not able to sponsor visas.” Please send a CV and covering letter. It is important that you DO NOT include your Personal Information i.e. name and contact details in your CV or Cover Letter . This is because the Society is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive community - a place where we can all be ourselves and succeed on merit. We offer a range of family friendly, inclusive employment policies to support staff from different backgrounds. The Society takes the security of your data seriously. It has internal policies and controls in place to ensure that your data is not lost, accidentally destroyed, misused or disclosed, and is not accessed except by our employees in the proper performance of their duties. Please note that due to limited resources it is not possible for the Society to acknowledge receipt of applications. If you do not hear from us within two weeks of the closing date, please assume that your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion. Refreshed on: 28 August 2026 Closing date: 11 September 2026 at 17:00 Job ref: BCS24/8 Tags: Administration, Advice / Information, Policy, Volunteering Management, Operations, Compliance / Quality, Ethnic Minority / BAME, Governance / Management The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.

item.title: Fundraising Manager (Philanthropy and Partnerships)
item.description: This is an exciting opportunity for a senior fundraising professional who combines strategic thinking with excellent relationship-building skills and a passion for making a tangible difference. The Fundraising Manager will lead on the development and growth of several key income streams, including: Major Donors Corporate Partnerships and Giving Regular Giving Gifts in Wills (Legacies) Working in close partnership with SUDEP Action's other Fundraising Manager (who oversees Community fundraising, Trusts and Grants and other aspects of our in-memory giving), the postholder will also share responsibility for the development, delivery and performance of wider fundraising activity across the charity. A significant aspect of this role will involve re-engaging existing high-value supporters while identifying and cultivating new prospects. The ideal candidate will be confident networking, opening doors, building meaningful relationships and inspiring people to support a cause that may be unfamiliar to them. The postholder will work collaboratively with colleagues across the organisation, including fundraising colleagues, the CEO, and wider management team, drawing upon their expertise to develop effective fundraising plans, test assumptions and ensure the charity is represented professionally, authentically and consistently. Given the nature of SUDEP Action's work, the role also requires sensitivity, empathy and the ability to engage thoughtfully with people affected by epilepsy and bereavement. Full details of the role and experience required can be found in the Job Pack attachment.

item.title: Assistant Director of Services - Criminal Justice & Housing/Homelessness
item.description: 12-month fixed-term contract | Full-time Salary: £58,560 – £71,480 per annum Hours: 35 per week Location: Home-based with regular national travel Job reference number: 1766 Help shape the future of Cranstoun’s services Cranstoun is a social justice and harm reduction charity supporting and empowering people to live healthier and safer lives. Each year, we support more than 45,000 people through services including substance use, criminal justice, domestic abuse, housing and services for children and young people. Following a successful five-year strategy and significant growth, we remain ambitious about the difference we can make. As we enter our next phase, we are investing in the leadership and operational capability needed to support our continued development. We are now recruiting an Assistant Directors of Services to join our senior management team. This is a significant senior leadership role offering the opportunity to lead substantial service portfolios while helping shape how Cranstoun’s services are led and delivered across the organisation. The role Reporting to the Director of Operations, you will lead a substantial portfolio of complex commissioned services and senior operational managers. You will lead nine services with nine direct reports, spanning criminal justice and housing/homelessness provision. You will have clear accountability for ensuring services are safe, effective and well-led, with strong contractual performance, financial sustainability and positive outcomes for the people and communities we support. You will provide operational grip and evidence-based assurance, strengthen safeguarding and management accountability, build effective relationships with commissioners and partners, and ensure risks and underperformance are identified, escalated and addressed early. You will also work collectively with fellow senior operational leaders to embed a One Cranstoun approach, strengthening common standards, sharing learning, developing leadership capability and improving quality and resilience across our services. What you will be accountable for As an Assistant Director, you will take senior operational accountability for: Safe, effective and well-led services – ensuring strong safeguarding, quality, operational risk management and service user outcomes. Contractual performance – ensuring services deliver against contractual requirements and KPIs, with strong commissioner relationships and timely action to address underperformance. Financial sustainability – maintaining strong financial oversight, effective workforce management and oversight of the sustainability of individual contracts. Evidence-based assurance – using reliable performance, quality, workforce and financial information to identify risks and drive improvement. Collective organisational leadership – working beyond individual portfolio boundaries to build consistent standards, stronger leadership and shared ways of working across Cranstoun. You will lead and develop senior operational managers, set clear expectations and create a culture in which support and accountability operate together. You will also lead and contribute to service mobilisation, transformation, workforce planning and continuous improvement. Who we are looking for We are looking for established senior operational leaders with substantial experience leading complex commissioned services and geographically dispersed teams. You will bring a strong track record of: leading safe, high-quality services for people with complex needs; safeguarding, quality and operational risk management; contract and performance management; managing significant service budgets and improving financial performance; building effective relationships with commissioners, regulators and strategic partners; leading service improvement, mobilisation and organisational change; developing senior operational managers and addressing underperformance; and using performance, quality, workforce and financial information to provide assurance and drive improvement. You will need to combine strategic leadership with operational pragmatism, understanding the detail when necessary while maintaining oversight of performance, risk, quality and sustainability across a complex portfolio. Above all, we are looking for collaborative, credible and values-led leaders who can support and challenge in equal measure, build leadership capability and bring people together around common standards and organisational priorities. Specialist experience For this role, you will need significant leadership experience across both Criminal Justice and Housing/Homelessness services, including housing or accommodation-based provision. You will understand the complexity of working across criminal justice, housing, local government and other statutory systems and be experienced in building effective relationships with commissioners and partners while maintaining strong operational and contractual oversight. This is a 12-month fixed-term appointment at an important stage in Cranstoun’s transformation, offering the opportunity to lead a significant portfolio, strengthen operational performance and help shape the future development of our operating model. Be part of Cranstoun’s next chapter Our successful five-year strategy has seen Cranstoun grow considerably, extending our reach and the range of services we provide. We remain ambitious and innovative, committed to developing services that respond to the changing needs of people and communities. As we look to the future, we are investing in the leadership, operational capability and organisational infrastructure needed to support our continued development, strengthening operational governance, consistency and assurance across our services. This role offers the opportunity to do more than manage established portfolios. You will help shape the future of our services and build an Operations Directorate characterised by high standards, clear accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement. Find out more Please refer to the accompanying recruitment pack for the full Job Description, Person Specification and details of the application process. Please note: All posts are subject to an Enhanced DBS check. How to Apply: For more details and to apply, please visit our website via the apply button. Please quote the appropriate Job Ref in all correspondence. Applicants must be able to provide satisfactory evidence of their right to work in the UK at the application stage. Sponsorship is not available for this post. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK that does not require employer sponsorship for the duration of the appointment. Closing date: Sunday 20 September 2026. We are an inclusive employer, committed to promoting equality and diversity in all areas of our work. Registered Charity No: 1061582

item.title: Principal Gift Manager
item.description: Are you a seasoned fundraiser who has experience of securing six-figure gifts? We’re looking for a Principal Gifts Manager, who will be responsible for developing and maintaining meaningful relationships with those whose generous contributions make a transformational impact on the work we do. What does this job do? As Principal Gift Manager, you will: build and manage relationships with ultra-high-net-worth individuals and families to secure six- and seven-figure multi-year gifts, develop tailored cultivation, solicitation and stewardship strategies that deliver exceptional donor experiences and long-term engagement, identify and progress new principal gift prospects, strengthening the pipeline and contributing to long-term income growth, work closely with senior leaders, trustees, and internal teams to maximise high-value fundraising opportunities and develop compelling cases for support. Interviews for this role are provisionally scheduled for Friday 18th September and Monday 21st September, and will take place on Teams. Could this be you? To be successful in this role, you’ll need proven experience of securing six- and seven- figure gifts, from cultivation and stewardship through to “making the ask”. You’ll need significant experience managing a diverse portfolio, and the ability to build, influence and maintain relationships with senior stakeholders and donors. You’ll be highly organised, proactive, and collaborative, and thrive while working in a fast paced environment. A passion for the work we do is essential. About Dogs Trust We love dogs. That’s why we do whatever we can to make sure every four-legged friend gets the love they deserve. We’ll never put a healthy dog down, so our work is focused on helping dogs in need, supporting owners every step of the walk, and creating a better world for dogs in the future. It’s what we’ve been doing since 1891 and how we’ve grown to become the UK’s leading dog charity, helping 12,000 loyal friends find their forever homes every year. To apply for this position please click the APPLY NOW button. Our application process requires you submit a personal statement explaining your interest and suitability for the role. Dogs are incredibly diverse, much like the humans that love them! At Dogs Trust we value diversity, and we're committed to fostering an inclusive culture. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, abilities, and cultures and believe that a diverse workforce helps us to achieve our mission. Our colleague networks give our people a voice, acting as vehicles for real and meaningful change within Dogs Trust. We truly want to see every candidate shine throughout the entire job application process, interview stages, and during their time with us. If there's anything on your mind or any adjustments you may need, don't hesitate to reach out to us. We're here to support you every step of the way.
item.dc:creator: Dogs Trust

item.title: Finance Manager
item.description: We are seeking a proactive, forward-thinking, part-qualified or qualified accountant to lead the development of an efficient, AI-assisted finance function for the charity. Reporting directly to the CEO, you will be part of Home-Start Southwark and Lewisham's senior leadership team, in the only finance-focussed role within the team, taking ownership of the organisation's financial systems, reporting, and compliance — and critically, you will have the opportunity to strategically shape how finance operates over the next 6–12 months. This is a growth opportunity for someone who has an interest and belief in our work supporting local families and combines strong technical finance skills with curiosity about technology, a willingness to challenge existing ways of working, and the confidence to work at Board level. You will implement cloud-based accounting with AI-enabled features, design meaningful management reporting, and ensure the charity is fully compliant with SORP 2026 and Charity Commission requirements — all while keeping the CEO's time focused on leading the organisation, not managing the books. Why this role matters now This is not a maintenance role. We are looking for someone who wants to build something — to design and embed a finance function that is fit for a growing charity. You will have the rare opportunity to shape the tools, processes, and reporting frameworks from the ground up, working directly with the CEO to make finance a strategic enabler rather than an administrative burden.

item.title: Housing and Compliance Officer
item.description: 37 hours per week / permanent / Monday - Thursday 9am - 5pm; Friday 9am - 4.30pm / Based onsite in Hove, this role also involves regular weekly visits to our properties across Sussex. To support this travel, you will need a full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle. YMCA DownsLink Group is the leading charity for children and young people across Sussex and Surrey. We offer safe homes, mental health support and trusted advice. We believe that every child and young person has the right to be safe, heard and to shape their own future. We work alongside them to make that happen. We are here for children and young people, many of whom face multiple challenges and need our support. Our Values - we do what’s right, we work with heart, and we build real connections – guide us in all our actions. We are seeking a proactive, tenant-focused Housing and Compliance Officer to deliver high-quality housing management and property compliance services across our Sussex properties. Reporting to the Income and Property Manager and working as part of the Asset Management Team, you will play a key role in ensuring our general needs properties are well-managed, compliant with all relevant regulations, and provide safe, secure homes for our residents. This role combines housing management responsibilities with oversight of property compliance, requiring strong organisational skills, attention to detail, and a commitment to excellent customer service. The role involves overseeing tenants throughout their housing journey, conducting home visits, managing tenancy matters, coordinating repairs, and ensuring properties remain safe, compliant, and meet the Decent Homes Standard. You will work closely with tenants, contractors, and internal teams to maintain excellent housing services, manage compliance programmes, address damp and mould cases, and ensure adherence to housing regulations and safety standards. You will also play a key role in safeguarding tenant safety, monitoring contractor performance, supporting income collection, responding to complaints, and championing tenant voice to drive service improvements. Key areas of responsibility: Housing and tenancy management Resident engagement and support Repairs and maintenance coordination Property compliance and health and safety Damp, mould and disrepair case management Contractor and supplier management Income collection and tenancy enforcement Customer service and complaint resolution Please also download the job profile (below), which includes the full role description and person specification. This is an excellent opportunity for a housing professional with experience in housing management, property compliance, and health and safety. You'll be passionate about delivering high-quality, customer-focused services that make a tangible difference to people's lives and help ensure residents have safe, secure, and well-maintained homes. Qualifications, Knowledge and Experience A minimum of a CIH Level 3 qualification in Housing, Housing Maintenance, Asset Management, Letting and Managing Residential Property, or Housing Practice/Services (desirable) We will also consider candidates who can demonstrate significant relevant experience in property compliance, building safety, or health and safety, or who hold a recognised City & Guilds, IOSH, or NEBOSH qualification Awareness of the Housing Health and Safety Rating System (HHSRS), or a willingness to develop expertise in this area, to support YMCA DLG's commitment to providing safe, compliant, and high-quality homes Significant experience within the social housing sector, ideally in housing management, resident engagement, or customer-focused service delivery roles Experience working for a Registered Provider, housing association, local authority, or other social housing organisation Demonstrable experience of working within a regulated housing environment, delivering housing management and property compliance services while building positive relationships with residents and stakeholders Experience supporting tenancy-related processes, including starter and continuation documentation, to help residents sustain successful tenancies Experience of working within a psychologically informed environment and applying trauma-informed approaches is desirable; training can be provided Strong experience in auditing, data collection, record management, and maintaining accurate housing management systems Experience coordinating and monitoring contractors to ensure works are delivered safely, efficiently, and to the required standard Proven ability to engage effectively with residents, contractors, local authority departments, partner agencies, and regulatory bodies Experience of income collection, tenancy sustainment, and arrears management within a social housing setting Good working knowledge of housing legislation and statutory compliance requirements, including fire safety, gas safety, electrical safety, water safety, and resident access arrangements for compliance works Ability to identify, promote, and embed best practice across teams and services CLOSING DATE: Wednesday 16 September at midnight. PLEASE NOTE: We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorship for this role, so applicants must already have the right to live and work in the UK independently. An inclusive workplace We are committed to policies and practices of equity, diversity, and inclusion and to supporting our people to make sure our culture is consistent with this commitment. Accessibility If you require assistance or have questions regarding the application process, please do contact us. YMCA DLG requires all staff and volunteers to be committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people, and to respond proactively to safeguarding concerns. Successful applicants will undergo a thorough background screening process, conducted by an accredited third-party provider. This includes an Enhanced DBS check (with Children’s and Adults’ Barred Lists) as well as comprehensive reference and activity checks.

item.description: Application Deadline : 21 September 2026 Department : Business Services Location : London/Brussels Compensation : London £76,431 / year and Brussels €7,066 / month Description If you are a strategic HR leader who thrives in complex international environments, we would love to hear from you. We are looking for an exceptional Head of People & Culture to partner with senior leaders, lead a global People & Culture function, and help build an organisation capable of delivering lasting environmental impact. This is a unique opportunity to influence strategy, culture and organisational effectiveness at a critical leadership level. If this opportunity excites you, we would encourage you to submit your application early and don't wait until the deadline. While the vacancy will remain open, we will begin reviewing candidates throughout the advertising period. Important dates to note: Deadline to submit an initial application: 21st of September If your profile passes initial screening, you will be asked to submit additional information in the form of three additional questions. The deadline to submit your answers is the 24th of September If we do not receive a response to these questions by the deadline we will assume you are no longer interested in the role. Interviews will take place from the week beginning 28 September 2026 Please also review the "Our Hiring Process" section at the bottom of this advert to learn more about the stages involved for this specific role. Key Responsibilities Act as a trusted adviser to the Global Leadership Team and, with the People Business Partners, other senior leaders, providing expert guidance on People-related organisational design implications, workforce planning, leadership effectiveness, and change. Provide functional leadership and coordination across the People team, ensuring high standards, alignment and delivery while retaining clear accountability for the overall effectiveness and performance of the global People function Lead any People-related organisational development initiatives to support growth, international expansion, and evolving organisational models Contribute to the development and leadership of ClientEarth’s EDI and Decolonisation strategy, ensuring alignment with global best practice and organisational values and measurable progress in systems, decision-making, and leadership practice See the job description for a full list of duties for this role.
