item.title: Employee Relations Advisor
item.description: We're looking for an experienced Employee Relations Partner to join the People Team at Save the Children UK, where you'll act as a trusted expert and help shape a more human-centric, fair and empathetic colleague experience across the organisation. About Us Save the Children UK believes every child deserves a future. In the UK and around the world, we work every day to give children a healthy start in life, the opportunity to learn, and protection from harm. When crisis strikes, we are always among the first to respond and the last to leave, ensuring children are protected, supported and heard. About the Role As our Employee Relations Partner , you'll be the organisation's go-to expert on employee relations, supporting leaders to navigate complex people challenges while ensuring our approach remains legally robust, values-led and people-centred. You'll manage a varied and often sensitive caseload, lead the development of ER policies and practices, build capability across the People Team and work closely with senior stakeholders to foster a culture of trust, accountability and fairness. Working alongside HR Business Partners as part of a self-managed team, you'll help ensure a consistent and practical approach to employee relations across a unionised environment, bringing clarity and confidence to complex people matters. In this role, you will: Manage a broad range of employee relations cases, from day-to-day matters to complex and high-risk issues. Provide expert advice and coaching to managers, senior leaders and People colleagues on employee relations and people risk. Lead the development and continuous improvement of ER policies, guidance and resources. Build organisational capability through coaching, mentoring and sharing ER expertise across the People Team. Identify trends and opportunities to improve processes, strengthen colleague experience and reduce organisational risk. Lead staff safeguarding cases in partnership with the Safeguarding Team, ensuring a trauma-informed and victim-centred approach. Collaborate with teams including Legal, Safeguarding and senior leadership to resolve complex workforce challenges. About You To be successful, you'll bring: Strong knowledge of UK employment law and employee relations best practice. Significant experience managing complex, sensitive and high-risk ER casework. The ability to influence, coach and challenge stakeholders at all levels, including senior leaders. Experience developing policies, guidance and practical tools that improve employee experience. A track record of building capability and confidence in others through coaching and mentoring. Comfort navigating complex, sensitive and sometimes challenging situations, with the ability to remain balanced, pragmatic and solutions-focused. Skilled at translating policy into practice, providing clear and practical guidance that supports fair and consistent decision-making. Able to bring clarity to processes and people issues, helping managers and colleagues navigate complexity with confidence. Excellent communication, facilitation and conflict resolution skills. A commitment to Save the Children's vision, mission and values. What we offer you We promote flexibility, inclusion, collaboration, and wellbeing both at work and beyond, and offer a wide range of benefits designed to reward your hard work and inspire you to help improve the lives of children every day. Some of the benefits you can expect include: Generous Annual Leave – Starting at 27 days per year (pro rata for part-time employees) increasing with service up to 32 days, plus public holidays and our annual 'Save the Children Day'. Family Leave – Up to 39 weeks of maternity/adoption pay (including up to 21 weeks full pay) and paternity/adoption leave of 10 weeks full pay (plus statutory entitlement). Special Leave – Up to 10 days paid leave per year (pro rata) for urgent or exceptional personal circumstances, without using annual leave. Volunteer Leave – Up to 3 days paid leave per year to support volunteering and give back. Pension & Life Assurance – Helping you plan for the future with up to 7% employer pension contributions. Employee Discounts – Access thousands of deals across groceries, retail, tech, travel, fitness, and more. Health & Wellbeing Support – Including access to a 24/7 Virtual GP and Employee Assistance Programme and Counselling, eye care support, and seasonal flu vaccinations. Please note: To avoid disappointment, you are advised to submit your application as soon as possible as we reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a high volume of applications are received. This is to ensure that we can manage application levels whilst maintaining a positive candidate experience. Unfortunately once a vacancy has closed, we are unable to consider further applications. Location & Ways of Working: The majority of our roles can be performed remotely in the UK, but at times you will be required to come to your contracted office (usually between 2–4 days per month, depending on the needs of your role, team, or service). For many roles, this is likely to be the minimum required to deliver impact. This will be discussed and agreed with your manager / team and we encourage candidates to discuss our ways of working in more detail at interview stage. Flexible Working - We are happy to discuss flexible working options at interview . Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion: Save the Children UK believes in a world that is fair, inclusive and equitable where all children have the opportunity to change their world. We apply this to our workforce, and we are committed to developing and supporting a diverse, equitable, and inclusive organisation where structural inequality is actively addressed, and all employees have a sense of belonging and feel that they can thrive. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, and are especially interested in hearing from people with diverse and intersecting identities such as lived experience of poverty, people of faith, people of colour, people with disabilities, with experience of migration and/or refugee status, care-experienced people, the LGBTQIA+ community and individuals with experience living in diverse families. We are not looking for just one type of person - we want to recruit people who can add fresh perspectives, innovative ideas or challenge that disrupts the risk of group think. We know that different voices working together will enable us to do our work better, improving the lives of children around the world. Salary Structure: Save the Children is committed to paying staff in a fair and equitable way and will benchmark all salary offers in line with the pay of existing staff. To see our full offer please visit this link: Save the Children | Careers Interview Expenses: Candidates should note that unfortunately it is not our policy to reimburse expenses accrued when attending interviews at Save the Children UK unless you are requested to attend an interview in an alternative location to where the role is based. Pre-employment Checks: Any Employment with Save the Children UK will be subject to the following checks prior to your start date: A satisfactory police record check to include a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check and/or an International Criminal Record Check (If applicable) Receipt of satisfactory references - As a committed member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, as part of our onboarding process, Save the Children UK will undertake a minimum of 2 references, and any additional references required to collectively cover the last 5 years of your employment history. Proof of eligibility to work in the national location for this role Closing Date: 20 September 2026

item.title: Safeguarding Officer
item.description: ROLE OVERVIEW: The Safeguarding Officer is responsible for delivering high-quality operational safeguarding across RABI, ensuring safeguarding concerns involving beneficiaries are managed consistently, professionally and in accordance with legislation, statutory guidance and organisational policy. Working as one of two Safeguarding Officers, the postholder provides specialist safeguarding advice, guidance and support to colleagues across England, Wales and Northern Ireland. The role manages safeguarding concerns from initial notification through to resolution, undertakes safeguarding risk assessments, coordinates safeguarding activity, maintains accurate safeguarding records, supports multi-agency working and contributes to achieving safe outcomes for beneficiaries. Working closely with the Safeguarding Manager, the second Safeguarding Officer and the Designated Safeguarding Lead, the postholder contributes to the continuous improvement of safeguarding practice, supports organisational safeguarding awareness and helps maintain a resilient safeguarding service through collaborative working and continuity of operational delivery. Key Accountabilities 1. Operational Safeguarding Work alongside the Safeguarding Manager and Designated Safeguarding Lead to support the continuous development and implementation of safeguarding practice across the organisation. Act as an operational point of contact for staff, volunteers and external partners regarding safeguarding concerns and queries, providing advice and guidance whilst escalating complex or high-risk matters appropriately. Manage safeguarding concerns from initial notification through to resolution, ensuring concerns are assessed, risk managed, recorded and progressed in accordance with legislation, statutory guidance and RABI policies and procedures. Undertake safeguarding risk assessments, exercising professional judgement to support proportionate, person-centred and defensible safeguarding decision-making. Promote professional curiosity, reflective practice and consistent safeguarding approaches across the organisation. Provide delegated Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead cover in the absence of both the Designated Safeguarding Lead and both Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads, in accordance with RABI policies, procedures and delegated authority. 2. Professional Advice and Guidance Provide specialist safeguarding advice, guidance and practical support to Regional Support Officers, managers, staff and volunteers to support the effective management of safeguarding concerns and increase confidence in safeguarding practice. Support colleagues to recognise safeguarding concerns, understand safeguarding responsibilities and apply safeguarding procedures consistently. Support the Safeguarding Manager in developing and delivering safeguarding training, awareness sessions and operational guidance for staff and volunteers. Effectively engage with staff and volunteers across RABI to promote safeguarding awareness, encourage good practice and embed a positive safeguarding culture. 3. Case Management, Recording and Information Management Maintain day-to-day administration, quality assurance and oversight of safeguarding records within RABI's case management system, ensuring information is accurate, timely, complete and compliant with organisational standards. Follow up safeguarding recording queries and support colleagues in maintaining high-quality safeguarding records. Prepare and provide operational safeguarding information, data, trends and case information to support the Safeguarding Manager in producing monthly, quarterly and annual safeguarding reports. Produce clear, evidence-based safeguarding documentation and maintain confidentiality in accordance with information governance requirements. Identify emerging safeguarding themes, trends and learning to support continuous improvement of safeguarding practice. Monitor safeguarding activity to ensure agreed actions are completed appropriately and within agreed timescales. Maintain confidentiality and information governance standards in accordance with organisational policy and legislation. 4. Partnership Working Develop and maintain effective working relationships with Adult and Children's Social Care, Police, Health Services, Mental Health Services, Domestic Abuse Services, counselling providers and other statutory and voluntary sector partners. Coordinate safeguarding referrals and information sharing, ensuring referrals are timely, appropriate and well evidenced. Represent RABI appropriately within multi-agency safeguarding discussions and maintain effective working relationships that support positive outcomes for beneficiaries. Maintain an up-to-date knowledge of safeguarding legislation, guidance and referral pathways across England, Wales and Northern Ireland. 5. Service Delivery and Continuous Improvement Promote and champion safeguarding practice across all departments, supporting compliance, increasing staff awareness and embedding safeguarding within everyday practice. Maintain effective working relationships with internal teams, including Volunteering, Partnerships, Fundraising, Campaigns and other departments, providing safeguarding advice on new initiatives and emerging projects. Maintain up-to-date knowledge of safeguarding legislation, statutory guidance and best practice, proactively engaging with professional networks and partner organisations to ensure RABI continues to deliver high-quality safeguarding practice. Manage referrals into RABI's counselling provision, ensuring agreed service standards and referral processes are maintained. Facilitate safeguarding supervision sessions with Regional Support Officers and Regional Support Managers where agreed by the Safeguarding Manager. Support the management and monitoring of RABI's StaySafe lone working system. Work collaboratively with the Safeguarding Manager and second Safeguarding Officer to ensure continuity of safeguarding provision during periods of leave, absence or increased operational demand. Undertake any other duties commensurate with the responsibilities and grading of the role. Decision Making and Autonomy The Safeguarding Officer manages a varied operational safeguarding caseload, exercising professional judgement within legislation, statutory guidance and organisational policy. The postholder independently assesses safeguarding concerns, determines appropriate safeguarding actions and coordinates operational safeguarding interventions. Complex safeguarding concerns involving significant organisational, legal or reputational risk are escalated to the Safeguarding Manager. Strategic safeguarding leadership, policy development, organisational assurance, resource management and line management remain the responsibility of the Safeguarding Manager. Key Working Relationships Internal Safeguarding Manager Second Safeguarding Officer Regional Support Officers Service Delivery colleagues Managers, staff and volunteers External Adult and Children's Social Care Police Health Services Mental Health Services Domestic Abuse Services Counselling Providers Voluntary and Community Organisations Other safeguarding partners Person Specification Qualifications and Professional Development Essential Educated to degree level or able to demonstrate equivalent knowledge and experience gained through professional practice. A recognised safeguarding qualification or evidence of substantial safeguarding training relevant to the role. Commitment to maintaining continuing professional development and keeping knowledge of safeguarding legislation, guidance and best practice up to date. Willingness to undertake further training appropriate to the requirements of the role. Desirable Specialist safeguarding qualifications or accredited safeguarding training. Mental Capacity Act, Domestic Abuse, MARAC, Prevent, suicide prevention or trauma-informed practice training. Membership of a relevant professional body. Knowledge Essential Sound knowledge of safeguarding legislation, statutory guidance and best practice relating to adults. Understanding of safeguarding principles, risk assessment, information sharing and multi-agency working. Knowledge of the roles and responsibilities of statutory safeguarding partners. Understanding of professional boundaries, confidentiality, consent and information governance. Knowledge of safeguarding practice within complex family situations, domestic abuse, mental ill health, self-neglect, exploitation, substance misuse and other safeguarding risks. Understanding of equality, diversity, inclusion and the impact of discrimination and disadvantage on vulnerability. Desirable Knowledge of safeguarding arrangements across England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Sound knowledge of safeguarding legislation, statutory guidance and best practice relating to children. Understanding of safeguarding within charities or community-based services. Awareness of issues affecting farming and rural communities. Experience Essential Substantial experience of managing safeguarding concerns relating to adults. Experience of managing safeguarding concerns within a professional setting. Experience of undertaking safeguarding risk assessments and making defensible safeguarding decisions. Experience of providing safeguarding advice and guidance to colleagues. Experience of working collaboratively with statutory agencies and partner organisations. Experience of maintaining accurate, confidential and legally compliant case records. Experience of managing competing priorities within a busy operational environment. Desirable Experience within the voluntary or charity sector. Experience of coordinating safeguarding referrals. Experience of contributing to safeguarding training or awareness programmes. Experience of using electronic case management or customer relationship management systems. Experience of supporting organisational service improvement. Skills and Abilities

item.title: Senior Advice Manager
item.description: About Toynbee Hall Based in the East End of London since 1884, Toynbee Hall is a charity working alongside people facing poverty, injustice, and inequality to build a fairer East London. We provide vital advice and support, working in partnership to tackle unfairness and ensure everyone has an equal chance to thrive. Job purpose The Senior Advice Manager is responsible for the effective day-to-day management and coordination of Toynbee Hall’s debt advice services across multiple locations. The postholder will ensure services are appropriately resourced, accessible and delivered consistently, meeting agreed contractual, quality, compliance and performance requirements. The Senior Advice Manager will manage and develop Debt Advisers, Trainee Debt Advisers and Administrators; monitor service performance and capacity; address operational issues and risks; and ensure appropriate action is taken where performance or quality falls below expected standards. Working closely with the Head of Debt and Money, Quality Assurance and Technical Supervision colleagues, the postholder will use performance information, quality findings and operational insight to identify areas for improvement and ensure agreed actions are implemented. Key Responsibilities Management of local sites to ensure all services are available. Ensure local services are available daily by effectively managing staffing, sickness, annual leave, emergencies and operational challenges. Work closely with internal teams, external contractors and local stakeholders to ensure all sites operate safely, efficiently and in line with organisational standards. Identify resource gaps, operational risks and service pressures, implementing solutions to maintain service delivery and performance. Build and maintain strong relationships with local authorities, housing providers, community organisations and partner agencies, representing Toynbee Hall at meetings, networking events and community engagement activities to strengthen referral pathways. Line management of a team to ensure objectives are set and met Lead, motivate and support the team to achieve agreed service, quality, compliance and performance objectives. Conduct regular one-to-one supervision, team meetings and performance reviews providing constructive feedback and clear expectations. Coach, mentor and develop staff, identifying learning and development needs supporting career progression and fostering a culture of continuous improvement. Provide technical guidance and support on complex debt advice cases, ensuring advisers deliver accurate, compliant and client-centred advice. Ensure compliance and the quality of advice required are achieved Ensure the team consistently delivers high-quality, client-focused debt advice in line with FCA requirements, funder expectations and Toynbee Hall policies. Monitor case quality through audits, supervision, management information and performance data, implementing improvement plans where required. Analyse service performance and management information, identifying trends, risks and areas requiring action, and provide recommendations to the Head of Debt and Money. Ensure case files meet all quality assurance, audit and contractual standards. Manage and respond to complaints relating to debt advice service delivery in line with Toynbee Hall’s complaints procedure, ensuring appropriate investigation, timely resolution and that learning is used to improve service delivery. Essential Criteria Experience and Skills Significant experience of managing frontline advice services and managing highperforming teams to achieve service, quality and performance objectives. Demonstrable experience of line management, including supervision, performance management, coaching, mentoring and staff development, including effectively addressing underperformance. Experience of delivering regulated debt advice services and having management responsibility for maintaining high standards of quality, compliance and client care. • Proven ability to provide technical guidance and appropriate support on complex debt advice cases, working within agreed technical supervision and escalation arrangements. Hold a recognised debt advice qualification (e.g. CertMAP or equivalent) with demonstrable experience of delivering FCA-regulated debt advice and supporting the quality and development of debt advice practice. Communication and Interpersonal Skills Excellent leadership, communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to inspire and motivate others. Ability to build positive relationships with colleagues, partners, funders and external stakeholders. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Our Benefits Package Annual Leave 25 days of annual leave, plus 3 additional days for our Christmas shutdown (on top of bank holidays). After 2 years: +3 extra days of leave. After 3 years: +1 additional day. After 5 years: A total of 30 days annual leave, plus the 3-day Christmas shutdown. Pension Standard Life Pension Scheme – Employer contribution: 4%, Employee contribution: 5% Additional Perks & Support Enhanced Sick Pay for peace of mind during illness Enhanced Maternity & Paternity Leave to support growing families Employee Eyecare Vouchers to support your vision health Employee Assistance Programme for free, confidential advice and support Mental Health First Aid to ensure workplace well-being Tenancy Deposit Scheme to help secure your home Interest-Free Season Ticket Loan for cost-effective commuting Cycle to Work Scheme to promote a healthier, greener way to travel Charity Mentoring Network to support professional development and networking Westfield Healthcare Cash Plan Perk Box Further information We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. Please refer to the attached job description for more details

item.title: Project Development Co-ordinator
item.description: About us National Energy Action (NEA) is the national fuel poverty charity. We’ve worked across England, Wales, and Northern Ireland for over 40 years, to ensure that everyone can afford to live in a warm, healthy home. Millions of households across the UK still face high energy bills, low incomes and poor energy efficiency We work with frontline practitioners, companies, regulators and governments, to support vulnerable clients, raise awareness and achieve enduring change . Our work tackles these challenges head‑on, delivering practical support, influencing policy and improving lives. Our values guide how we work every day — we make things happen, we put people first and we lead the way . These values come to life through our behaviours, including pulling together, owning the outcome and supporting one another . Our teams are friendly, knowledgeable and passionate about what we do. We offer a supportive, rewarding workplace where you can build a meaningful career while making a real difference every day. The Role We are looking for a motivated and skilled Project Development Co‑ordinator working in the North-East / Yorkshire area. You will play a key role in delivering NEA’s work programme across the region, leading on stakeholder engagement, community outreach and direct support to low‑income and vulnerable households. Travel within the region and occasionally beyond will be required. This is an exciting opportunity to: · Lead and deliver impactful projects during a critical time for household energy needs · Build strong partnerships with local authorities, housing providers and community organisations · Provide one‑to‑one energy and fuel debt advice to householders · Deliver group awareness sessions and upskilling activities · Oversee project outputs, outcomes and reporting to funders · Support the development of new programmes, including funding proposals and presentations Your work will directly contribute to improving health, wellbeing and energy resilience for those most at risk. What you will need to succeed You will bring: · Demonstrable experience of developing and/or managing projects in energy efficiency, community development, housing, social policy or related fields · An understanding of the environmental, social and economic challenges facing deprived communities · Strong organisational skills and the ability to maintain accurate records and produce high‑quality reports · Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with vulnerable or disadvantaged households · A commitment to making a positive difference · Knowledge of domestic energy efficiency (desirable) This role is ordinarily hybrid, based at NEA’s Newcastle office, but we can offer hybrid or fully remote working depending on your home location . Some national travel will be required from time to time to meet partners and attend events. The successful post holder will also be expected to travel throughout the North East and Yorkshire to meet stakeholders and deliver community outreach activities. Hybrid and home working arrangements are subject to necessary health and safety and GDPR checks. Post holders must be resident within the UK and be able to provide their Right to Work in the UK. Due to the nature of this role, successful candidates will be subject to an Enhanced DBS check. What We Offer · £35,017 to £39,829 per annum (Levels 6-7, Points 23 – 28). New appointments will usually begin at the starting point of the scale. · 11½% non-contributory pension. · 25 days annual leave plus 3 additional days in between Christmas New Year Period when our offices close; · All public holidays · Flexible working arrangements including hybrid working · Enhanced family friendly payments. · Employee Assistance Programme. · Employee benefits platform Interviews : Week commencing 28 September 2026 Please note that National Energy Action is not a sponsoring organisation. Therefore, the successful applicant must already possess the right to work in the UK or be able to secure the right to work in the UK independently. Please note CVs will not be accepted as part of the application process. No recruitment agency or advertising enquiries, please. NEA is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all people with the necessary skills and experience. Only shortlisted candidates selected for interview will be notified of the confirmed time and location of interview.

item.title: Stakeholder Engagement Manager/ Rheolwr Ymgysylltu â Rhanddeiliaid
item.description: The National Lottery Community Fund is recruiting for a Stakeholder Engagement Manager, a key role in our External Affairs Team within our Communications, Impact and Influence Team. This role offers an exceptional opportunity to shape our stakeholder engagement during an exciting time. You will position the Fund as a convening force in civil society, advancing community priorities through evidence-based advocacy that demonstrates how our funding strengthens communities. Using your insight into the sector, you will work with colleagues to map and manage priority stakeholder relationships relevant to our missions and the impact of our funding. You will develop targeted engagement strategies to strengthen and diversify our stakeholders, delivering key activities including communications, events, briefings and meetings to support the development of these relationships. You will identify and act upon opportunities to demonstrate the impact of our funding on communities and how it aligns with relevant and influential stakeholders and organisations. You will have strong project management experience, with a robust approach to tracking relationships and managing stakeholder data, ideally through the use of Stakeholder Relationship Management (SRM) systems. The ideal candidate will bring a strong communications and engagement background, as well as experience in working with senior level stakeholders. Ideally you will have had exposure to the voluntary, community and social enterprise sectors. You should excel at building relationships with diverse stakeholders and be adept at navigating complex external environments. Key responsibilities: Map and prioritise the Fund's stakeholder framework, identifying key influencers and decision-makers across sectors, ensuring an effective cadence of engagement (making it clear who are we talking to, when and why) Design strategic engagement plans that align stakeholder relationships with our missions and corporate plan, as part of the Fund’s integrated communications strategy Coordinate high-profile events and engagement opportunities that strengthen the Fund's position in civil society Lead a range of stakeholder communications, including newsletters, bespoke emails, meetings and briefings. Lead the creation of stakeholder toolkits and narrative materials that enable senior leaders and colleagues to engage effectively Build measurement frameworks to evaluate the impact of stakeholder engagement activities Provide expert counsel to colleagues on relationship management and influencer engagement Maintain the SRM system and support colleagues across the Fund to use appropriately. Interview Details: Date: W/C 28th September Format: Virtual Location: UK Wide We have a hybrid approach to working. Work pattern will be agreed with the successful candidate. Our offices are in Belfast, Birmingham, Cardiff, Exeter, Glasgow, Leeds, London, Manchester and Newcastle. If you would like an informal conversation about the role specifically, please contact us. Any questions about the recruitment process, please email us. How to apply: Upload your CV in word format and write a supporting statement (1000 words) with the following criteria, we will use this to score your application. Essential criteria Strong experience in stakeholder engagement and partnership development, with a track record of advising at senior levels. Proven ability to design and deliver engagement programmes that meet organisational objectives. Experience in delivering high-level communications and events. Experience building stakeholder mapping tools and evaluation frameworks. Strong project management, coordinating complex engagement activities. Experience drafting and delivering high-quality presentation materials, often under tight timeframes. Desirable criteria Understanding of, or background in VCSE, public sector or civil society partnership development. People management experience. Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Communities in the UK come in all shapes and sizes. National Lottery funding is for everyone – therefore, we are committed to equity, diversity and inclusion and we work hard to ensure our funding reaches where it is needed. We also believe our people should represent the communities, organisations and individuals we work with. That’s why The National Lottery Community Fund is committed to being an inclusive employer and a great place to work. We recognise and celebrate the fact that our people come from diverse backgrounds. We positively welcome applications from people from ethnic minority backgrounds, people with disabilities or longstanding health conditions, people who are LGBTQ+, and people from different socio-economic and educational backgrounds, as well as people of all ages. As a Disability Confident Employer, we take a proactive approach in making reasonable adjustments, if needed, throughout the recruitment process and during employment. (This can be related to a physical and mental health condition.)

item.title: Development Coordinator
item.description: About the Role We are looking for a Development Coordinator to support and develop Outside Edge Theatre Company’s fundraising and income generation. Working closely with the Artistic Director/CEO, Trustees and external consultants, you will play a key role in the day-to-day delivery of fundraising activity, with a particular focus on trust and foundation fundraising, individual giving, corporate relationships, supporter communications and donor stewardship. This is a newly created role and we welcome applications from candidates interested in taking their first steps in a career in fundraising. Training, strategic support and development opportunities will be provided. Key Responsibilities Grant Management – Research, prepare and write high-quality applications to trusts and foundations. – Identify new funding opportunities and manage application deadlines. – Coordinate funder acknowledgements, monitoring and evaluation reports. – Support the development of statutory contracts and restricted project funding. Individual & Major Giving – Support the implementation of a new individual and major giving strategy. – Analyse donor data to identify engagement and fundraising opportunities. – Develop fundraising campaigns, donor events and personalised supporter communications. – Lead supporter stewardship and cultivation events. – Develop targeted content and approaches for high-net-worth individuals and corporate partners. Corporate & Challenge Events – Support the implementation of the corporate and challenge events strategy. – Develop and deliver challenge events. – Build relationships with corporate partners and sponsors. – Support social media and community engagement to recruit challenge event fundraisers. Communications & Administration – Oversee the monthly supporter newsletter and other fundraising communications. – Update donor communications, website and promotional materials. – Maintain accurate Gift Aid, income and expenditure and fundraising records. – Keep the development database up to date and use Salesforce and Mailchimp effectively. – Ensure fundraising systems and procedures are effective and GDPR compliant. – Prepare fundraising reports and keep up to date with fundraising and charity sector developments. Person Specification We are looking for someone with: – An interest in fundraising or supporter engagement, gained through paid work, volunteering or other relevant experience. – Excellent copywriting and editing skills, with the ability to adapt communications for different audiences and platforms. – Experience in an administrative, fundraising, customer service or similar role. – Excellent organisation, time management and attention to detail. – Strong communication skills and confidence engaging with a wide range of people, including public speaking. – Good IT skills; CRM experience is desirable. – The ability to analyse data and identify trends. – A positive, inspiring and collaborative approach. – A passion and commitment to arts with social inclusion at its core. – The ability to manage a varied workload in a busy, fast-changing environment. – A willingness to meet the requirements of Outside Edge’s Vulnerable Adults Protection Policy. – A willingness to support marketing and promotional activity. We particularly welcome applications from people with relevant transferable skills, even if you do not meet every criterion. Access & Inclusion Outside Edge aims to encourage a culture where people can be themselves and be valued for their strengths and we want our team to represent the same diversity of our participants, audiences and artists. We are keen to hear from a diverse range of candidates from all backgrounds drawing on different perspectives, experience and knowledge. We particularly want to encourage people to apply for this role who have lived experience of being affected by addiction and those who are representative of the diverse communities we serve. Please feel free to contact us if you require further assistance or would like to submit your application in an alternative format. We will support any access requirements you may have during the recruitment process and ensure that reasonable adjustments are in place as required by the Equalities Act 2010. Your application and any associated personal information will be stored and processed in accordance with our Data Policy and destroyed after six months. We will keep your equal opportunities form for a period of up to 6 months, after which point the data will be anonymised and aggregated for monitoring purposes. If you are engaged by us, the information you supply will be kept securely and form part of your record with us.

item.title: Talent and Culture Business Partner
item.description: Salary: £53,500 per annum Contract Type: Permanent Closing date: 30 September 2026 at 12pm Interview date: Week commencing 12 and 19 October 2026 About CARE CARE International is a global humanitarian organisation leading the fight to end poverty in the world’s most challenging situations. Women and girls are at the centre of our work, because we cannot overcome poverty and inequality until all people have equal rights and opportunities. We know that when a crisis erupts, women are often the first to pick up the pieces, so we work alongside women, so they have the power to make change where it’s needed most. Founded in 1945, CARE currently works in over 100 countries and last year alone reached 53.4 million people through nearly 1,500 projects. Why work for CARE International UK? At CARE International UK, we're committed to creating lasting change in the fight against poverty and inequality around the world. Behind that impact is a community of talented, passionate people who bring expertise, collaboration and purpose to everything they do. We're committed to fostering a workplace where colleagues feel valued, supported and empowered to contribute their best. As part of our People & Organisational Development team, you'll have the opportunity to shape how people experience working at CARE, influence organisation-wide initiatives, and help build an environment where individuals and teams can flourish. This is a chance to use your expertise in a role that combines strategic influence with meaningful, people-centred work, all within an organisation driven by a clear social purpose. About the role Working closely with leaders across the organisation, you'll take the lead on talent management and learning and development initiatives that help colleagues build rewarding careers and reach their full potential. From leadership development and succession planning to career pathways and organisational capability, you'll play a pivotal role in ensuring CARE has the talent, skills and leadership needed to achieve its ambitions now and in the future. You'll develop and deliver initiatives that strengthen employee engagement, support professional growth and contribute to a positive organisational culture. By fostering a culture of continuous learning and development, you'll help ensure colleagues have the tools, skills and experiences needed to reach their full potential and make their greatest contribution to CARE's mission. You'll be instrumental in helping the organisation navigate change, strengthen communication and foster a shared sense of direction and purpose. Combining insight, creativity and practical delivery, you'll identify opportunities to improve how we support our people and continuously enhance the experience of our colleagues. This is a varied and influential role for someone who enjoys building relationships, turning ideas into action and making a visible contribution to organisational success. About you You'll be an experienced people professional with a strong track record of delivering talent, learning, engagement and culture initiatives that drive organisational performance and improve employee experience. Combining both a strategic and pragmatic approach, you’ll be able to identify opportunities for improvement and find practical solutions. Alongside your ability to build strong relationships, you’ll be able to influence and challenge constructively while maintaining credibility and trust. Experience within the charity, international development or wider values-led sector would be highly desirable, as would experience managing external consultants. Above all, you are collaborative, curious and solutions-focused, committed to continuous learning and passionate about creating an environment where people can thrive and do their best work. Right to Work in the UK All applicants must have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom at the time of appointment. Proof of right to work will be required as part of the recruitment process. For more information, please visit the UK Government's guidance on right to work. Where you do not have current right to work in the UK, then this will be discussed with you as part of the recruitment process. Please note that not all roles are eligible for sponsorship and further information (should you require sponsorship to work in the UK) on eligibility can be found here. Safeguarding CARE International UK has a zero-tolerance approach to any abuse or sexual harassment or exploitation of people in crisis by any of our staff, representatives or partners. CARE International UK expects all staff to share this commitment through our Safeguarding Policy (link here) and our Code of Conduct (link here). They are responsible for ensuring they understand and work within the remit of these policies throughout their time at CARE International UK. Safeguarding the communities we work with is our top priority in everything we do, including recruitment. All offers of employment at CARE International UK are subject to: · Satisfactory references. CARE International UK participates in theInter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (link here).In line with this Scheme, we willrequest information from successful applicants’ previous employersabout any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment,or incidents under investigationwhen the applicant left employment. · Appropriate criminal record checks (including a Bridger check, link here). By submitting an application, the applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures. Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) We are committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, respectful, and safe work environment where all persons are treated fairly, with dignity and respect. We are a Disability Confident Employer and particularly welcome applications from people with disabilities. We guarantee interviews to applicants with disabilities who meet the essential criteria for the role (see person specification). If you require the candidate brief or need to submit your application in an alternative format, because of a disability, please do get in touch by sending an email to the HR Team. We also encourage people from minoritised communities to apply for roles at CARE International UK. Please note that in compliance with the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006, all job offers at Care International UK are conditional on eligibility to work in the UK. CARE’s EDI Vision Statement We are guided by the communities we serve and grounded by our values which are: women-centred, inclusive, collaborative and quality. We share power responsibly and transparently, we earn trust and are accountable to each other, and we create supportive spaces for collaboration so that everyone is empowered to share ideas. Equity, diversity and inclusion are embedded in all we do - creating ways for everyone to be heard, respected and to thrive.

item.title: Community Insight and Partnerships Officer
item.description: Connecting evidence, community experience and local action to build a shared understanding of East Surrey Be part of establishing a new Community Insight Partnership. Are you a skilled relationship-builder who can bring people together, identify themes across different sources of information and turn community intelligence into clear, useful insight? The Opportunity ESCIP is a one-year proof of concept designed to strengthen how community experience and VCSE intelligence inform local decision-making. It connects voluntary, community and social enterprise organisations with health, local authority and wider partners, creating stronger two-way feedback between communities and decision-makers. This is not primarily an administrative post. You will build trusted relationships, coordinate a new quarterly forum, develop practical ways to gather and synthesise intelligence, and demonstrate how insight has influenced priorities and action. Because the programme is new, you will have genuine scope to shape how it works. What You Will Achieve Over the first 12 months, you will: Establish a quarterly East Surrey VCSE and Community Forum. Build trusted relationships with diverse VCSE organisations, including smaller groups and under-represented communities. Develop and test practical two-way feedback mechanisms between communities, VCSE partners and system leaders. Map intelligence sources and introduce consistent approaches to gathering and synthesising insight. Produce concise briefings highlighting emerging themes and implications for decision-makers. Maintain strategic relationships across health, local government, housing and neighbourhood partners. Support independent evaluation and contribute to the case for Year 2. Main Responsibilities Partnerships and Networks Coordinate day-to-day delivery of ESCIP, maintaining workplans, milestones and actions. Plan and support the quarterly East Surrey VCSE and Community Forum. Develop strong relationships across the VCSE sector and with NHS, local authority, housing, primary care and neighbourhood partners. Maintain wider partner engagement through targeted conversations, briefings and limited observer participation. Represent ESCIP professionally and act as a key point of contact. Engagement and Community Insight Plan and deliver insight activity, including stakeholder conversations, workshops, surveys, desk research and analysis. Enable organisations of different sizes and capacities to contribute, particularly voices less often heard. Map existing intelligence sources, identify gaps and common themes, and distinguish between individual feedback, recurring themes and wider evidence. Communication, Influence and Learning Turn qualitative and quantitative information into accessible summaries, briefings and recommendations. Create visible feedback loops so contributors understand what was heard and what happened next. Prepare stakeholder briefings and contribute to programme and funder reporting. Work with the independent evaluator and contribute learning to the future development of ESCIP. Working Arrangements This is a part-time role based in Oxted with autonomy and variety. Some meetings and community activity will take place across East Surrey, so the postholder must be able to travel within the area. Reasonable travel expenses will be reimbursed. Occasional evening activity may be required by prior agreement, with time off in lieu. The postholder will work closely with colleagues from VASE and CSVA and will have access to office space, HR support and appropriate IT equipment. About You We welcome transferable experience from community development, participation, research, service improvement, public engagement, local government, health or partnership working. Experience, Knowledge and Skills Essential Experience building productive relationships across organisations, sectors or communities. Experience planning and facilitating meetings, workshops or engagement activities. Experience gathering information or feedback and identifying meaningful themes and insights. Ability to translate complex information into clear reports, briefings and recommendations. Ability to organise projects or programmes, manage competing priorities and deliver outcomes with limited supervision. Strong written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills, including confidence engaging senior stakeholders. Commitment to equitable and inclusive engagement, with an understanding of barriers faced by smaller organisations and under-represented communities. Confidence using standard digital tools for collaboration, data analysis, presentations and record-keeping. Desirable Knowledge of the VCSE sector in East Surrey or a comparable area. Understanding of health inequalities, neighbourhood working, integrated care or local government. Experience of monitoring and evaluation, research methods or funder reporting. Please see the Application Pack for full details. How to apply Please submit: • A current CV, including contact details and employment or activity history. • A personal statement answering the three questions below. Please use no more than 350 words for each answer. 1. Building relationships Tell us about a time when you built positive relationships with people from different organisations or backgrounds to achieve a shared goal. What did you do, how did you handle different perspectives, and what was the outcome? We will assess: relationship-building, collaboration, communication and influencing. 2. Turning information into insight Tell us about a time when you gathered information, feedback or community views and used them to improve a service, project or decision. How did you identify the important themes and communicate your findings? We will assess: curiosity, analytical thinking, judgement and clear communication. 3. Organisation and initiative Tell us about a project or piece of work that you coordinated from start to finish. How did you organise the work, manage stakeholders and keep delivery moving when priorities changed? We will assess: planning, initiative, prioritisation and delivery.

item.title: Volunteer Co-ordinator
item.description: Are you passionate about helping others? Do you want to make a difference to the lives of vulnerable families? Have you considered working in the Charity Sector and are you passionate about supporting Volunteers? If so, we want to hear from you! Home-Start Medway is a well-established Charity which has been supporting parents with children aged 0-5 years since 1987. Our ethos is simple and clear, ‘To be there for parents when they need us the most because childhood cannot wait’. It's an exciting time to join our growing team. Having been identified as a leading light amongst Home-Starts and recently received the Kent Charity Award for best use of volunteers and the Queens Award for Voluntary service, we are now looking for a new Volunteer Co-ordinator. The Volunteer Co-ordinator is responsible for the recruitment, training and supervision of Volunteers who provide 1-1 support to parents / carers of children aged 0-5 years, sometimes providing direct support themselves. Job Title: Volunteer Co-ordinator Employer: Home-Start Medway (Charity no: 1108057) Location: Medway Hours of Work: Part time and Full time hours considered Salary: £26,355 – £29,190 per annum dependant on experience Responsible to: CEO Main Responsibilities · Work co-operatively with other team members to recruit and train volunteers and maintain a satisfactory level of available volunteers to meet demand. · Manage a case load of families who are referred to the Scheme, matching them with appropriate volunteers and overseeing this support. · Work with partners to review and design the volunteer training courses so that they include specialist models as identified by client need. · Ensure essential records and checks for volunteers are accurate and up to date. · Match appropriate volunteers with families and introduce them / monitor support. · Provide support and supervision to volunteers that are working with families on your caseload. · Provide regular bulletins / newsletters to volunteers and potential volunteers to retain enthusiasm and motivation. · Develop and facilitate Volunteer social events and support meetings. · Maintain accurate records of the support provided for families on our database system. · Support parent to enrich their living environments by applying for grants for white goods or furniture when needed. · To refer to and / or work in partnership with other agencies and service providers as and when required. · To model age appropriate play activities to parents/carers and offer a range of strategies and activities to manage behaviour and assist child development. · Signpost families to parenting groups that can support them such as the Solihull course or Incredible Years. · Signpost parents / carers to relevant services to ensure they have the necessary provisions to meet their child/ren’s needs. · Maintain and improve competencies through continuous professional development. · To attend regular supervision meetings and annual appraisal. · Work co-operatively with Management to support the preparation of the monthly, quarterly and annual reporting requirements. · To contribute to the effective day to day operation of Home-Start Medway in accordance with governing documents, standards and methods of practice, Home –Start agreement and Quality Assurance standards. · To keep efficient, accurate and confidential records, including statistics collection and collation. This would include the use of evaluation tools to enable us to evidence the impact of our work. · To work within all Home-Start’s policies and procedures including: Confidentiality, Safeguarding Children Policies and Procedures and Health and Safety Policies. · Be flexible and carry our other associated duties as may arise, develop, or be assigned in line with the broad remit of the position. · To work within the ethos of Home-Start and have high standards of practice. The need to respect confidentiality is paramount, as is a mature and flexible approach to the work. This role is a permanent post. You will be based at our office in Strood although will be required to work across the Medway area. As well as joining a friendly, dedicated, and hardworking team you will have access to numerous benefits, including: · 30 days annual leave (including 8 Bank Holidays) · 2 days special leave days per year · Birthday leave day · Free tea and coffee provided in the office · Pension contribution of 3% · Christmas staff appreciation token · Annual pay reviews · Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) via D.A.S · Access to the Charity Worker Discount Scheme Access to a reduced-price local gym membership Home Start Medway is committed to creating a safe and supportive environment for children, families, staff and volunteers. As part of our safer recruitment process, the successful applicant will be asked to complete relevant pre employment checks, including an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check, satisfactory references, right to work checks and verification of qualifications and employment history. All staff are expected to share our commitment to safeguarding and to follow our safeguarding policies and procedures.

item.title: Children & Families Worker
item.description: At Hestia, we are guided by our core values and are dedicated to fostering an equitable, diverse, and inclusive organisation. Our mission is to empower individuals to rebuild their lives and achieve independence. Right now, we are looking for a Children and Families Worker to play a pivotal role in our Domestic Abuse Service in Ealing Sounds great, what will I be doing? The role focuses on building positive and supportive relationships with women and their children, empowering them to work towards their goals through a strengths-based approach. This includes creating, implementing, and reviewing personalised support plans in collaboration with service users and external agencies, while also advocating on their behalf when needed. Key responsibilities involve assisting mothers with parenting skills, signposting them to appropriate services, and offering targeted support to families facing issues such as domestic abuse. Ensuring the safeguarding of children and maintaining confidentiality at all times are central to the role, alongside working within relevant policies and procedures. Additionally, the position emphasises the importance of children's development and wellbeing by providing educational, recreational, and interactive play opportunities both during term time and holidays. Service users and children are encouraged to actively participate in shaping projects through consultations, feedback, and creative engagement. The role also involves promoting community involvement by networking, fundraising, and collaborating with statutory and voluntary organisations. Ultimately, the work contributes towards the five key outcome areas: being healthy, staying safe, enjoying and achieving, making a positive contribution, and achieving economic wellbeing. What do I need to bring with me? You'll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires as well as match our values and mission. You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you're willing to learn. We also value lived experience of the areas we support, so if you feel comfortable, please do mention this on your application. Here's what the team will be looking for This role is restricted to female applicants under Schedule 9 (1a) of the Equality Act 2010 due to the nature of the work. It requires someone who can bring optimism, resilience, and a non-judgemental, anti-discriminatory approach when supporting women and children. A calm manner, empathy, and compassion are essential, particularly when working with service users who have experienced trauma or domestic abuse. The role demands the ability to engage directly with families in a supportive, constructive way, while maintaining professionalism and confidentiality at all times. In addition, the post holder must be skilled in partnership working with statutory, voluntary, and community agencies to achieve the best possible outcomes for families. Strong problem-solving abilities, accuracy in processing and sharing sensitive information, and a clear understanding of safeguarding responsibilities are vital. The role also requires flexibility to travel between service premises and to accompany clients when necessary. Success in this position relies on being able to manage responsibilities effectively within a structured and often pressured environment, while always keeping the wellbeing and empowerment of families at the centre of practice. Interview Steps We keep our interview process simple, so you know exactly what to expect. Shortlisting call: We have a team of dedicated recruitment specialists who will speak to you about your experience, motivations and values. They will also tell you about all the great work we do! Face to face interview: Now you will have face to face interview with the hiring manager. Our interviews are value and competency based. Don't be alarmed if there are other stages in the process, it's all part of the plan for some of our roles. Our commitment to Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion Our services users come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds because it makes us stronger. We are committed to creating and maintaining a diverse and inclusive workforce and value the skills, abilities, talent and experiences, different people and communities bring to our organisation. We are a disability confident employer Hestia is proud to be a disability confident employer, dedicated to the employment and career development of individuals with disabilities. We offer a guaranteed interview scheme for all applicants with disabilities who meet the minimum criteria for the role they have applied for. We also provide reasonable adjustments during the selection and interview process, and throughout your employment with us. Safeguarding Statement Hestia is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of adults, children and young people who are potentially at risk, and we therefore expect all staff and volunteers to do the same. We require all staff to undertake internal and external safeguarding training throughout their employment with Hestia. Important Information for Candidates If your application is successful, please be aware that you will be required to undergo pre-employment checks before a formal offer of employment can be confirmed. We reserve the right to close this job advert early should we receive a high volume of applications or if the position is filled before the closing date. We encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible to ensure their application is considered.
item.dc:creator: Hestia

item.title: Sports Coordinator
item.description: About the role: Sport and physical activity can be a powerful way to improve wellbeing, build confidence and help people feel more connected to themselves and their communities. As a Sports Coordinator, you’ll play a key role in making those opportunities happen for people experiencing homelessness and multiple disadvantage across Single Homeless Project (SHP). This is a hands on and outward facing role where you’ll bring energy, creativity and momentum to our sports programme. You’ll deliver engaging sport and exercise sessions, help expand activity across our services and work with the Sport Lead to coordinate freelancers, volunteers and peers who bring additional skills and opportunities into the programme. You’ll build strong relationships with clients and teams, spot where new activities could make a difference and help turn ideas into opportunities people genuinely want to take part in. You’ll also help take the programme beyond SHP, building relationships with sports providers, community organisations and charities across London to open up new opportunities for clients. You’ll champion the role physical activity can play within homelessness services, encourage more people to get involved and help services build the confidence, networks and resources to make sport and exercise a lasting part of the support they offer. At SHP, you’ll be supported to keep developing too. You’ll have access to learning and development opportunities, the chance to strengthen your skills across programme development, partnership working and inclusive practice, and opportunities to build experience that can support your longer-term career progression across SHP and the wider homelessness and support sector. About you: You have experience delivering engaging sport, exercise or physical activity sessions, alongside relevant sports or coaching qualifications. You know how to motivate and encourage people who may face barriers to taking part in physical activity, creating sessions that feel inclusive, positive and achievable. You’re confident building relationships and can bring clients, colleagues, volunteers, freelancers and external partners with you. You’re proactive and resourceful, with the confidence to spot new opportunities, build partnerships and help grow the reach and impact of a sports programme. You’re organised, adaptable and passionate about using sport and physical activity as a tool to improve health, wellbeing and connection. About us: We’re London’s leading homelessness charity – and we get things done. In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we’re not shying away. We’re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up. We’re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own. Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that’s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You’ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that’s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable. We’re not perfect, but we’re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn’t just a job. It’s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind. Important info: Closing Date: Monday 14th September at midnight Interview Date: Wednesday 23rd September at SHP Head Office in Kings Cross This post will require an Enhanced DBS check to be processed (by SHP) for the successful applicant. Please note applications are reviewed for AI use in application questions. Applications with insufficient/without current right to work or requiring sponsorship will not be accepted for this role.
item.dc:creator: Single Homeless Project

item.title: Website and Analytics Manager
item.description: Why join us? We’re a values-driven charity committed to saving lives by funding world-leading research, treatment, and care at The Royal Marsden. You’ll be part of a collaborative, ambitious and kind team, with plenty of opportunities for learning and development. About the Web and Analytics Manager We are looking for a Website and Analytics Manager to join our digital team. This role will suit a digital and analytics expert. A proactive, supportive and solution focused digital professional who is keen to hit the ground running, enjoys collaborating with colleagues across the team and wider organisation, and is passionate about adding value. The Website and Analytics Manager is responsible for the day-to-day management and improvement of our digital platforms, website and their connected tools. As well as analysis and reporting of results, content creation and more. This person is a technical expert and will play a crucial role in how we develop our digital channels. Relationship management across the Charity and with third party suppliers is also a key part of the role. What you’ll be doing Day to day ownership of the web ecosystem including royalmarsden org, subdomains, microsites and donation platforms including managing relationships with third party agencies and suppliers to maintain and improve these platforms. Work with the Senior Digital Manager to set the strategic direction for our websites and associated digital experiences, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities, supporter needs and fundraising objectives Manage website improvements and Manage website improvements and performance optimisation work, including CRO, SEO and core web vitals, driving continuous improvement of our supporter journeys and embedding a data led approach. Lead the web team, line managing the Digital Officer and Senior Digital Officer, supporting the effective allocation of resources across the team, coaching direct reports and fostering a high performing team culture. Manage the Digital Officer and Senior Digital Officer to deliver relevant, engaging, optimised and audience centred content, landing pages and digital journeys across various digital channels, and overseeing the website content calendar and campaign content deploys. Work alongside Marketing and Digital colleagues to ensure our project planners are up to date and website content is in line with our wider audience journeys and content needs. Partner with teams across the charity to understand user and organisational needs, to deliver a range of projects and campaigns, including fundraising campaigns. Analyse and interpret website analytics data, communicate results to the wider team and use insights gained to inform and direct positive change. The Website and Analytics Manager also owns the relationship with a third-party agency to deliver improvements to our tracking set up, and ensures compliant, accurate and reliable data collection. Ensure the website platforms are secure, accessible, scalable and complaint with all relevant regulation and legislation. Work with the Senior Digital Manager and Head of Digital Content and Engagement to develop and manage the website budget, contributing to business planning, forecasting, and monitoring spend. Work to improve digital literacy across the charity alongside Marketing and Digital colleagues, training colleagues in how to use our CMS and other key digital skills such as data and insights. Occasional out of hours support where required for critical website/campaign related activity. Keep up to date with digital technology and share this knowledge with colleagues both within the digital team and across the wider Charity team. About you - The successful candidate will need: Experience of working on CMS systems, knowledge of headless CMS systems would be an advantage. Experience managing digital agencies, developers and third party suppliers. Knowledge of UX and digital user journeys. Understanding of PPC advertising. Experience of line management and developing junior digital staff, including coaching, performance management and workload prioritisation. Experience of creating content for websites, including a strong understanding of SEO and CRO principles. Understanding and experience using website reporting systems e.g Google Analytics , Hotjar, Google search console. Interest in digital technologies, fundraising/donation platforms and innovation within the charity sector. Excellent communications skills, particularly within stakeholder management. A proactive, solution focused approach to prioritisation and workflow management. The following are beneficial but not essential: Experience owning and developing digital products, platforms or websites, including roadmap planning and prioritisation. Experience managing budgets, forecasting expenditure and monitoring performance against management accounts. Project management, digital publishing and any related software technology training. Experience of working within a fundraising organisation. Analytics training. Paid advertising training/skills. Strong team ethos with a track record of collaborative and supportive working. Experience managing Google Ad Grants and/or Google Ads accounts, including campaign optimisation, reporting and compliance with programme requirements. Experience managing budgets, forecasting expenditure and monitoring performance against management accounts. If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you! What we offer Hybrid working between home and Chelsea with travel to Sutton once a month. Flexible working around our core hours of 10am to 4pm. 27 days annual leave rising with length of service. Up to 6% employer contributions subject to matched contribution from you (increasing with length of service). Training, support and development opportunities. Access to the blue light discount scheme and other discounts opportunities. Access to subsidised staff restaurants, on-site yoga and wellbeing classes, staff choir and much more. Range of wellbeing initiatives including access to an employee assistance programme designed to save money and improve your physical, financial and mental health and wellbeing, access to free online GP appointments and free eye tests and contribution towards any glasses required for work purposes. Inclusion matters We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the communities we serve. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and walks of life.
